properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify the stored-key set equals exactly the nonzero-valued keys: after each SSTORE/set_storage/trie_set, a key is enumerated iff it is a written key AND its value is nonzero; flag any retained zero-valued key or dropped nonzero-valued key.
properties.assertion: forall k: k in stored_keys(state) <=> (k in written_keys(state) and get_storage(k) != 0)

audit_packet.guarantee: For every storage key k, membership of k in the materialized/enumerated stored-key set of an account's storage is logically equivalent to (k belongs to the written-key domain) AND (its value is nonzero). Equivalently: the stored-key set is exactly the support of the key->value map — no zero-valued key is ever retained, and no nonzero-valued key is ever dropped.
preconditions: The root theorem declares no must-establish obligation; the biconditional holds unconditionally for any value function f and any key list l, so no guard may be added that narrows it.
Directional guard for the forward facts (L002, L003): the key k is present in the stored-key set (k in supportOf f l).

Directional guard for the reverse fact (L004): the key k is in the written-key domain (k in l) AND its value is nonzero (f k != 0). Both conjuncts are required together; neither alone licenses membership.
The value function f is total over the key domain (every key in l has a defined Nat/uint256 value), matching the Lean typing f : A -> Nat.

supporting_facts.claim: Exactness (biconditional, both directions): k is in the stored-key set IFF (k is in the written-key domain AND value(k) != 0). This is an equivalence, not a one-way implication, and must not be weakened to a mere 'nonzero keys are stored' check.
supporting_facts.check: For a representative account, enumerate the actual stored-key set produced by the state/trie layer (post-SSTORE / set_storage / trie_set) and independently compute the set of written keys whose current value is nonzero. Compare the two sets for exact equality, in both directions, over a matrix that includes: nonzero-write, zero-write, nonzero-then-zero, zero-then-nonzero, and repeated writes of the same key.
supporting_facts.expected: Set equality holds exactly: stored_keys == { k in written_keys : value(k) != 0 }. Symmetric difference is empty in both directions.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sets differ in either direction, or the implementation only enforces one direction (e.g. inserts nonzero keys but never removes keys whose value became zero), or the equivalence is tested only for the nonzero case.

supporting_facts.claim: Soundness of domain (no phantom keys): if k is in the stored-key set, then k is in the written-key domain. Storage enumeration can never surface a key that was never written through SSTORE/set_storage/trie_set.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate the stored-key set after an arbitrary sequence of writes and assert every enumerated key traces to a key that appears in the write domain for that account. Include cases where keys share prefixes/nibble paths and where an unrelated account is written, to catch key derivation or path-collision defects that fabricate entries.
supporting_facts.expected: Every enumerated stored key is a member of the written-key domain; no key of unknown provenance appears.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Enumeration yields a key that was never written for that account (fabricated, cross-account leaked, or path-collision-derived), or the key set is derived from a source other than the actual write domain.

supporting_facts.claim: No zero retention (exact value predicate): if k is in the stored-key set, then value(k) != 0. Zero is the exact excluded value — the predicate is inequality to 0, not 'small', 'default-ish', or 'unset flag'.
supporting_facts.check: Write a nonzero value to k, then write exactly 0 to k. Enumerate the stored-key set and read back via SLOAD / get_storage. Repeat where the zero write is the first write to k, and where many sibling keys under the same trie path remain nonzero.
supporting_facts.expected: k is absent from the stored-key set after the zero write, and SLOAD/get_storage(k) returns 0. Sibling nonzero keys remain present and unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: k remains enumerated after being set to 0 (zero-valued entry retained as a live key), or a separate 'deleted/tombstone' marker is enumerated as a stored key, or the zero test is implemented as a boolean/truthiness or bounded test rather than exact equality to 0.

supporting_facts.claim: Completeness (no silent drops): if k is in the written-key domain AND value(k) != 0, then k IS in the stored-key set. Both hypotheses jointly suffice — a nonzero written key may never be omitted.
supporting_facts.check: Write nonzero values to a set of keys, including keys whose values are minimal (1), maximal (2^256-1), and keys that were previously zero/absent. Enumerate the stored-key set and read each back via SLOAD / get_storage.
supporting_facts.expected: Every written key with a nonzero value is present in the enumerated stored-key set, and reads return the exact written value.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A nonzero-valued written key is missing from enumeration, or a write is skipped/short-circuited (e.g. treated as a no-op because the prior value was zero, or because the new value looked 'empty'), or a nonzero write is dropped when it collides on a trie path with an existing entry.

derived_obligations.check: Round-trip the equivalence through the trie root: apply the same write multiset in two different orders and via two different paths (direct set_storage vs. SSTORE), then compare the resulting stored-key sets and state roots.
derived_obligations.expected: Both produce the identical stored-key set and identical root, because the set is determined solely by the support predicate (in-domain AND nonzero), not by write order or entry path.
derived_obligations.flag_if: State roots or enumerated key sets diverge between orderings or entry paths — a remotely reachable consensus divergence, since two nodes processing the same transaction would commit different roots.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the delete-on-zero path in set_storage/trie_set removes the key from the trie structure itself (node removal / branch collapse), not merely from an in-memory overlay used for reads.
derived_obligations.expected: After a zero write, the key is absent from both the read path and the committed trie structure, and the committed root matches a trie built from scratch containing only the nonzero-valued keys.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Reads report 0 but the committed trie still contains the key (root mismatch versus a from-scratch build), which breaks FACT-3 at the consensus-visible layer even though local reads look correct.

derived_obligations.check: Exercise the boundary between 'absent' and 'present with value 0' on the read path: SLOAD / get_storage for a never-written key, for a key written to 0, and for a key written nonzero then zeroed.
derived_obligations.expected: All three return 0 and all three are absent from the stored-key set — absence and zero-value are the same observable state, exactly as the biconditional requires.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The implementation distinguishes 'absent' from 'zero' in any consensus-visible way (different return, different gas/refund classification derived from key presence rather than value, or different root), letting an attacker craft a transaction that makes nodes disagree.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is a biconditional characterizing membership in supportOf f l as exactly (membership in l) AND (f a != 0). L001 restates that equivalence and decomposes into three independent lemmas: L002 and L003 are the two forward projections (support membership implies domain membership, and implies nonzero value), each guarded by the hypothesis 'a in supportOf f l'; L004 is the reverse direction, guarded by BOTH hypotheses 'a in l' and 'f a != 0'. FACT-2, FACT-3, and FACT-4 preserve those three facts at full strength rather than collapsing them into the weaker consequence 'stored keys are nonzero'; FACT-1 preserves the equivalence itself so that neither direction can be satisfied vacuously. Read onto the state-trie surface, l is the written-key domain reached through SSTORE / set_storage / trie_set, f is the key-to-value map read back through SLOAD / get_storage, and supportOf f l is the enumerated/committed stored-key set. The improper_state_update class is the teaching context: a violation in either direction (retaining a zeroed key, or dropping a nonzero key) changes the committed state root, so a single crafted transaction makes nodes that share the defect and nodes that do not commit different roots — a chain split, matching the High severity band. The derived obligations push the equivalence to the consensus-visible layer (root equality, structural removal, absent-vs-zero indistinguishability) because the theorem constrains the set itself, not just the read path. No obligation was invented for the root: the evidence states it has none, so the preconditions record only the lemma-level directional guards.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) (l : List A) (a : A),
  Iff (List.instMembership.mem (EthTotal.supportOf f l) a) (And (List.instMembership.mem l a) (Ne (f a) 0))
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Iff (List.instMembership.mem (EthTotal.supportOf f l) a) (And (List.instMembership.mem l a) (Ne (f a) 0))

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) {a : A} (l : List A),
  List.instMembership.mem (EthTotal.supportOf f l) a → List.instMembership.mem l a
∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) {a : A} (l : List A), List.instMembership.mem (EthTotal.supportOf f l) a → Ne (f a) 0

∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) {a : A} (l : List A),
  List.instMembership.mem l a → Ne (f a) 0 → List.instMembership.mem (EthTotal.supportOf f l) a

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify that a saturating balance debit conserves ether exactly: the post-debit balance plus the amount actually moved must equal the pre-balance, with the move capped at min(debit, balance) and never wrapping.
properties.assertion: balance_after + moved == balance_before && moved == min(d, balance_before) && balance_after == sat_sub(balance_before, d) >= 0

audit_packet.guarantee: For every balance b and requested debit d, a saturating debit preserves total value exactly: the remaining balance (b - d, saturating at 0) plus the amount actually debitable min(d, b) equals b. Neither the full-debit path (d <= b) nor the saturated path (b <= d) may create or destroy ether, and the subtraction must never wrap around.
preconditions: Root theorem EthTotal.a_saturating_debit_keeps_the_shortfall carries no must-establish obligation; the equality holds for ALL b, d : Nat with no guard, so the implementation must not gate this conservation behind any additional condition.

Balances and debit amounts are non-negative integers (Nat): the subtraction operator used by the balance check / saturating subtraction path must be the truncating one that yields 0 when d > b, not a wrapping or signed one.

Lemma-level guards are case guards internal to the proof, not caller obligations: d <= b selects the exact-debit case [L002,L003] and b <= d selects the saturated case [L004,L005]; the two cases must be exhaustive in the implementation.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact conservation identity: (b - d) + min(d, b) = b for all b, d. The post-debit balance and the amount actually moved sum back to the pre-debit balance with no loss and no gain.
supporting_facts.check: Across the balance-check / saturating-subtraction / state.move_ether surface, sum the resulting debited balance and the value actually transferred (or recorded) and compare against the pre-debit balance, including the case where the requested debit exceeds the balance.
supporting_facts.expected: balance_after + moved == balance_before holds as an exact equality for every (balance_before, requested_debit) pair, including requested_debit > balance_before.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any path where balance_after + moved != balance_before — e.g. the balance is saturated to 0 while the full requested d is credited elsewhere or written into a receipt (value creation), or the balance is reduced by d while only min(d,b) is credited (value destruction).

supporting_facts.claim: The conservation identity is order-independent: min(d, b) + (b - d) = b is the same exact equality with the operands commuted, so the guarantee does not depend on whether the credit or the debit is applied first.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the conserved total is invariant under the order in which the saturating debit and the corresponding credit are applied within state.move_ether, and that no intermediate rounding, clamping, or re-read of the balance sits between them.
supporting_facts.expected: Both orderings yield the same final total; the identity is preserved as an equality, not merely as an inequality or a 'balance did not go negative' boolean.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The conserved sum depends on application order, or an intermediate step re-reads/clamps the balance so that the sum equals b only for one ordering.

supporting_facts.claim: Sufficient-balance case, exact: when d <= b, min(d, b) = d exactly [L002], and d + (b - d) = b exactly [L003]. The full requested amount is moved and the remainder is exactly b - d.
supporting_facts.check: For requested debits within the available balance, verify the moved amount equals the full requested d (not a clamped, rounded, or capped variant) and the resulting balance equals exactly b - d.
supporting_facts.expected: moved == d and balance_after == b - d, as exact equalities.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A sufficient balance still yields a partial move (moved < d), or balance_after != b - d, or the code takes the saturated branch when d <= b (off-by-one at d == b is in scope).

supporting_facts.claim: Insufficient-balance case, exact: when b <= d, min(d, b) = b exactly [L004] and the truncating subtraction b - d = 0 exactly [L005]. The moved amount is exactly the whole remaining balance and the account is left at exactly zero — the shortfall (d - b) is never silently materialized.
supporting_facts.check: For requested debits exceeding the available balance, verify the moved amount equals exactly the pre-debit balance b, the resulting balance is exactly 0, and any receipt or downstream credit records min(d, b) = b rather than the requested d.
supporting_facts.expected: moved == b (the full remaining balance, not 0 and not d) and balance_after == 0, as exact equalities.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An over-debit produces a wrapped/huge balance instead of 0, produces a negative or error-swallowed value, moves 0 instead of the available b, or records the requested d in a receipt or credit while only b was debited — the remotely reachable value-creation path.

derived_obligations.check: Exercise the saturating-subtraction primitive itself with d > b at boundary values (b = 0, d = 1; b = 0, d = max; d = b; d = b + 1) and inspect the raw result before any downstream use.
derived_obligations.expected: The subtraction truncates at 0 with no wraparound, no exception-swallowed default, and no signed reinterpretation.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The primitive wraps to a large positive value, throws where the caller ignores it, or is implemented with an unchecked native subtraction on an unsigned type.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the value recorded in receipts / emitted as the transfer amount against the value actually removed from the source balance on the saturated path.
derived_obligations.expected: Both equal min(d, b); the recorded and applied amounts are identical.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The receipt or emitted amount is the requested d while only min(d, b) left the source balance — a divergence that different clients could resolve differently, producing a consensus split.

derived_obligations.check: Treat the debit and its counterpart credit as one atomic state update over the state trie and re-sum the two affected balances before and after.
derived_obligations.expected: The two-account total is unchanged: the credited amount is exactly the debited min(d, b), so aggregate supply is conserved by the same equality.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The credit side uses the requested d while the debit side saturates, or a failure partway leaves the debit applied without the matching credit (or vice versa), breaking the equality at the state-trie level.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the two cases d <= b and b <= d are exhaustive and consistent at the overlap d == b, where both lemma branches apply.
derived_obligations.expected: At d == b both branches agree: moved == d == b and balance_after == 0, satisfying the same conservation equality.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The branch condition uses a strict/non-strict comparator mismatch so that d == b falls through to an unhandled path, or the two branches disagree at the boundary.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem [ROOT] states (b - d) + min(d, b) = b. Its proof commutes the sum and applies min_add_sub [L001], which is the same exact equality in the form min(d, b) + (b - d) = b — hence FACT-1 and FACT-2 are the identical conservation guarantee under either operand order. L001 in turn splits on the total order of Nat: in the branch d <= b it uses min_eq_left [L002] to get min(d, b) = d and add_sub_cancel_of_le [L003] to get d + (b - d) = b, giving the exact full-debit case FACT-3; in the branch b <= d it uses min_eq_right [L004] to get min(d, b) = b and sub_eq_zero_of_le [L005] to get b - d = 0, giving the exact saturated case FACT-4 where the moved amount is precisely the whole remaining balance and the residue is precisely zero. The audit therefore preserves the equalities themselves (moved == d, moved == b, balance_after == b - d, balance_after == 0) rather than weakening them to a 'balance did not underflow' boolean. The derived obligations bind these arithmetic equalities to the named code surface — the saturating subtraction primitive (OBS-1), the receipt/emitted amount (OBS-2), the paired state.move_ether credit over the state trie (OBS-3), and the branch boundary (OBS-4) — which is where an improper_state_update defect would remotely mint or burn ether on a single message and split the chain.

properties.label: opcodes
properties.text: Verify SELFDESTRUCT/state.destroy_account on a live account lowers total supply by exactly the pre-op balance, that a self-directed destruct (beneficiary == self) is supply-neutral, and that no debit path lets v > balance mint (v - balance) of supply.
properties.assertion: s∈live ∧ distinct(live) ⇒ supply(setBal(s,0))+bal(s)==supply ∧ supply(selfXfer(s))==supply ∧ Δsupply(xfer v)==v-min(v,bal s)==0

audit_packet.guarantee: For a live account s, destroying/zeroing s conserves total accounted value exactly: the post-state supply plus the pre-state balance of s equals the pre-state supply, and a self-directed transfer (source == destination == s) leaves supply bit-for-bit unchanged. Every debit/credit pair on the ledger must move value, never create or silently destroy it; any deviation is a state-root divergence between clients.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hs: the destroyed account s is a member of L.live — i.e. s is present in the tracked account set at the moment of the operation. The guarantee is only claimed for accounts already in state; the check must establish membership (or its implementation equivalent) before applying the burn.

Ledger.live_distinct (Distinct L.live): the tracked account list contains no duplicate entry for s. Supply is a sum over this list, so a duplicated account would be counted twice and the conservation equality would not hold.
Ledger.bal_live: any account with a nonzero balance is in L.live, so no value exists outside the summed set.
Ledger.supply is defined as sumOver bal live — 'total supply' in every check below means the sum of balances over exactly the tracked account list, not a separately maintained counter.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact-burn conservation (equality, not merely 'supply decreases'): (L.setBal s 0 hs).supply + L.bal s = L.supply. Zeroing a live account's balance removes exactly bal s from the total and nothing else.
supporting_facts.check: For a live account s with an arbitrary pre-state balance b (including b = 0 and b = max representable), apply the destruct/zeroing path, then recompute total supply as the sum of balances over the tracked account set. Compare post_supply + b against pre_supply.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply + b == pre_supply exactly, for every b, with no rounding, saturation, or truncation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: post_supply + b != pre_supply; the code asserts only post_supply <= pre_supply or 'supply changed'; the delta is derived from a cached/duplicated supply counter rather than the actual tracked balances; or the account's balance is zeroed in one structure but still counted in the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Self-directed transfer is supply-neutral: debiting s by bal s and then crediting the same account s by bal s returns supply to exactly L.supply. The degenerate source == destination case must not double-count the credit or drop the debit.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise the destruct/transfer path with beneficiary == the account being destroyed, and with a transfer amount v equal to the full balance. Recompute supply over the tracked set and compare to pre_supply.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply == pre_supply exactly; the account's own balance is unchanged in the self-directed case.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The credit is applied to a stale snapshot of the source account so the debit is lost (supply decreases), or the debit is applied to a stale snapshot so the credit is duplicated (supply increases); the source==destination case is special-cased in a way that produces a different supply than the general path.

supporting_facts.claim: Credit is exact and unsaturating: (L.setBal d (L.bal d + v) hd).supply = L.supply + v, and more generally (L.setBal a v ha).supply + L.bal a = L.supply + v. Crediting an account by v raises total supply by exactly v — no more.
supporting_facts.check: Credit a live account by v and recompute supply over the tracked set; vary v across zero, small, and near-maximum values and vary the recipient's existing balance.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply == pre_supply + v exactly for every v and every pre-existing recipient balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: post_supply exceeds pre_supply + v (value minted), or the credit silently wraps/saturates so post_supply < pre_supply + v (value destroyed without a corresponding burn).

supporting_facts.claim: Debit is exact but SATURATING: (L.setBal s (L.bal s - v) hs).supply + min(v, L.bal s) = L.supply. The supply actually removed by a debit of v is min(v, bal s), not v. This is the strong form and must not be weakened to 'supply decreases by v'.
supporting_facts.check: Debit a live account by v for v < bal s, v == bal s, and v > bal s, and recompute supply.
supporting_facts.expected: pre_supply - post_supply == min(v, bal s) in all three cases; for v > bal s the balance floors at zero and only bal s leaves the supply.
supporting_facts.flag_if: For v > bal s the code removes v from a supply accumulator while only bal s left the account (supply understated), or the balance underflows/wraps to a huge value instead of flooring at zero.

supporting_facts.claim: UNGUARDED OVER-DEBIT MINTS VALUE: with no v <= bal s precondition, the debit-then-credit pair yields supply + (v - bal s); equivalently supply + min(v, bal s) = supply + v. Transferring more than the source holds inflates total supply by exactly the shortfall v - bal s.
supporting_facts.check: Attempt the destruct/transfer path with a transfer amount v strictly greater than the source account's balance (including the case where the balance was already reduced earlier in the same operation, e.g. by a fee burn). Recompute supply over the tracked set.
supporting_facts.expected: Either the operation is rejected before any state change, or post_supply == pre_supply — never post_supply == pre_supply + (v - bal s).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any reachable path applies the credit of v while the debit only removed bal s, producing a net supply increase; or the sufficiency guard (v <= bal s) is checked against a balance read before an intervening deduction rather than the balance at debit time.

supporting_facts.claim: Conservation depends on the tracked account list being duplicate-free and on the updated account being a member of it: sumOver (update a v f) l + f a = sumOver f l + v holds only under Distinct l and a ∈ l.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the account set summed to produce total supply cannot contain the same account twice, and that the destruct target is looked up in that same set that the supply sum ranges over.
supporting_facts.expected: The account collection is duplicate-free by construction, and the destruct target is a member of exactly the collection the supply is summed over.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The same account can appear twice (e.g. added again on touch/creation without a membership test), or the balance write targets a different collection/overlay than the one the supply accounting reads — either makes the burn delta differ across clients.

supporting_facts.claim: Updating the balance of an account NOT in the tracked list leaves the sum entirely unchanged: sumOver (update a v f) l = sumOver f l when a ∉ l. Value written to an untracked account is invisible to supply accounting.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the destruct target's membership is established before the burn (the ROOT precondition hs), and that a credited beneficiary is likewise in the tracked set before the credit is counted.
supporting_facts.expected: No balance-affecting write occurs against an account outside the tracked set; a beneficiary not yet tracked is added to the set before its credit is counted toward supply.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A burn or credit is applied to an account outside the summed set, so the operation appears supply-neutral to one client's accounting and supply-changing to another's — the classic consensus-divergence shape for this invariant.

supporting_facts.claim: Balance arithmetic is truncated (Nat) subtraction: x - y = 0 whenever x <= y. In particular bal s - bal s = 0 exactly, which is what makes the self-destruct debit land on zero rather than wrapping.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the balance type/arithmetic used in the destruct path floors at zero on subtraction and cannot produce a negative-then-reinterpreted value.
supporting_facts.expected: Subtracting an amount >= the balance yields exactly 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Balance subtraction wraps modulo the word size, producing a near-maximum balance and a catastrophic supply inflation from a single transaction.

derived_obligations.check: Establish the ROOT obligation explicitly: the destruct path must confirm the target account is present in the tracked account set BEFORE zeroing its balance, and the balance used in the conservation equation must be the value read at that same point.
derived_obligations.expected: Membership is established first; the burned amount equals the balance read at burn time.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The burn amount is read at one point and the zeroing happens at another, so an intervening balance change (e.g. a fee burn debiting the same account) makes the recorded burn differ from the actual supply delta.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce the sufficiency guard that L003 requires (hv: v <= bal s) on every debit-then-credit path reachable from the destruct operation, evaluated against the live balance at debit time.
derived_obligations.expected: No reachable path performs a credit of v without having actually removed v from the source.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The guard is absent, is evaluated against a stale balance, or is bypassed on any branch — L005 shows the exact inflation (v - bal s) that follows.

derived_obligations.check: Sequence-compose the destruct burn with the fee burn on the same account: apply both in the order the implementation uses and recompute total supply over the tracked set.
derived_obligations.expected: The total supply delta equals the sum of the individually accounted deltas, each computed against the balance at the time of its own application; both orderings that the implementation could take must yield the same final supply.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The two burns are each computed from the same pre-operation balance snapshot, so combined they remove more (or less) than the account ever held — the second burn saturates per FACT-4 while the accounting still charges the full amount.

derived_obligations.check: Cross-check the value reported in receipts for the operation against the recomputed supply delta over the tracked account set.
derived_obligations.expected: The reported/receipted amount equals the actual supply delta (bal s for a full burn, 0 for a self-directed destruct).
derived_obligations.flag_if: Receipts report a nominal requested amount rather than the saturated actual amount min(v, bal s), letting a receipt-derived and a state-derived supply figure disagree.

derived_obligations.check: Determinism sweep across the degenerate cases the proof covers: bal s == 0, beneficiary == self, target absent from the tracked set, and target present twice.
derived_obligations.expected: Every case is either rejected deterministically or produces the exact supply of FACT-1/FACT-2; behaviour does not depend on iteration order, map ordering, or overlay layering.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any degenerate case produces an implementation-defined or ordering-dependent supply — this is precisely a remotely triggerable state-root split from a single transaction.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is a conjunction of two independent conservation statements about a live account s (its only obligation being hs : s ∈ L.live). The first conjunct (L001, via the general transfer lemma L003) says a self-directed move of bal s leaves supply exactly equal to L.supply. The second (L002, via L004) says zeroing s reduces supply by exactly bal s: post_supply + bal s = pre_supply. Both reduce to the update lemma for sums over the tracked list (L007/L012), which holds only when that list is duplicate-free and contains the updated account — hence the preconditions and FACT-6/FACT-7. The strong quantitative content lives one layer down and must not be collapsed into 'supply decreases': L014 gives exactness on the credit side (+v exactly), L015 gives SATURATION on the debit side (-min(v, bal s), not -v), and L005/L009 spell out what happens when the v <= bal s guard of L003 is dropped — supply grows by exactly v - bal s, i.e. value is minted from nothing. That is the remotely-reachable, single-transaction failure this packet is aimed at: a client that credits a beneficiary the nominal amount while the source only saturated to zero produces a different total supply and a different state root than its peers, splitting the chain. L006 supplies the underlying truncated-subtraction fact that makes bal s - bal s = 0 rather than a wraparound.

omitted_facts.reason: Pure arithmetic (right-cancellation of addition on Nat); proof plumbing with no implementation-observable content.
Pure arithmetic (left-cancellation of addition on Nat); proof plumbing only.
Commutativity of min on Nat — a mathematical identity with no distinct implementation obligation beyond the saturation behaviour already captured in FACT-4.
Folded into FACT-4 rather than listed separately: min v b + (b - v) = b is exactly the algebraic identity that makes the debit's saturating delta min(v, bal s), which FACT-4 checks directly.
Lattice property of min (c <= min a b from c <= a and c <= b); arithmetic support for L010 with no separate implementation check.
min a b <= b; arithmetic support with no separate implementation check beyond FACT-4.
min a b <= a; arithmetic support with no separate implementation check beyond FACT-4.
min a b = a when a <= b; case-split arithmetic used to derive L011, already covered by FACT-4.
x + (y - x) = y when x <= y; truncated-subtraction arithmetic, the general form of the saturation already covered by FACT-8 and FACT-4.
min a b = b when b <= a; the mirror case of L019, already covered by FACT-4.
Nothing is a member of the empty list — base case of the list recursion behind L012; no implementation-observable obligation.
Membership elimination on a cons cell — list-recursion plumbing for L012; the security-relevant consequences (distinctness and membership) are captured in FACT-6 and FACT-7.

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify that a zero-valued storage write to key k leaves the storage support exactly equal to the pre-write support — not merely non-growing — while k stays in the enumerated key domain, so no client retains a zero-valued slot in the trie.
properties.assertion: f(k)=0 => supportOf(f, k::l) == supportOf(f, l) (exact list equality) AND k in (k::l)

audit_packet.guarantee: When the value written at key k is zero, the storage support after the write is exactly the support of the pre-existing key list l (identical contents, no added entry for k), and k is still a member of the enumerated key sequence k :: l.
preconditions: Root obligation hz: the value at the written key is zero — f k = 0 under the post-write valuation.
The post-write key sequence is k :: l, where k is the key just written and l is the pre-existing key list.
supportOf is the evidence's support extractor: it retains exactly those keys of the list whose valuation is nonzero.

supporting_facts.claim: Under f k = 0, supportOf f (k :: l) = supportOf f l — an exact equality of the support, not a subset or a size bound: the zero write adds no entry for k and perturbs no other entry.
supporting_facts.check: After a zero write via SSTORE / state.set_storage on key k, compute the storage support over the resulting key sequence k :: l and compare it element-by-element against the support computed over l alone.
supporting_facts.expected: The two supports are identical: same elements, same multiplicity, same order; k does not appear in either.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The post-write support contains k, or differs from supportOf f l in length, ordering, or any element — including implementations that only assert |support| does not grow, or that assert a subset relation, while permitting the contents to change.

supporting_facts.claim: k ∈ (k :: l): the written key remains a member of the enumerated key sequence even though it is absent from the support. Key-domain membership and support membership are distinct.
supporting_facts.check: After the zero write, enumerate the key sequence and the support separately; confirm k is a member of the key sequence and simultaneously absent from the support.
supporting_facts.expected: k is present in the key sequence k :: l and absent from supportOf f (k :: l).
supporting_facts.flag_if: The implementation conflates the two — treating presence of k in the key domain as evidence of a support entry (retaining a zero-valued leaf under trie_set), or deriving support membership from key enumeration rather than from a nonzero valuation.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the equality path is gated on the obligation hz itself: the no-add / removal behaviour must be selected by the written value being zero, and a nonzero write must not be routed through it.
derived_obligations.expected: Support equality with l holds exactly when the written value is zero; a nonzero write is handled by a different path and is outside this guarantee.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The zero-write path is selected by anything other than the written value being zero (e.g. by key shape, by prior presence of k, or by a stale reading of the value), so that a nonzero write can silently take the support-preserving path.

derived_obligations.check: Apply the zero write when k already occurs in l, and again repeatedly on the same key.
derived_obligations.expected: supportOf f (k :: l) = supportOf f l holds in every case; repeated zero writes are idempotent on the support.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A repeated or duplicate-key zero write changes the support — e.g. removes a distinct entry, double-removes, or appends a residual entry for k.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the state-trie image produced by trie_set for the key sequence k :: l after a zero write against the image produced for l alone, across every execution path that can be reached remotely by a single transaction performing SSTORE with a zero value.
derived_obligations.expected: The two trie images agree, since the supports they encode are equal by FACT-1; no zero-valued leaf survives for k.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any reachable path leaves a zero-valued leaf for k, or otherwise produces a trie image differing from the one built from l — this is the improper_state_update failure that makes clients disagree on state after an ordinary transaction, i.e. a remotely triggerable consensus divergence.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes the single obligation hz : f k = 0 and yields a conjunction. Its right component is exactly L001 (EthTotal.supportOf_cons_zero) instantiated at x := k, giving the exact equality supportOf f (k :: l) = supportOf f l — preserved here as FACT-1 without weakening to a subset or cardinality claim. Its left component is the membership k ∈ (k :: l), preserved as FACT-2, which separates the enumerated key domain from the support. FACT-1 and FACT-2 together are the full root conclusion; OBS-1 pins the guarantee to the root obligation, OBS-2 exercises the equality under duplicate and repeated writes, and OBS-3 carries the equality to the trie image reachable by a single transaction.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) {x : A},
  Eq (f x) 0 → ∀ (l : List A), Eq (EthTotal.supportOf f (List.cons x l)) (EthTotal.supportOf f l)
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq (EthTotal.supportOf f (List.cons x l)) (EthTotal.supportOf f l)

properties.label: gas
properties.text: Verify the sender-funding guard: reject unless intrinsic cost P ≤ balance BEFORE subtracting, then value ≤ balance−P, with no wraparound in P+value; and confirm prepay debits sender exactly P, credits escrow exactly P, escrow≠sender, both accounts live.
properties.assertion: P+value<=bal0(sender) <=> (P<=bal0(sender) AND value<=bal0(sender)-P); prepay: sender'=bal0-P, escrow'=escrow+P, escrow!=sender, both live

audit_packet.guarantee: For a live sender and a distinct live escrow account, the single combined admission guard `intrinsic_cost P + value <= balance(sender)` is EXACTLY equivalent (both directions) to the two-stage guard `P <= balance(sender)` followed by `value <= balance(sender) after the P prepay`, where the prepay sets balance(sender) to exactly balance0(sender) - P and balance(escrow) to exactly balance0(escrow) + P. No admission decision may differ between the combined form and the staged form, and no intermediate arithmetic may wrap or truncate.
preconditions: escrow (fee/prepay recipient) is a DIFFERENT account from sender (root obligation hse: escrow ≠ sender); the two balance writes must not alias.
sender is a live/known account of the ledger before the prepay (root obligation hs₀: sender ∈ L₀.live).
escrow is a live/known account of the ledger before the prepay (root obligation he₀: escrow ∈ L₀.live).
Balances are non-negative unbounded quantities in the model; any fixed-width representation in the implementation must be shown not to wrap for P, value, P+value, balance-P, or balance(escrow)+P.

supporting_facts.claim: Admission is an IFF, not an implication: `P + value <= balance0(sender)` holds if and only if `P <= balance0(sender)` AND `value <= balance(sender) after prepaying P to escrow`. Neither direction may be lost.
supporting_facts.check: Extract both the combined funding predicate and the staged predicate actually evaluated during validate_transaction / process_transaction, and compare their accept/reject verdicts over the same (balance0, P, value) triples, including boundary triples P+value = balance0, P = balance0 with value = 0, and value = balance0 - P.
supporting_facts.expected: Identical verdict for every triple: any transaction admitted by one form is admitted by the other, and any rejected by one is rejected by the other.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any (balance0, P, value) exists where the implementation admits a transaction the combined predicate rejects (over-spend admitted) OR rejects one the combined predicate accepts (spurious rejection / consensus divergence).

supporting_facts.claim: The guard split is exact: `P + v <= b  <->  (P <= b AND v <= b - P)`. Its soundness rests on the exact arithmetic identities `(n + m) - m = n` and `x <= y -> x + (y - x) = y`, i.e. subtraction of P from b is information-preserving precisely when P <= b has already been established.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the implementation evaluates `P <= balance` FIRST and only then forms `balance - P` for the value comparison; confirm the subtraction operand order and that the result is used unmodified (no clamping, no saturating-to-zero substituted for the guard).
supporting_facts.expected: Order is: (1) compute P (intrinsic cost) exactly; (2) test P <= balance; (3) only on success compute remainder = balance - P; (4) test value <= remainder. Both tests must be able to fail independently.
supporting_facts.flag_if: `balance - P` is computed before or without the `P <= balance` test; or the subtraction saturates/clamps at zero and that clamped value is then compared against `value` (a saturating remainder of 0 silently converts an underfunded account into a 'value <= 0' pass when value is 0, and hides the missing P check); or `P + value` is compared against balance in a fixed-width type where the sum can wrap.

supporting_facts.claim: EXACT post-prepay balance: after debiting P from sender and crediting P to escrow, `balance(sender) = balance0(sender) - P`. This is an equality, not merely 'balance(sender) is nonzero' or 'balance(sender) >= 0'.
supporting_facts.check: After the intrinsic-cost prepay step, compare the sender's stored balance against the independently computed value `balance0(sender) - P`.
supporting_facts.expected: Bit-exact equality for every admitted transaction.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The post-prepay sender balance differs from balance0 - P by any amount, or the code only asserts a weaker property (non-negative, nonzero, 'did not error') instead of the exact remainder — a wrapped subtraction would satisfy 'non-negative' while yielding an enormous balance.

supporting_facts.claim: Frame property: writing a balance for account a leaves the balance of every account b ≠ a exactly unchanged. Specifically, crediting the escrow does not perturb the sender's balance, which is why the staged `value <= balance(sender)` check reads the intended post-debit remainder.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the escrow credit touches only the escrow entry, and that the sender balance observed by the value check is the post-debit value with no contribution from the escrow credit; verify the same for all other accounts in the ledger.
supporting_facts.expected: Only the sender and escrow entries change across the prepay; the sender's value equals balance0(sender) - P and every third-party balance is byte-identical before and after.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The escrow credit also mutates the sender's balance (aliasing, shared reference, or the same entry written twice), or any unrelated account balance changes across the prepay.

supporting_facts.claim: Write-exactness and conservation: a balance write stores EXACTLY the supplied value — sender becomes exactly `balance0(sender) - P` and escrow becomes exactly `balance0(escrow) + P`. The amount debited from the sender equals the amount credited to the escrow; the prepay neither mints nor burns.
supporting_facts.check: Sum the balance deltas of sender and escrow across the prepay; separately read back each written balance and compare against the exact intended value.
supporting_facts.expected: delta(sender) = -P, delta(escrow) = +P, sum of all balance deltas across the ledger = 0, and each read-back equals the intended written value exactly.
supporting_facts.flag_if: delta(sender) + delta(escrow) != 0 (value created or destroyed); or the escrow credit `balance(escrow) + P` wraps/overflows a fixed-width accumulator and lands below balance0(escrow); or a read-back differs from the written value.

supporting_facts.claim: All three root obligations are jointly required — escrow ≠ sender, sender live, escrow live. The equivalence is asserted only under all three; dropping any one leaves the staged guard unjustified.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm each obligation is enforced or structurally guaranteed on every path reaching the funding guard: the prepay recipient is derived so it can never equal the sender, and both accounts are present in the ledger prior to the debit/credit.
supporting_facts.expected: All three obligations hold on every path; when any fails the transaction is rejected rather than processed under the staged guard.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any path can reach the guard with escrow == sender (self-payment aliasing collapses the two writes and lets the credit undo the debit, so `value <= balance(sender)` is checked against the pre-debit balance), or with either account absent/implicitly defaulted into existence.

derived_obligations.check: Determine the representation used for `P + value` (or its equivalent combined funding sum) and prove it cannot wrap for the maximum representable P and value admitted upstream.
derived_obligations.expected: The sum is computed in a width that dominates the maximum admissible P and value, or the combined form is never materialized and only the staged form of FACT-2 is used.
derived_obligations.flag_if: P + value can wrap to a small number, making an under-funded transaction pass the funding guard — the highest-impact remote failure: a single crafted transaction admitted by one implementation and rejected by another, splitting consensus.

derived_obligations.check: Trace every computation of the post-prepay remainder `balance - P` and confirm the `P <= balance` guard strictly dominates it on all paths, with no unsigned subtraction performed on the unguarded path.
derived_obligations.expected: No subtraction of P from balance executes unless P <= balance was already established; the remainder is exact.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An unsigned `balance - P` underflows to a near-maximal value that then satisfies `value <= remainder`, admitting an arbitrarily large transfer from an account that could not even fund its intrinsic cost.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate how the escrow/prepay recipient is selected and test the case where it coincides with the sender.
derived_obligations.expected: escrow == sender is impossible by construction, or explicitly rejected before any balance write.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A transaction can make the prepay recipient equal to the sender, so the debit and credit alias and the sender is effectively never charged the intrinsic cost while still passing the value check.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm both sender and escrow are established members of the ledger state before the debit/credit, matching root obligations hs₀ and he₀.
derived_obligations.expected: Both accounts resolve to existing entries; absence is handled by an explicit, deterministic rule rather than by an implicit zero-balance materialization inside the guard.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An absent account is implicitly created with an assumed balance during the guard, so the funding check evaluates against a fabricated balance rather than ledger state.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the conservation identity delta(sender) = -P and delta(escrow) = +P across the prepay, including at the extremes: P = 0, P = balance0(sender), and escrow balance near the representation maximum.
derived_obligations.expected: Conservation holds exactly at every extreme; no wrap on the escrow credit.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The escrow credit overflows and conservation breaks (funds destroyed or created), or the identity only holds for mid-range values — a fund-integrity break reachable by a single transaction.

audit_packet.derivation: The arithmetic identities L005 ((n+m)-m = n) and L006 (x <= y -> x + (y-x) = y) yield L002, the exact guard split P + v <= b <-> (P <= b AND v <= b - P). Independently, the point-write lemmas L007/L008 give L003/L004: a balance write stores exactly the supplied value at its own account and leaves every other account untouched. Applying L004 to the sender debit and L003 to the escrow credit (which is where escrow != sender is consumed) gives L001: after the prepay, balance(sender) = balance0(sender) - P exactly. Substituting L001 into both directions of L002 yields the root equivalence ROOT (admission_iff_guards). The audit therefore checks the split (FACT-2 / OBS-1, OBS-2), the exact post-prepay remainder and frame (FACT-3, FACT-4), write-exactness and conservation (FACT-5 / OBS-5), and the three root obligations (FACT-6 / OBS-3, OBS-4).

properties.label: gas
properties.text: Verify validate_transaction independently enforces both fee guards — gas_used ≤ gas_limit and base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas — before any unsigned subtraction, since dropping either guard alone breaks the exact fee-conservation identity.
properties.assertion: reject unless (gas_used <= gas_limit) && (base_fee <= max_fee_per_gas); then (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + (U*f + Fb)) == G*p + Fb exactly

audit_packet.guarantee: Over unsigned (truncating) arithmetic, the fee split — unused-gas refund (G-U)*p, priority tip U*(p-f), base-fee component U*f, and the carried balance Fb — reconstructs the pre-charge total G*p + Fb EXACTLY, and this exact equality is guaranteed only when BOTH guards hold simultaneously: gas_used ≤ gas_limit (U ≤ G) and base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas (f ≤ p). Neither guard is redundant: the proof exhibits concrete counterexamples where one guard holds, the other is violated, and the reconstructed total differs from G*p + Fb.
preconditions: Quantities are the natural/unsigned-integer values G = gas limit, U = gas used, f = base fee per gas, p = max fee per gas, Fb = the pre-existing balance term carried through the split.
Subtraction on these quantities is unsigned/truncating (Lean ℕ: G - U and p - f saturate at 0 rather than going negative), matching unsigned integer arithmetic in the implementation.
Root theorem EthTotal.both_fee_guards_are_independently_necessary carries no must-establish obligation; the two guards below are read off the conclusion's counterexample structure, not invented.
Guard A (gas limit guard): U ≤ G, i.e. gas_used ≤ gas_limit.
Guard B (base fee guard): f ≤ p, i.e. base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas.

supporting_facts.claim: The gas limit guard cannot be dropped: there exist G, U, f, p, Fb with f ≤ p (base fee guard SATISFIED) and ¬(U ≤ G) (gas_used exceeds gas_limit) such that (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + (U*f + Fb)) ≠ G*p + Fb. This is an exact disequality of the two totals, not merely a 'suspicious value' — the base fee guard alone does not rescue the identity.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate/fuzz the fee-split computation over unsigned inputs restricted to f ≤ p but allowing U > G (e.g. by feeding a gas_used larger than the transaction's gas limit, or a gas limit reduced after gas accounting). Compare the reconstructed total (gas_limit-gas_used)*max_fee + (gas_used*(max_fee-base_fee) + (gas_used*base_fee + balance)) against gas_limit*max_fee + balance.
supporting_facts.expected: No reachable code path evaluates the fee split with gas_used > gas_limit; every such input is rejected or made unreachable by an explicit gas_used ≤ gas_limit check that precedes the (gas_limit - gas_used) subtraction.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The (gas_limit - gas_used) subtraction is performed on unsigned types without an established gas_used ≤ gas_limit guard, or the guard exists only downstream/after the subtraction, or it is assumed to follow from the base fee guard — any of these admits the L001 counterexample class (truncated/underflowed refund term, value not conserved).

supporting_facts.claim: The base fee guard cannot be dropped: there exist G, U, f, p, Fb with U ≤ G (gas limit guard SATISFIED) and ¬(f ≤ p) (base_fee exceeds max_fee_per_gas) such that (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + (U*f + Fb)) ≠ G*p + Fb. Again an exact disequality — the gas limit guard alone does not rescue the identity.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate/fuzz the same fee-split computation over unsigned inputs restricted to U ≤ G but allowing f > p (e.g. a transaction whose max_fee_per_gas is below the block's base fee, including base fee moving between validation and execution). Compare the reconstructed total against gas_limit*max_fee + balance.
supporting_facts.expected: validate_transaction rejects every transaction with max_fee_per_gas < base_fee of the block it is included in, so the (max_fee_per_gas - base_fee) subtraction only ever runs with base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The tip term (max_fee_per_gas - base_fee) is computed on unsigned types without an established base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas guard, the guard is applied against a stale/different base fee than the one used in the subtraction, or the guard uses a strict/off-by-one comparison that admits f > p — each admits the L002 counterexample class (truncated tip, value not conserved).

supporting_facts.claim: The root theorem is the CONJUNCTION of FACT-1 and FACT-2: both counterexample families exist simultaneously, so the two guards are independently necessary. Neither guard implies the other, and no single check can substitute for the pair; conversely, the exact conservation equality (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + (U*f + Fb)) = G*p + Fb is only warranted when both guards hold together.
supporting_facts.check: Trace every call site reaching the fee split (validate_transaction and any path that computes the refund, tip, or base-fee components) and confirm BOTH guards are established on that path — not one guard in validation and the other assumed. Confirm no path reaches the arithmetic with only one guard proven.
supporting_facts.expected: Every path into the fee-split arithmetic establishes gas_used ≤ gas_limit AND base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas; removing either check from the codebase produces a demonstrable failing input (a regression test should exist for each direction).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Only one guard is enforced; the two guards are enforced on different objects/blocks (e.g. base fee guard against a parent block's base fee while the subtraction uses the current one); a refactor collapses the two checks into one combined condition that can be satisfied by either disjunct; or the code relies on a saturating/checked-subtraction helper to 'absorb' a missing guard, which silently produces a total ≠ G*p + Fb rather than rejecting.

derived_obligations.check: Locate the gas limit guard on the validate_transaction path and confirm it is a non-strict comparison in the correct direction (gas_used ≤ gas_limit) evaluated on the same unsigned types and the same values later fed to (gas_limit - gas_used).
derived_obligations.expected: Guard present, ordered before the subtraction, and type/width-consistent with the operands of the subtraction.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Guard absent, inverted, strict where it should be non-strict, applied to a narrower/wider or differently-signed copy of the values, or evaluated after the refund term is computed.

derived_obligations.check: Locate the base fee guard on the validate_transaction path and confirm it is a non-strict comparison in the correct direction (base_fee ≤ max_fee_per_gas) against the exact base fee value used in the (max_fee_per_gas - base_fee) subtraction.
derived_obligations.expected: Guard present, ordered before the subtraction, and bound to the same base fee value as the subtraction.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Guard absent, inverted, strict, or compared against a base fee that can differ from the one used in the tip subtraction.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the exact conservation identity as a runtime/property test on all guard-passing inputs: (gas_limit-gas_used)*max_fee_per_gas + (gas_used*(max_fee_per_gas-base_fee) + (gas_used*base_fee + balance)) == gas_limit*max_fee_per_gas + balance, using wide-enough arithmetic that the products cannot wrap.
derived_obligations.expected: Exact equality on every guard-passing input; no tolerance, no 'approximately', no nonzero-only weakening.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any guard-passing input yields inequality (indicating a truncating subtraction or a wrapping multiplication in the product terms G*p, U*p, U*f), or the test only asserts a weaker consequence such as 'total is nonzero' / 'no revert'.

derived_obligations.check: Mutation-test independence: separately delete each guard and re-run the property test from OBS-3, since the root theorem asserts each deletion is independently exploitable.
derived_obligations.expected: Deleting the gas limit guard alone produces a failing input; deleting the base fee guard alone produces a different failing input. Each failure is caught by a dedicated regression test.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Either deletion leaves the test suite green — the suite does not actually pin the necessity of that guard, so a future refactor can remove it silently. At network scale this is the High-severity path: nodes that diverge on the fee split compute different post-state balances from the same transaction and split the chain.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is a conjunction of two existential counterexample statements. L001 supplies a witness where the base fee guard f ≤ p holds but the gas limit guard U ≤ G fails, and the reconstructed fee total differs from G*p + Fb; L002 supplies the mirror witness where U ≤ G holds but f ≤ p fails, with the same disequality. Because both witnesses exist, neither guard is implied by the other and neither can be dropped: the exact conservation equality is warranted only under the conjunction of both guards. The failure mechanism is truncating unsigned subtraction — G - U saturates when U > G, and p - f saturates when f > p — which is precisely the integer_overflow_underflow defect class. The audit therefore checks (a) each guard exists on every path reaching the fee-split arithmetic and precedes the corresponding subtraction (OBS-1, OBS-2), (b) the full exact identity, not a weakened nonzero/boolean shadow of it, holds on all guard-passing inputs (OBS-3), and (c) the independence claim itself is pinned by tests so neither guard can be removed silently (OBS-4). Remote reachability: both witness families are expressible as ordinary transaction/block field values, so a single crafted transaction reaching a client that dropped one guard yields a state-transition disagreement — a chain split, matching the High severity rating.

properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: For every burn-capable event in block processing (fee burn, state.destroy_account), check the recorded burn site is none or exactly the one canonical burn address, and that the allowlist bounds check admits that single entry with no fallback or default branch.
properties.assertion: forall e in block_events: e.burnSite == none || e.burnSite == BURN_ADDR; len(burn_allowlist)==1; site not in allowlist => reject

audit_packet.guarantee: Across the complete set of supply-changing events produced by processing one block, every event either records no burn site at all or records a burn site that is exactly the single canonical burn address x — there is no third outcome, no partially-matching address, and no unchecked default.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] (hc : SiteConfined M [x] τ): the burn-site allowlist for the audited block-processing path is a one-element list containing exactly the canonical burn address x, and the mint-site allowlist is M; both are fixed before any event of the block is processed.

ROOT obligation [1], field burn_mem: for every audited event e and every s with e.burnSite = some s, s must be a member of the burn allowlist [x]. This is the guard the implementation's bounds check has to enforce — the audit must confirm the check exists, not assume it.

ROOT obligation [1], field mint_mem: for every audited event e and every d with e.mintSite = some d, d must be a member of M. SiteConfined is a conjunction of both fields; the burn conclusion is only established in a context where the mint-site confinement also holds, so the mint side must be confirmed rather than dropped.

ROOT obligation [2] (e ∈ τ): the audited event set is the entire trace τ of mint/burn events emitted while processing the block — every burn-capable code path in the relevant surface (fee burn, state.destroy_account) must append its event into that same trace. Any burn-capable path that emits nothing into τ is outside the proved guarantee.

supporting_facts.claim: Under single-site confinement, every event in the block's trace satisfies the dichotomy e.burnSite = none OR e.burnSite = some x. These are the only two admissible outcomes for any event.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate every event the block-processing path can emit that carries a burn site (fee burn and state.destroy_account among them) and record, for each, the burn site value actually written. Compare each recorded value against the two admissible outcomes.
supporting_facts.expected: Every recorded burn site is either absent (none) or byte-for-byte equal to the single canonical burn address x.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event can be produced whose burn site is present and is not exactly x — including an attacker-influenced, caller-supplied, or partially-validated destination reachable by a single remote message or transaction, since such an event makes the burn destination implementation-dependent and splits the state root across clients.

supporting_facts.claim: sites_of_confined_singleton lifts a pointwise membership hypothesis to a universally quantified conclusion over the trace: if the confinement hypothesis holds for all events, then the none-or-exactly-x dichotomy holds for all events. Nothing in the statement exempts any event class, position, or ordering.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the implementation's burn-site validation is applied on every burn-emitting path uniformly, not only on a subset (e.g. only on one of the two surfaces, only on the first burn per block, or only when an amount is nonzero).
supporting_facts.expected: The same allowlist check gates every burn-site assignment on every burn-capable path.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any burn-capable path assigns or writes a burn site without passing through the allowlist check, or the check is skipped under a condition (zero amount, early-return, error path, reorg/replay path) — a single such gap is enough to reach a non-canonical burn destination remotely.

supporting_facts.claim: site_of_confined_singleton reasons on the Option value itself: an event's burn site is either genuinely absent (none) or a present value that must be witnessed as a member of the allowlist. Absence and presence are distinct cases, not encodings of one another.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect how 'no burn site' is represented for events that do not burn. Confirm it is a real absence and not a sentinel, zero-value, uninitialized, or default address that the comparison then treats as valid.
supporting_facts.expected: Events that do not burn carry an explicit absent burn site; events that burn carry a present site that was validated against the allowlist.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The absent case is represented by a sentinel/zero/default address, or an uninitialized field is read as if it were a validated site — this collapses the two cases and lets an unvalidated value be accepted as a burn destination.

supporting_facts.claim: eqOfMemSingleton is an exact-equality fact, and must be preserved as such: membership of b in the one-element allowlist [x] yields b = x, full equality — not 'b resembles x', 'b is in some set', or 'b is nonzero'.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the comparison used to validate a burn site against the canonical address. Confirm it is a full-width, exact equality over the entire address value.
supporting_facts.expected: Validation is an exact equality against x over the complete address, with no truncation, prefix/suffix matching, masking, length-limited comparison, case-normalized or lossy comparison, and no 'nonzero implies valid' shortcut.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The check compares fewer bytes than the full address, masks or truncates before comparing, tests only that the site is nonzero/non-default, or accepts membership in a broader set than the singleton — any of these admits a non-canonical address that passes validation.

supporting_facts.claim: memConsElim is exhaustive two-way case analysis on a cons-list: membership in x :: l yields either equality with the head x or membership in the tail l. There is no third case and no fall-through.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the allowlist scan/branch structure. Confirm that after checking the head entry and after exhausting the remaining entries, control reaches a definitive accept or reject with no default, fall-through, or implicit-accept branch.
supporting_facts.expected: The scan has exactly two outcomes: matched an entry (accept) or exhausted the list (reject).
supporting_facts.flag_if: A default/else branch accepts, an exception or error is swallowed into acceptance, or the loop can exit without a decision — an unhandled case here is the missing bounds check itself and yields an accepted out-of-allowlist burn destination.

supporting_facts.claim: notMemNil: nothing is a member of the empty list. Once the allowlist entries are exhausted, no candidate can be a member — the correct outcome is rejection, and the empty/unconfigured allowlist admits nothing at all.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise the validation with the allowlist exhausted or empty/unconfigured, and with a candidate site that matches no entry.
supporting_facts.expected: Validation rejects; no burn event is recorded with that site.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An empty or unconfigured allowlist is treated as 'no restriction' and accepts, or the scan reads past the end of the entry list (index/bounds overrun) and compares against out-of-range memory — either turns the missing bounds check into an accepted arbitrary burn destination.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the burn allowlist under audit has exactly one entry (the canonical burn address) and that its length is validated before any indexed access or scan, so no read occurs outside the list.
derived_obligations.expected: Allowlist length is exactly 1; a configuration with 0 entries or more than 1 entry is rejected or is impossible to construct on this path.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Length is unchecked, an index is used without a bounds test, or a second entry can be introduced by configuration, upgrade, or attacker-influenced input — this widens the proved singleton and breaks the exact-equality guarantee.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the mint-site side of the confinement precondition also holds: every event recording a mint site records one drawn from the mint allowlist M, validated by the same kind of membership check.
derived_obligations.expected: Every recorded mint site is a member of M, checked explicitly.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Mint sites are unvalidated or validated by a weaker rule — the confinement precondition is then only partially established, so the burn conclusion is being relied on in a state where its hypothesis does not fully hold.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate all burn-capable paths on the audited surface (burn address handling, fee burn, state.destroy_account) and confirm each one appends its event into the same audited trace that the guarantee ranges over.
derived_obligations.expected: The audited event set is complete for the block: no burn-capable path emits a burn outside it or bypasses event recording.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any burn-capable path mutates supply without recording an event in the audited trace — such a path is outside the universally quantified conclusion and its burn destination is entirely unconstrained.

derived_obligations.check: Establish remote reachability: determine whether a single externally submitted message or transaction can drive any burn-capable path with a site value it influences, and whether the resulting event would still satisfy the none-or-exactly-x dichotomy.
derived_obligations.expected: No remotely supplied input can cause a burn site other than the canonical address to be recorded; every such attempt is rejected by the allowlist check.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A single remote message or transaction can produce a burn event whose site is not exactly x — this is the High-severity outcome, since implementations that validate differently will disagree on post-state and split the chain.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem's two obligations fix the audit's scope and its guard: obligation [2] (e ∈ τ) makes the claim range over every event in the block's trace, so the audit must enumerate all burn-capable paths (OBS-3); obligation [1] (hc : SiteConfined M [x] τ) supplies both confinement fields — burn_mem, the allowlist guard that the implementation must actually enforce, and mint_mem, which must be checked too or the precondition is only partly established (OBS-2). L001 lifts the pointwise confinement hypothesis to all events with no exempt class (FACT-2). L002 splits each event's burn site into a genuine absence or a present value requiring a membership witness, so a sentinel/default must not stand in for absence (FACT-3). L003 supplies the strong fact — membership in the one-element allowlist gives exact equality with x, which must not be weakened to a prefix, mask, or nonzero test (FACT-4). L003 in turn rests on L004's exhaustive head-or-tail elimination, forbidding a fall-through or default-accept branch (FACT-5), and on L005, which makes the exhausted/empty list reject rather than admit and forbids reading past the list end (FACT-6). Together these are exactly the bounds-and-membership discipline whose absence is the missing_bounds_check defect class: the guarantee holds only if the allowlist is length-1 (OBS-1), scanned within bounds, compared for full equality, and rejects on exhaustion — otherwise a single remote transaction can record a non-canonical burn destination and split the chain (OBS-4).
