properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: For every block-processing balance increase, require a witnessed authorized mint: verify supply/mint/burn accounting equality, mint-and-burn site confinement, live-set support preservation, and per-account balance monotonicity before any credit is accepted.
properties.assertion: L'.supply+burned(t)=L.supply+minted(t) & SiteConfined(M,B,t) & supp & mono & L.bal a0<L'.bal a0 => EX d in M, v>0. mint(d,v) in t

audit_packet.guarantee: Whenever any single account's balance strictly increases across a block-processing state transition (L -> L'), the recorded event trace must contain an explicit mint event Ev.mint d v with a strictly positive amount v > 0 whose destination site d belongs to the authorized mint-site set M. No account may gain value without a positive, site-authorized mint witness in the trace.
preconditions: [hacc] Supply accounting holds exactly as an equality over the transition: L'.supply + burned(tau) = L.supply + minted(tau), where L.supply = sumOver L.bal L.live. This is an equality, not an inequality or a nonzero test.

[hc] SiteConfined M B tau holds: for every event e in tau, if e.mintSite = some d then d is in M, and if e.burnSite = some s then s is in B. Both the mint_mem and the burn_mem components are required.
[hsupp] Support preservation: for every account a, if L.bal a != 0 then a is a member of L'.live. No funded pre-state account may be dropped from the post-state live set.
[hbal] Per-account monotonicity on the post-state live set: for every a in L'.live, L.bal a <= L'.bal a. This is a per-account ordering bound, not an aggregate one.
[hlt] Trigger condition: there exists an account a0 with L.bal a0 < L'.bal a0 (strict increase).
[Ledger structure] Both L.live and L'.live are Distinct (no duplicate account entries), and Ledger.bal_live holds: any account with nonzero balance is a member of its own ledger's live list.

supporting_facts.claim: Under all five root obligations, a strict increase in any single account balance implies the existence of d and v with Ev.mint d v in tau, 0 < v, and d in M. This is the full root guarantee: existence of a mint event, positivity of its amount, and membership of its site in the authorized set - all three conjuncts.
supporting_facts.check: For every state transition where any account balance strictly increases, confirm the implementation records a mint event carrying a strictly positive amount and a destination site drawn from the authorized mint-site set, and that all five preconditions above are enforced rather than assumed.
supporting_facts.expected: Every strict balance increase is accompanied by a positive-amount mint event at an authorized site in the recorded trace.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account balance can rise across the transition without a corresponding positive-amount mint event, or with a mint event whose site is outside the authorized set M, or if any of the five preconditions is unchecked at runtime.

supporting_facts.claim: lt_supply_of_lt_bal_on: given support preservation (hsupp), per-account monotonicity on L'.live (hbal), and one strictly increasing account a0, the TOTAL supply strictly increases: L.supply < L'.supply. The underlying sumOver_lt_mem preserves the strict ordering, derived from pointwise <= on all members plus a single strict < at a0 in the list.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that a single account's credit is reflected as a strict increase of the aggregate supply accumulator, and that no other account is silently debited to keep the aggregate constant - monotonicity must hold for EVERY live account, not just the credited one.
supporting_facts.expected: L.supply < L'.supply holds strictly whenever any live account strictly gains and no live account loses.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The aggregate supply is recomputed or cached in a way that lets a per-account credit leave the total unchanged, or if monotonicity is only checked for the account being credited while other accounts may be decreased in the same transition.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_eq_of_support_iff: the supply sum is invariant under changes to the live list provided both lists are Distinct and the lists agree on the support of the balance function (for every a with bal a != 0, membership in l1 iff membership in l2). Distinctness of both lists is a required hypothesis, not an assumption of convenience.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the live-account set contains no duplicate entries in either the pre-state or the post-state, and that reordering or rebuilding the live set never changes which nonzero-balance accounts it contains.
supporting_facts.expected: Both live sets are duplicate-free, and the set of nonzero-balance accounts is identical between any two representations used to compute supply.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can appear twice in the live/account set (double-counting its balance into supply), or the live set can be rebuilt in a way that adds or drops a nonzero-balance account, which would break the supply equality that the whole mint witness rests on.

supporting_facts.claim: pos_minted_of_supply_lt (via pos_of_lt_add_left): combining the accounting equality with L.supply < L'.supply yields minted(tau) > 0 strictly. The step is exact: from n < n + m conclude 0 < m; the burned term cannot absorb a supply increase.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that any net supply increase is matched by a strictly positive recorded mint total, and that the burn total is accounted on the correct side of the accounting equality so it cannot mask an unrecorded issuance.
supporting_facts.expected: minted(tau) > 0 strictly whenever the post-state supply exceeds the pre-state supply, with the burn term never able to cancel it out.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Supply can grow while the recorded mint total is zero, or the burn amount is added on the wrong side / netted against mint such that an issuance is hidden.

supporting_facts.claim: mint_event_of_supply_lt: a strictly positive minted total yields a concrete event e in tau with 0 < e.mintAmount (exists_pos_mintAmount_of_minted_pos), and any event with positive mintAmount is definitionally exactly Ev.mint d e.mintAmount for some d (eq_mint_of_mintAmount_pos). The witness is a specific event in the trace with a specific positive amount - not merely a nonzero counter.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the trace contains an identifiable individual mint event with its own positive amount, rather than only an aggregate issuance counter, and that burn events cannot contribute a positive mintAmount.
supporting_facts.expected: A concrete Ev.mint d v entry with v > 0 is present in the trace and recoverable for audit.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Issuance is only tracked as a running total with no per-event record, or a burn-shaped event can be read as carrying a positive mint amount (the mintAmount/burnAmount discrimination is not exhaustive on the event type).

supporting_facts.claim: mintSite_mint plus SiteConfined.mint_mem: (Ev.mint d v).mintSite = some d definitionally, and confinement forces every event in tau whose mintSite is some d to have d in M. Hence mint_witness_confined pins the witness's destination to the authorized mint-site set M.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the destination recorded on a mint event is the same value that the site-confinement check validates against the authorized set M, and that confinement is applied to EVERY event in the trace, not only to a sampled or first event.
supporting_facts.expected: Every mint event's destination site is checked for membership in M, using the event's own recorded destination.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The site-confinement check is applied to a different field than the mint destination, is skipped for some events, or the authorized site set can be extended by the same transition that performs the mint.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce the supply accounting equality L'.supply + burned = L.supply + minted as a hard, exact post-transition check over block reward, issuance and withdrawal processing - recomputed from the account set rather than trusted from an incrementally maintained counter.
derived_obligations.expected: The equality holds exactly for every processed block; any mismatch aborts the transition.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The check is absent, is only an inequality or bounds-approximation, or compares an incrementally updated supply variable against itself so a lost or duplicated update cannot be detected.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce that every balance-crediting path (block reward, issuance, withdrawal credit, and any direct balance setter) emits a mint event with a destination site validated as a member of the authorized mint-site set M before the credit is applied.
derived_obligations.expected: No code path can increase an account balance without emitting a site-authorized mint event.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A balance-setting path exists that writes a larger balance without emitting a mint event, or emits one whose site is never checked against M - the classic missing bounds/authorization check that would let an attacker mint at an unauthorized site with a single remotely-submitted message.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce a strict positivity and an upper bound on every credited amount: the recorded mint amount must be > 0, and the sum of all balance increases in the transition must not exceed minted - burned as fixed by the accounting equality. Reject zero-amount and out-of-range amounts explicitly.
derived_obligations.expected: Every credit amount v satisfies 0 < v, and total credited value is bounded above by the recorded net issuance.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Amounts are accepted without a range check, an unchecked arithmetic operation can wrap a balance or the supply accumulator, or the aggregate of credits can exceed the recorded net issuance - the Critical missing_bounds_check failure this invariant guards.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce that the live/account set used to compute supply is duplicate-free in both the pre-state and post-state, and that supply is computed over that duplicate-free set.
derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness holds for both live sets at every point supply is computed.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An account can be inserted twice into the account set or iterated twice during supply accumulation, double-counting its balance and invalidating the accounting equality that the mint witness depends on.

derived_obligations.check: Enforce support preservation and per-account monotonicity as explicit guards: any account with a nonzero pre-state balance must still be present in the post-state live set, and no live account's balance may decrease during a pure crediting transition.
derived_obligations.expected: Every funded pre-state account is present post-state, and L.bal a <= L'.bal a for all a in L'.live.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An account with nonzero balance can be pruned, garbage-collected, or reset out of the live set during processing, or an account can be silently debited to offset a credit - either would let supply stay flat while a balance rises, defeating the mint witness entirely.

audit_packet.derivation: The trigger is a strict per-account balance increase L.bal a0 < L'.bal a0 (hlt). Support preservation (hsupp) places every funded pre-state account inside L'.live, and per-account monotonicity (hbal) bounds every live account below by its pre-state balance; sumOver_lt_mem [L006] then lifts the single strict increase at a0 to a strict increase of the aggregate, giving L.supply < L'.supply [L002]. Aggregate supply is well-defined and representation-independent because both live lists are Distinct and agree on the nonzero-balance support [L005]. Combining the strict supply increase with the accounting equality (hacc) and pos_of_lt_add_left [L020] forces minted(tau) > 0 strictly [L008]; the burn term cannot absorb the increase. A positive minted total yields a concrete trace event with positive mintAmount [L007], which is definitionally exactly an Ev.mint d v constructor application [L009], producing the existential mint event with 0 < v [L003]. Finally mintSite_mint [L004] gives (Ev.mint d v).mintSite = some d, and SiteConfined.mint_mem (hc) then forces d in M [L001], yielding the full root conclusion: an explicit, positive-amount, authorized-site mint witness for every balance increase [ROOT]. All five root obligations are load-bearing: dropping hacc breaks the mint total, dropping hc breaks site authorization, dropping hsupp or hbal breaks the aggregate lift, and hlt is the trigger itself.

omitted_facts.reason: sumOver_congr_mem is a pointwise-congruence plumbing lemma for the summation operator; it carries no independent security-relevant condition beyond the Distinct and support-agreement hypotheses already surfaced in FACT-3 and OBS-4.
notMemNil is a vacuous-membership base-case lemma about the empty list with no implementation-level obligation.
sumOver_zero states that summing the constant-zero function is zero; a definitional arithmetic identity with no auditable check.
memConsElim is a list cons-membership case-analysis eliminator, pure structural recursion machinery.
exists_split_of_mem is a list-decomposition helper used to isolate a member; no implementation-level condition.
memRemoveMiddleOfNe is list-surgery bookkeeping for membership under middle-element removal; subsumed by the distinctness and support-agreement obligations in OBS-4.
memInsertMiddle is the dual list-surgery membership lemma; same reason as L015.
Distinct.notMemMiddle is an internal consequence of list distinctness; the auditable content is the distinctness requirement itself, captured in FACT-3 and OBS-4.
Distinct.removeMiddle preserves distinctness under middle-element removal; internal to the sum-invariance proof, its auditable content is already OBS-4.
sumOver_middle is an arithmetic decomposition of the sum around a distinguished element; no independent implementation obligation.
sumOver_append is the additivity of the summation operator over list concatenation; a definitional arithmetic property with no auditable runtime check.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} {L L' : EthTotal.Ledger A} {τ : EthTotal.Trace A} {M B : List A},
  Eq (instHAdd.hAdd L'.supply (EthTotal.burned τ)) (instHAdd.hAdd L.supply (EthTotal.minted τ)) →
    EthTotal.SiteConfined M B τ →
      instLTNat.lt L.supply L'.supply →
        Exists fun d =>
          Exists fun v =>
            And (List.instMembership.mem τ (EthTotal.Ev.mint d v))
              (And (instLTNat.lt 0 v) (List.instMembership.mem M d))
x_proof_closure.conclusion:
Exists fun d =>
  Exists fun v =>
    And (List.instMembership.mem τ (EthTotal.Ev.mint d v)) (And (instLTNat.lt 0 v) (List.instMembership.mem M d))

∀ {A : Type u} (L L' : EthTotal.Ledger A),
  (∀ (a : A), Ne (L.bal a) 0 → List.instMembership.mem L'.live a) →

      ∀ {a₀ : A}, instLTNat.lt (L.bal a₀) (L'.bal a₀) → instLTNat.lt L.supply L'.supply

  EthTotal.Distinct (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)) →
    Not (List.instMembership.mem (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂) a)

∀ {A : Type u} {a : A} {l₁ l₂ : List A},
  EthTotal.Distinct (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)) →
    EthTotal.Distinct (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)

∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) (l₁ : List A) (a : A) (l₂ : List A),
  Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)))

Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)))
  (instHAdd.hAdd (f a) (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)))

x_proof_closure.statement: ∀ {n m : Nat}, instLTNat.lt n (instHAdd.hAdd n m) → instLTNat.lt 0 m

∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) (l₁ l₂ : List A),
  Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂))
    (instHAdd.hAdd (EthTotal.sumOver f l₁) (EthTotal.sumOver f l₂))
x_proof_closure.conclusion:
Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂))
  (instHAdd.hAdd (EthTotal.sumOver f l₁) (EthTotal.sumOver f l₂))

properties.label: transactions
properties.text: Guard every CALL/state.move_ether transfer: require bal(s) >= v before any balance write, and assert post-transfer total supply + burned == pre-supply + minted, so a clamped or wrapped debit cannot silently create the shortfall v - bal(s).
properties.assertion: pre: s,d in live && bal(s) >= v; post: supply' + burned == supply + minted && every mint site in M && mint amount > 0

audit_packet.guarantee: For an ether transfer of value v from s to d on a live ledger, if the debit is attempted while bal(s) < v (overdraft) and the implementation still reports the global accounting identity supply' + burned = supply + minted with all mint/burn sites confined to the authorized site lists M and B, then the trace provably contains an explicit mint event Ev.mint e w with w > 0 and e in M. Contrapositive and the actual audit target: if no authorized, positive, explicitly recorded issuance event exists, then an overdrafting move_ether must be impossible — the balance check must reject it before any state write, because the underlying arithmetic silently manufactures exactly v - bal(s) new wei.
preconditions: ROOT/hs: the sender s is a member of the live account set (L.live) — the account is present in state, not a synthesized or defaulted entry.
ROOT/hd: the recipient d is a member of the live account set (L.live) — the credit target exists in state before the write.
ROOT/hgt: the overdraft condition bal(s) < v holds — the requested transfer value strictly exceeds the sender's balance. This is exactly the situation the balance check must reject.

ROOT/hacc: the global accounting identity supply' + burned(τ) = supply(τ) + minted(τ) is asserted to hold across the transfer, where supply is the sum of all live balances (EthTotal.Ledger.supply = sumOver bal live).

ROOT/hc: SiteConfined M B τ — every event in the trace whose mintSite is some d has d in M, and every event whose burnSite is some s has s in B; issuance and destruction are confined to the enumerated authorized sites.

Ledger well-formedness carried by the structure: live is Distinct (no duplicate account entries) and bal_live holds (any account with nonzero balance is in live). Duplicate or missing live entries invalidate the supply accounting used throughout.

supporting_facts.claim: An overdrafting transfer that still satisfies the global accounting identity, under site confinement, forces the existence of a mint event Ev.mint e w in the trace with w > 0 and e in M. There is no silent path: the created value must appear as authorized, recorded issuance.
supporting_facts.check: Construct or replay a transfer where the requested value strictly exceeds the sender balance (bal(s) < v) with both accounts live. Capture the pre-state supply, the post-state supply, and the full issuance/burn event log the implementation emits for that transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: Either the transfer is rejected before any balance mutation (no state write, no supply change), or the implementation emits an explicit issuance event with a strictly positive amount at an account that appears in the authorized issuance site list M.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The transfer mutates balances and the post-state total supply differs from the pre-state total supply while no positive, authorized issuance event is recorded — value was created outside the accounting.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact quantity, not merely 'some increase': after an overdrafting transfer of v from s to d, the new total supply equals supply + (v - bal(s)). The inflation amount is exactly the shortfall v - bal(s), and it is strictly greater than zero (L002 gives supply < supply').
supporting_facts.check: For an overdrafting transfer, compute total supply as the sum over all live accounts before and after the transfer, and compare the delta against the shortfall v - bal(s) computed from the pre-state sender balance.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply - pre_supply == v - pre_bal(s), exactly, with no rounding or truncation, whenever the overdrafting path is reachable at all. Under a correct implementation this path is unreachable because the balance check rejects it first.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The delta is nonzero but is only reported as 'balance changed' or 'nonzero' by monitoring, or the delta differs from v - pre_bal(s) — either indicates the accounting model does not match the arithmetic actually performed.

supporting_facts.claim: The inflation is a direct consequence of saturating subtraction on a natural-number balance domain: L026 gives x - y = 0 when x <= y, and L016 gives min(v,b) + (b - v) = b. So debiting bal(s) - v when bal(s) < v clamps to 0 instead of going negative, and L006 gives 0 < v - bal(s): the clamped-away remainder is strictly positive and is precisely what gets created.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the balance-debit arithmetic on the transfer path for the underflow discipline of the value domain: whether subtraction saturates at zero, wraps modulo the word size, or traps. Then confirm that the sufficiency check on the sender balance strictly precedes the subtraction and cannot be bypassed on any branch (including nested CALL frames and reverted-then-resumed paths).
supporting_facts.expected: The value-sufficiency comparison bal(s) >= v gates the subtraction on every path, so the subtraction is only ever evaluated where it is exact and the clamping/wrapping branch is dead code.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any path reaches the debit subtraction without a preceding, non-bypassable bal(s) >= v check, or the subtraction relies on saturation or modular wraparound to 'handle' insufficiency rather than rejecting the transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: The per-account update laws are exact equalities and must be preserved individually, not just in aggregate. L018: crediting d adds exactly v to total supply. L019: debiting s removes only min(v, bal(s)) — strictly less than v under overdraft. L014: supply' + min(v, bal(s)) = supply + v. L027/L028/L029: a single-account balance write changes the sum by exactly the write delta, and this relies on live being duplicate-free (Distinct).
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the credit leg and the debit leg move the accounted total by equal and opposite amounts on every successful transfer, and that the account set used to compute total supply contains no duplicate entries. Compare the credit amount applied to d against the debit amount removed from s for the same transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: debit_amount_removed_from_s == credit_amount_added_to_d == v for every accepted transfer, and the account set is duplicate-free so the sum-over-accounts equals the accounted supply.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The debit leg removes less than the credit leg adds (the min(v, bal(s)) clamp), the two legs are computed from different value sources, the credit is applied before the debit can fail, or the same account appears twice in the balance-summation set.

supporting_facts.claim: Any strict increase in total supply under the accounting identity forces minted(τ) > 0 (L008), which forces an actual event in the trace with positive mint amount (L007), which is necessarily of the form Ev.mint d amount (L009). The obligation is an explicit, positively-valued, individually-attributable issuance event — not merely a nonzero aggregate counter.
supporting_facts.check: Whenever the accounted total supply increases across a transfer, require a corresponding recorded issuance event with a strictly positive amount and an identified destination account. Confirm the aggregate issuance total for the interval equals the sum of the individual recorded issuance events.
supporting_facts.expected: supply increase > 0 implies at least one recorded issuance event with amount > 0 and a named destination, and aggregate issuance == sum of individual issuance event amounts.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Total supply rises with only an aggregate counter incremented and no per-event record, or the aggregate issuance total exceeds the sum of the individually recorded, positively-valued issuance events.

supporting_facts.claim: Membership, not just existence: L004 gives mintSite (Ev.mint d v) = some d, so each mint event names its destination as its site; combined with SiteConfined.mint_mem (L001), the destination of every mint witness must be a member of the authorized issuance site list M. The witness produced by the root theorem satisfies mint event in trace AND amount > 0 AND site in M.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate the destination accounts of all issuance events produced by the transfer path and check each for membership in the authorized issuance site list M. Symmetrically, check that every destruction event's source account is a member of B.
supporting_facts.expected: Every issuance event destination is a member of M and every destruction event source is a member of B; the transfer/CALL path itself introduces no issuance site outside M.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An issuance event names a destination outside M — in particular, if the overdraft shortfall surfaces as issuance credited to an ordinary transfer recipient d rather than an authorized issuance site, which is the concrete remote fund-integrity break.

derived_obligations.check: On the value-transfer path (CALL with nonzero value, state.move_ether), confirm the sender balance sufficiency comparison bal(s) >= v is evaluated and enforced strictly before any balance mutation, on every branch and at every nesting depth, with no path that mutates first and validates afterwards.
derived_obligations.expected: Insufficient-balance transfers are rejected with zero balance mutation on both legs; the debit arithmetic is unreachable when bal(s) < v.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any reachable ordering where the debit or credit is applied before the sufficiency check, or where the check is skipped for a subset of call types, depths, or value sources.

derived_obligations.check: Audit the arithmetic domain of the balance debit: reject saturating (clamp-to-zero) and modular-wrapping subtraction as the insufficiency handler. Fuzz with v spanning the sender balance boundary and the maximum representable value, including v = bal(s), v = bal(s)+1, and v at the domain maximum.
derived_obligations.expected: Out-of-range or insufficient values cause explicit rejection; no input produces a debit that removes less than v while the credit adds v.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any tested value yields a post-state where the sender balance clamped at zero or wrapped, while the recipient was still credited the full v.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the conservation identity as a runtime or differential-test invariant across the transfer path: sum of all account balances after + total destroyed == sum of all account balances before + total issued. Compute the sums over a duplicate-free account set.
derived_obligations.expected: The identity holds exactly for every transfer; any residual is zero.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero residual appears on any transfer, or the identity is only checked in aggregate over long intervals where a per-transfer shortfall of v - bal(s) can be netted out against unrelated issuance and destruction.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate every code path that can increase the accounted total supply and confirm each is an authorized issuance site in M, emits a per-event record with a strictly positive amount and a named destination, and that the value-transfer path is not among them.
derived_obligations.expected: The set of supply-increasing paths equals the authorized issuance sites in M; the transfer/CALL path never increases total supply.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The transfer path can increase total supply, or a supply increase occurs at a site absent from M, or an increase occurs without a per-event positive-amount record.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the ledger well-formedness assumptions the accounting rests on: both the sender and recipient are resolved to real entries in the live account set before the transfer, and the account set used for balance summation is duplicate-free.
derived_obligations.expected: Both transfer endpoints resolve to live entries prior to mutation; no account is counted twice in the supply sum.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A transfer endpoint is synthesized, defaulted, or aliased into existence during the transfer, or duplicate account entries let one balance contribute more than once to the accounted supply.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is proved by composing two independent halves. The inflation half (L002, via L005/L010) shows that an overdrafting transfer — debit bal(s) - v with bal(s) < v, then credit d with +v — produces a strictly larger total supply, and pins the exact increase at v - bal(s). That exactness comes from the per-account update laws: L018 (credit adds exactly v), L019 (debit removes only min(v, bal(s))), combined in L014 as supply' + min(v, bal(s)) = supply + v, all resting on L027/L028/L029 (a single-account write shifts the sum by exactly the write delta, given a duplicate-free live set). The clamp is the defect mechanism: L026 gives x - y = 0 when x <= y and L016 gives min(v,b) + (b - v) = b, so under overdraft the debit saturates and only min(v, bal(s)) = bal(s) leaves the sender while v arrives at the recipient; L006 makes the residual v - bal(s) strictly positive. The attribution half (L001) then takes any strict supply increase together with the accounting identity and forces a witness: L008 turns supply < supply' into minted(τ) > 0, L007 turns a positive aggregate into an actual event with positive mint amount, L009 shapes that event as Ev.mint d amount, and L004 plus SiteConfined.mint_mem places its destination inside M. Composed, the root delivers a positive, explicitly recorded, authorized-site issuance witness for every overdrafting transfer that claims to conserve value. The audit consequence runs the implication backwards: since no authorized issuance site is supposed to fire on an ordinary value transfer, the overdraft path must be unreachable, which is precisely what the pre-mutation balance check enforces (OBS-1). All five root obligations are covered — hs and hd by OBS-5, hgt by OBS-1/OBS-2 as the condition to be rejected, hacc by OBS-3, hc by OBS-4.

omitted_facts.reason: add_sub_cancel_right ((n + m) - m = n) is generic natural-number arithmetic plumbing with no distinct implementation-observable surface; its security content is already carried by FACT-3's saturating-subtraction check.
pos_of_lt_add_left (n < n + m implies 0 < m) is a generic ordering step internal to L008; its consequence, minted > 0, is exposed directly in FACT-5.
add_right_cancel is generic cancellation used to rearrange the supply equations; the resulting exact equalities are exposed in FACT-2 and FACT-4.
min_comm is a commutativity rewrite with no implementation-observable content; the clamp semantics it supports are covered by FACT-3.
add_left_cancel is generic cancellation supporting L013; no independent audit surface.
le_min is a generic lattice property of min used only to prove min_comm; subsumed by FACT-3 and FACT-4.
min_le_right is a generic min bound supporting L015; no independent audit surface.
min_le_left is a generic min bound supporting L015; no independent audit surface.
min_eq_left is a generic case split on min supporting L016; the clamp behaviour it formalizes is checked in FACT-3.
add_sub_cancel_of_le (x + (y - x) = y when x <= y) is generic arithmetic supporting L016; its content is checked as exactness of the debit in FACT-4.
min_eq_right is the complementary case split to L023 supporting L016; no independent audit surface.
notMemNil is a list base-case elimination internal to the sumOver induction; no implementation-observable surface.

sumOver_update_notMemOfPoint states that updating an account absent from the summation list leaves the sum unchanged — an induction step for L029. Its audit-relevant corollary, that the summation account set must be exact and duplicate-free, is carried in FACT-4 and OBS-5.
memConsElim is a list-membership case-split combinator internal to the sumOver induction; no implementation-observable surface.

properties.label: transactions
properties.text: Verify that a CALL-driven ether transfer rejects value > sender balance before any state write, so a self-transfer to an existing live account cannot truncate the debit to min(value, balance) and mint value - balance into total supply.
properties.assertion: v > bal(s) => transfer aborts before any write; if applied: supply' == supply + (v - bal(s)) > supply; for d == s require supply' == supply

audit_packet.guarantee: An ether transfer whose value exceeds the sender's balance must be rejected before any balance is written. If a two-step debit-then-credit is executed instead with unsigned/truncating subtraction, total supply is not merely perturbed: it increases by exactly (value - sender_balance), which is strictly positive, and the self-transfer case (recipient == sender) is the maximal-leverage instance because the sender is credited the full value it was never able to pay. The audited implementation must make this state unreachable and must preserve exact supply conservation across every transfer.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hs: the sender account s is an existing entry of the live account set (s ∈ L.live); i.e. the transfer path operates on an account that is already counted in the total-supply sum.

ROOT obligation hgt: the transfer value v strictly exceeds the sender's recorded balance (L.bal s < v); this is the trigger condition and must be treated as reachable input, not as an impossible case.
Balances are unsigned naturals (Nat) whose subtraction truncates at zero rather than reverting or wrapping; total supply is defined as the sum of balances over the live account list.
The live account list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct / Distinct), so each account contributes to total supply exactly once.

supporting_facts.claim: For a live sender s and value v with bal(s) < v, the naive sequence 'set bal(s) := bal(s) - v; then set bal(s) := bal(s) + v' yields a ledger whose total supply is STRICTLY GREATER than the original total supply. The root theorem is the self-transfer instance (d = s) of the general overdraft transfer result, which inflates supply for any live destination d.
supporting_facts.check: Drive a value transfer (CALL semantics) where the recipient equals the sender and value > sender balance, and compare the sum of all account balances before and after the operation. Also run the general case with a distinct live recipient.
supporting_facts.expected: The operation is rejected before any balance mutation, and the sum of all balances is unchanged. No execution path may reach the post-state described by the theorem.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The sum of all account balances after the operation is greater than before, or the operation is accepted at all when value > sender balance.

supporting_facts.claim: The inflation is an EXACT equality, not just an inequality: supply_after = supply_before + (v - bal(s)). The minted amount equals the shortfall exactly. Do not weaken this to 'supply changes' or 'supply is nonzero'.
supporting_facts.check: If any code path performs debit-then-credit without a prior sufficiency check, compute the exact delta of total supply for chosen (bal(s), v) pairs with v > bal(s) — e.g. bal(s)=0 with v = 2^128, and bal(s)=1 with v = 2.
supporting_facts.expected: Delta is identically zero on every accepted path; the value (v - bal(s)) is never realizable as newly created balance. Any sufficiency check must compare against the FULL value v, not against the post-debit or clamped amount.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Measured supply delta equals v - bal(s) for any input, or a guard bounds only the debit amount (min(v, bal(s))) instead of rejecting v > bal(s) outright.

supporting_facts.claim: Under the root precondition bal(s) < v, the shortfall is strictly positive: 0 < v - bal(s). Every overdraft transfer therefore mints a nonzero amount — there is no benign boundary case.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the sufficiency guard rejects the entire range v > bal(s), including v = bal(s) + 1, and accepts the exact-boundary case v = bal(s).
supporting_facts.expected: v = bal(s) accepted (zero shortfall); every v >= bal(s) + 1 rejected before mutation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An off-by-one guard (e.g. rejecting only v > bal(s) + 1, or comparing with the wrong operand order) admits any v > bal(s), or the boundary v = bal(s) is spuriously rejected while larger values pass.

supporting_facts.claim: The general conservation identity for a debit-then-credit pair is supply_after + min(v, bal(s)) = supply_before + v. Supply is conserved only in the regime where min(v, bal(s)) = v, i.e. exactly when v <= bal(s).
supporting_facts.check: For a transfer between a live sender and a live recipient, verify the conservation identity holds with the FULL value on both sides — i.e. that the amount removed from the sender equals the amount added to the recipient.
supporting_facts.expected: Debited amount == credited amount == v on every accepted transfer, so supply_after == supply_before.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The debited amount is computed by a saturating/clamping operation (min, checked-with-fallback, or unsigned subtraction that floors at zero) while the credited amount uses the unclamped v.

supporting_facts.claim: Debit side, exact: supply(after debit) + min(v, bal(s)) = supply_before. The debit removes only min(v, bal(s)) from total supply — this asymmetry is the direct root cause of the defect.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect and exercise the sender-side balance write (the debit in the ether-movement path). Determine whether subtracting v from a smaller bal(s) floors at zero, wraps, or aborts.
supporting_facts.expected: The subtraction cannot silently produce a floored or wrapped result: either the sufficiency check has already made bal(s) >= v, or the subtraction itself aborts the whole operation with no state retained.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Unsigned subtraction floors at zero (bal(s) becomes 0 and the deficit is silently discarded), wraps to a huge value, or the deficit is otherwise absorbed without aborting.

supporting_facts.claim: Credit side, exact: supply(after credit) = supply_before + v. The credit adds the full v to total supply unconditionally, regardless of what the debit actually managed to remove.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the recipient credit is never applied unless the matching debit removed the identical amount v, and that the credit is not applied twice or applied to a re-read (stale) sender balance when recipient == sender.
supporting_facts.expected: Credit and debit are atomic and equal-valued; when recipient == sender the net balance change is exactly zero and the account's balance is unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The credit executes on a path where the debit was skipped, clamped, or partially applied; or the self-transfer case reads the sender's balance before the debit and writes back that stale value plus v.

supporting_facts.claim: Single-account update conservation, exact: supply(setBal a v) + bal_before(a) = supply_before + v. Any single balance write shifts total supply by exactly (new_value - old_value), so total supply is fully determined by the writes performed.
supporting_facts.check: For each individual balance write in the transfer path, confirm the total-supply delta equals new_value minus old_value, and that the sender's pre-debit balance is read once and not re-read after the debit when recipient == sender.
supporting_facts.expected: Per-write supply delta accounts exactly for the write; the two writes of a self-transfer cancel to zero net delta.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A write is computed from a balance snapshot taken before an intervening write to the same account (the aliasing pattern in the theorem), producing a net nonzero delta on a self-transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: Total supply is the sum of balances over the live account list, and updating one account changes that sum only through that account's entry — provided the list is duplicate-free (Distinct); updating an account absent from the list leaves the sum unchanged.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the account set used to compute or reason about total supply contains no duplicate entries for a single account, and that touching an account not present in that set (e.g. an account created or resurrected by the transfer) is accounted for consistently rather than double-counted or dropped.
supporting_facts.expected: Each account contributes exactly one balance to the supply sum; account lookup for the sender resolves to the same single entry that the debit and the credit both write.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The sender can be resolved to two distinct entries (so the debit hits one and the credit the other), or a balance change lands on an account outside the counted set and is silently lost or duplicated.

derived_obligations.check: Locate every ether-value-movement path reachable from a CALL-style operation and confirm each one performs an explicit sender-sufficiency comparison (value <= sender balance) BEFORE the first balance write.
derived_obligations.expected: Every such path has the check, and the check precedes all mutation.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path writes a balance before the sufficiency comparison, or lacks the comparison entirely.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm rejection is a full abort of the pending state changes, not a partial application — no debit, no credit, no account creation survives when value > sender balance.
derived_obligations.expected: Post-state on rejection is bit-identical to the pre-state for all touched accounts and for total supply.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any residue of the failed transfer persists (e.g. a zeroed sender balance, a created recipient entry, or a partial credit).

derived_obligations.check: Test the aliasing case explicitly: sender == recipient, with (a) value <= balance and (b) value > balance.
derived_obligations.expected: (a) balance and total supply both unchanged; (b) rejected before mutation with total supply unchanged.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Case (a) changes the balance or supply, or case (b) succeeds and raises the sender balance and total supply by (value - balance).

derived_obligations.check: Audit the arithmetic type and operator used for the sender debit: is it an unsigned type whose subtraction saturates at zero, wraps modulo 2^n, or raises?
derived_obligations.expected: Underflow is impossible by construction on the accepted path (guard established balance >= value) and, defensively, the subtraction operator itself aborts rather than saturating or wrapping.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Saturating or wrapping subtraction is used for the debit while the credit adds the unclamped value.

derived_obligations.check: Assert a global conservation property over the transfer: the sum of all account balances is invariant across every accepted transfer, and rejected transfers leave it invariant too. Exercise it with randomized (balance, value, sender==recipient?) inputs biased toward value > balance and toward zero-balance senders.
derived_obligations.expected: Sum of balances is constant across the whole test population; no input yields a positive delta.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any input yields a nonzero supply delta, in particular a delta equal to value - balance.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the sender's balance is read exactly once per transfer and that the debit and credit operate on the same resolved account entry, so the credit cannot be computed from a pre-debit snapshot when recipient == sender.
derived_obligations.expected: A single resolved account handle is used for both writes; the self-transfer reduces to a no-op.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Separate account lookups or a cached pre-debit balance feed the credit computation.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem models a transfer as two independent balance writes on a ledger whose total supply is the sum of balances over a duplicate-free live account list. FACT-8 (L021/L022/L024) establishes that a single-account update moves the sum only through that account's entry; FACT-7 (L020) makes that shift exact (new minus old). Applying it to each leg gives the two asymmetric halves: FACT-6 (L011) shows the credit adds exactly v, while FACT-5 (L012) shows the debit removes only min(v, bal(s)) because unsigned subtraction truncates at zero. Combining them yields the conservation identity FACT-4 (L007): supply_after + min(v, bal(s)) = supply_before + v — conserved precisely when v <= bal(s). Under the root precondition bal(s) < v the min collapses to bal(s), and the identity simplifies to the exact shortfall equation FACT-2 (L002/L004): supply_after = supply_before + (v - bal(s)). FACT-3 (L003) makes the shortfall strictly positive, turning the equality into the strict inequality FACT-1 (L001/ROOT). The root theorem is the d = s instance, where the same account absorbs both writes, so an account with insufficient funds ends up strictly richer and the network's total ether supply grows — a remotely triggerable, single-transaction fund-integrity break, hence Critical. The defensive obligation therefore is not 'detect the anomaly afterwards' but 'make the precondition bal(s) < v unreachable past the first state write', plus a standing exact-conservation assertion so any future truncating debit is caught as a nonzero supply delta rather than a silently absorbed deficit.

omitted_facts.reason: add_sub_cancel_right ((n + m) - m = n) is a pure Nat arithmetic identity used only to discharge the strict-positivity step; it carries no independent implementation obligation.
add_right_cancel is a generic cancellation lemma used to reshape supply equations; the security content is already captured by the exact supply identities in FACT-4, FACT-5, FACT-6, FACT-7.
min_comm is a commutativity fact about Nat min, used only for rewriting; it asserts nothing about ledger state.
min_add_sub (min(v,b) + (b - v) = b) is the arithmetic core of the truncation behaviour, but its security-relevant consequence is already stated in stronger, ledger-level form as FACT-5 and FACT-4.
add_left_cancel is a generic cancellation lemma with no ledger content.
le_min is a lattice property of Nat min used in proving min_comm; no implementation obligation.
min_le_right is a lattice property of Nat min; no implementation obligation.
min_le_left is a lattice property of Nat min; no implementation obligation.
min_eq_left is a case-split helper for Nat min; its effect on the ledger is subsumed by FACT-4's conservation regime condition.
add_sub_cancel_of_le is a Nat arithmetic identity under a <= hypothesis, used only to close the conserved branch.
min_eq_right is the dual case-split helper for Nat min; subsumed by FACT-4 and FACT-2.
sub_eq_zero_of_le states Nat subtraction floors at zero; this is the modelling assumption behind FACT-5, already surfaced as a precondition and as OBS-4 rather than as a separate check.
notMemNil is a base-case elimination for the empty list in the sum-update induction; it is proof plumbing with no implementation counterpart.
memConsElim is the cons-case eliminator for list membership used in the same induction; proof plumbing only, its ledger-level consequence is FACT-8.

properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: Verify every supply-increasing step (block reward, issuance, withdrawal credit) bounds-checks its mint amount before it is applied, and that over any n blocks with all mint amounts zero the total supply never rises and burn accounting balances exactly.
properties.assertion: (forall i<n, forall mint(d,v) in trace(i): v==0) => supply(n) <= supply(0) && supply(n) + sum_{i<n} burned(i) == supply(0)

audit_packet.guarantee: Over any finite run of n consecutive recorded state transitions, if every mint event recorded in every step's trace carries amount 0, then the total supply cannot increase; moreover supply is conserved exactly: final supply plus all burned amounts equals the initial supply. The general per-step and per-chain accounting identity (supply' + burned = supply + minted) holds unconditionally, so any supply increase must be attributable to a positive, explicitly recorded mint amount.
preconditions: Root obligation [1] (h): for every step index i < n, and for every mint event Ev.mint d v occurring in the trace of step i, the minted amount v equals 0. This must hold for ALL i in [0, n) and for ALL mint events in each trace — a single unbounded or unchecked mint amount at any index voids the guarantee.

Every step of the run is a Recorded transition from Ls i to Ls (i+1): each step carries a trace of mint/burn events and satisfies the balanced field, supply(Ls (i+1)) + burned(trace) = supply(Ls i) + minted(trace). Every supply change must therefore be recorded as an event in that step's trace.

Each Ledger is well formed: the live account list is Distinct (no duplicate accounts) and any account with a nonzero balance is a member of live (bal_live), so supply = sumOver bal live counts every funded account exactly once.
The index range is the full range [0, n): the run under audit covers every step, with no skipped, batched, or reordered index.

supporting_facts.claim: If every mint event amount in every step trace for i < n is 0, then supply(Ls n) is not greater than supply(Ls 0); equivalently (by not_lt_iff_le) supply(Ls n) <= supply(Ls 0). This is an ordering fact, not merely 'supply did not change by a lot'.
supporting_facts.check: Replay n consecutive transitions in which no supply-increasing operation (block reward, issuance, withdrawal credit) contributes a positive amount, and compare the total supply computed over the ledger before and after the run.
supporting_facts.expected: total_supply_after <= total_supply_before, for every n including n = 0 and long runs.
supporting_facts.flag_if: total_supply_after > total_supply_before for any run whose recorded mint amounts are all zero, or the comparison is implemented only as an approximate/tolerance check rather than an exact ordering.

supporting_facts.claim: Under the zero-mint hypothesis the result is an exact equality, not just an inequality: supply(Ls n) + sumOver (fun i => burned(trace i)) (range n) = supply(Ls 0). Total supply decreases by exactly the total burned amount and by nothing else.
supporting_facts.check: Over a zero-mint run, sum every burned amount recorded across all n steps and compare against the exact difference between initial and final total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: final_supply + total_burned == initial_supply, exact integer equality with no rounding, truncation, or residual.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The identity fails by any nonzero amount, or supply is reduced/increased through a path that emits no burn/mint event and therefore does not appear in the sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Unconditionally (no zero-mint hypothesis needed) the chain is balanced: supply(Ls n) + sumOver burned (range n) = supply(Ls 0) + sumOver minted (range n). Every unit of supply growth is exactly matched by recorded minted amounts.
supporting_facts.check: For an arbitrary run including nonzero rewards/issuance/withdrawal credits, recompute both sides of the conservation identity from the recorded event traces and the ledger supplies.
supporting_facts.expected: final_supply + total_burned == initial_supply + total_minted, exactly, for every run and every n.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Supply changes that are not reflected by a corresponding recorded mint or burn amount, i.e. any implicit credit or debit path that bypasses the accounting trace.

supporting_facts.claim: The single-step balanced field of Recorded is the atomic form of FACT-3: for each step, supply_after + burned(step trace) = supply_before + minted(step trace). The chain identity is only sound if it holds at every individual transition.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument or recompute the identity at each of the n steps individually rather than only on the run endpoints.
supporting_facts.expected: The identity holds at every step index i < n, not merely in aggregate.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A step where the identity fails while endpoint totals coincidentally reconcile (compensating errors across steps).

supporting_facts.claim: minted(trace) = 0 follows only when EVERY mint event in that trace has amount 0 (equivalently, every event's mintAmount is 0). The obligation is universally quantified over events, so it is the amount field of each individual mint that must be constrained — this is exactly where a missing bounds check on a supply-increasing amount breaks the invariant.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate every code path that emits a supply-increasing event (block reward, issuance, withdrawal credit) and confirm each validates/bounds the amount before it is applied to the ledger, with no path admitting an attacker- or input-controlled unchecked value.
supporting_facts.expected: Every mint-amount producing path is bounds-checked at its source; the per-step minted total is 0 exactly when all such paths contribute 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any supply-increasing path whose amount is derived from remotely supplied data (e.g. a message or transaction) without an explicit bounds/range validation, or where validation is applied to an aggregate total but not to each contributing amount.

supporting_facts.claim: The aggregated accounting for a chain of n steps equals the sum over the per-step values: chain(fs,n).mint = sumOver (fun i => mint i) (range n) and chain(fs,n).burn = sumOver (fun i => burn i) (range n). Aggregation neither drops nor double counts a step.
supporting_facts.check: Compare any running/aggregate mint and burn accumulators against an independent recomputation summing the per-step recorded amounts over the full index range.
supporting_facts.expected: Aggregate mint total and aggregate burn total each equal the sum of their per-step values over [0, n).
supporting_facts.flag_if: An aggregate accumulator that skips a step, counts a step twice, resets mid-run, or is updated on a path that diverges from the recorded per-step amounts.

supporting_facts.claim: supply is defined as sumOver bal live, and the Ledger invariants live_distinct and bal_live make this a faithful total: no account is counted twice, and no account holding a nonzero balance is excluded from the sum.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the total-supply computation iterates a duplicate-free account set and that no account with a nonzero balance can be absent from it (including accounts touched only by withdrawal processing).
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply equals the sum of balances over a distinct account set covering every nonzero-balance account.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Duplicate entries in the enumerated account set, or a nonzero-balance account omitted from it — either makes the supply comparisons in FACT-1/FACT-2 unsound even when the event accounting is correct.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the bounds check on supply-increasing amounts is enforced on every step index in the audited range, not just the first, the last, or a sampled subset; the root hypothesis quantifies over all i < n and membership in range n implies i < n (lt_of_mem_range).
derived_obligations.expected: Validation is unconditional per step; no fast path, cached path, or index-dependent branch skips it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A branch that bypasses amount validation for some indices, epochs, or repeated steps.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm that a run in which all mint amounts are zero accumulates a total minted of exactly zero across the whole range, so the conservation identity collapses to the exact form in FACT-2.
derived_obligations.expected: total_minted == 0 exactly, and final_supply + total_burned == initial_supply.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero residual total minted appears despite all recorded mint amounts being zero (indicating a supply increase outside the recorded events).

derived_obligations.check: Confirm every supply-increasing operation in the audited surface (block reward, issuance, process_withdrawal credit) records a mint event with the applied amount into the step's trace, so that the hypothesis 'all mint amounts are zero' genuinely implies 'no supply was created'.
derived_obligations.expected: No supply-increasing code path can apply a credit without emitting a corresponding recorded mint amount.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A credit applied directly to a balance without a recorded event — this makes the proved invariant vacuously satisfiable while supply still grows.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the exact-arithmetic assumption: amounts and supply are non-negative integers with no wrap, saturation, or truncation, since the invariant is stated over Nat and a missing bounds check that overflows a fixed-width accumulator would break the equalities in FACT-2/FACT-3 while leaving the comparison in FACT-1 superficially satisfied.
derived_obligations.expected: All mint/burn/supply arithmetic is exact and overflow-safe over the full admissible amount range.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An unbounded input amount can wrap or saturate any supply, mint, or burn accumulator.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem concludes ¬(supply(Ls 0) < supply(Ls n)) from the single obligation h: every mint event amount in every step trace with i < n is 0. The proof routes h through minted_eq_zero_of_mint_events_zero [L002] (itself from minted_eq_zero_of_no_mint [L005]) to obtain minted(trace i) = 0 per step, then applies chain_not_lt_supply_of_no_total_minted [L001]. That lemma rests on the exact conservation result chain_supply_exact_of_no_mint [L004] — supply(n) + total burned = supply(0) — which is stronger than the final inequality and is preserved here as FACT-2. [L004] in turn comes from the unconditional chain balance [L006]/[L010] (FACT-3), lifted from the per-step balanced field of Recorded (FACT-4) and the aggregation lemmas [L011]/[L012] (FACT-6). not_lt_iff_le [L003] converts the negated strict inequality into the ordering supply(n) <= supply(0), retained in FACT-1. The supply function's faithfulness (distinct live list, nonzero balances live) is retained as FACT-7 because the ordering and equality facts are only meaningful if supply is computed without duplication or omission. The missing_bounds_check class attaches at FACT-5/OBS-1: the obligation is a universal constraint on each individual mint amount, so an unchecked, remotely influenceable amount on any supply-increasing path at any index defeats the guarantee at chain scale.

omitted_facts.reason: sumOver_congr_mem is a generic congruence for folds over a list under pointwise equality on members; it carries no implementation-visible protocol content beyond the aggregation correctness already covered by FACT-6.

sumOver_zero states that folding the constant-zero function over a list yields 0 — pure arithmetic plumbing whose implementation-facing consequence (total minted is exactly zero under the zero-mint hypothesis) is captured by OBS-2.

lt_of_mem_range is a range-membership-to-inequality bridge with no standalone protocol meaning; its audit-relevant content, that the obligation must hold at every index in the full range, is carried by OBS-1.

properties.label: evm
properties.text: Reject any balance-decreasing transfer unless v <= bal(s), and require both s and d to be live accounts; otherwise the reported burn silently truncates to min(v, bal(s)) and total supply inflates by exactly v - bal(s).
properties.assertion: s,d in live; require v<=bal[s]; then burn==v && supply'==supply; else burn==min(v,bal[s])<v && supply'==supply+(v-bal[s])

audit_packet.guarantee: A single precondition v <= bal(s), checked before the balance-decreasing write, is exactly equivalent to BOTH (a) the reported fee/burn amount equalling the requested amount v and (b) total supply being conserved across the paired debit/credit. If that one bounds check is missing or checked after the write, both properties fail simultaneously and by an exactly quantified amount.
preconditions: Root obligation hs: the source account s is a member of the live account list (s in L.live) at the time of the debit.
Root obligation hd: the destination account d is a member of the live account list (d in L.live) at the time of the credit, evaluated against the ledger state that already reflects the debit.
The live account list contains no duplicate entries (Ledger.live_distinct / Distinct L.live); the supply summation is defined as sumOver bal over that list.
Balances are non-negative naturals, so subtraction saturates at 0 rather than going negative or wrapping.

supporting_facts.claim: The two leaks share one guard: burn-report accuracy holds if and only if v <= bal(s), and supply conservation holds if and only if v <= bal(s). These are iff (both directions), not one-way implications.
supporting_facts.check: Locate the single bounds check governing the debit path and confirm one condition equivalent to v <= bal(s) gates both the fee/burn accounting and the balance write.
supporting_facts.expected: One guard, evaluated before any call to state.set_account_balance on the source, controls both outcomes; when it holds both properties hold, and when it is absent both properties are violable.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The bounds check is absent, is applied only to the accounting/reporting path while the balance write proceeds, is applied only to the balance write while the reported burn is computed independently, or is evaluated after the source balance has already been mutated.

supporting_facts.claim: The recorded burn is exactly min(v, bal(s)): it is always <= bal(s) (L003), and it equals the requested v exactly when v <= bal(s) (L004). Preserve the exact equality burn = min(v, bal(s)) — do not weaken to 'burn is nonzero' or 'burn succeeded'.
supporting_facts.check: Compare the burn/fee amount recorded or emitted by the implementation against the requested amount v for an under-funded source (v > bal(s)).
supporting_facts.expected: With v <= bal(s): recorded burn == v exactly. With v > bal(s): the operation is rejected before any accounting is recorded.
supporting_facts.flag_if: For v > bal(s) the operation proceeds and records a burn of min(v, bal(s)) (i.e. bal(s)) while reporting or being treated downstream as if the full v were burned — a silent truncation that under-reports the burn by exactly v - bal(s).

supporting_facts.claim: Quantified failure: an unguarded debit-then-credit yields supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)). The shortfall is not merely 'supply may change' — it is minted out of nothing, exactly equal to the amount by which the source was overdrawn.
supporting_facts.check: With v > bal(s), sum all live balances before and after the paired debit/credit and take the difference.
supporting_facts.expected: Unreachable: the guard must reject the operation before the debit, so no such state transition exists.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Post-state supply exceeds pre-state supply by v - bal(s); equivalently, the source is saturated to 0 while the destination is credited the full v. Remotely reachable via a single transaction, this is unbounded fund-integrity inflation.

supporting_facts.claim: Conservation is exact and two-directional: with v <= bal(s) the post-transfer supply equals the pre-transfer supply exactly (L008); and observing supply' = supply forces v <= bal(s) (via L005/L009/L014, since v - bal(s) = 0 iff v <= bal(s)). Preserve the exact equality, not 'supply is approximately preserved'.
supporting_facts.check: For a guarded transfer with v <= bal(s), verify the total over all live accounts is bit-for-bit unchanged, including the boundary cases v = 0, v = bal(s), and s = d.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after == supply_before exactly for every accepted transfer.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any accepted transfer changes total supply, or the implementation relies on a supply-equality check as its only safety net instead of enforcing the v <= bal(s) precondition up front.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-write accounting: crediting d raises supply by exactly v (L015), debiting s lowers it by exactly min(v, bal(s)) (L016), and each single-account write shifts supply by exactly (new value - old value) (L020, L021). Both writes carry a membership obligation on the account being written.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm each state.set_account_balance call targets an account established as live (present in the account set) and that no compensating or duplicate write is issued for the same account in the same operation.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one debit write for s and one credit write for d, each on a live account; the credit for d is computed from the post-debit balance of d.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A write targets an account not established as live, the destination credit is computed from a stale pre-debit balance of d (mis-handling the s == d case), or an extra/duplicated write shifts supply outside the accounted amounts.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply summation is only well-behaved when the account list is duplicate-free (Distinct) and the updated account is a member: updating a non-member leaves the sum unchanged (L024), so a write to an unlisted account adds value invisible to the supply total.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the account set enforces uniqueness and that both s and d are resolved to entries in that set before either write.
supporting_facts.expected: Accounts are uniquely keyed; both root obligations (s live, d live) are discharged before any mutation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can appear twice in the enumerated set, or a balance can be written for an account absent from the set used to compute total supply — either breaks the conservation accounting independently of the bounds check.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the bounds check v <= bal(s) is evaluated on the source balance read from the current state and strictly precedes the first state.balance mutation on the debit path.
derived_obligations.expected: Guard evaluated pre-write; on failure the whole operation is rejected with no partial state change and no burn recorded.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Guard is missing, uses saturating/clamping subtraction in place of an explicit check, or runs after the source balance has been written.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the reported/emitted burn value is the requested v itself and not a clamped min(v, bal(s)).
derived_obligations.expected: burn == v for every accepted operation; no code path emits a clamped burn.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path computes the burn as min(v, balance) or as balance-after-saturation and reports it as the requested amount.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm both root membership obligations are discharged: s is live before the debit and d is live at the point of the credit.
derived_obligations.expected: Both accounts resolved as live members of the account set before their respective writes.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Either account is written without a liveness/membership check, or d's liveness is checked against the pre-debit state only.

derived_obligations.check: Sum all live balances before and after an accepted transfer, including boundary values v = 0, v = bal(s), and s = d.
derived_obligations.expected: Totals are exactly equal in every accepted case.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any accepted transfer changes the total, most notably the self-transfer case where a stale destination balance is used.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem (ROOT) is the conjunction of L001 and L002. L001 unfolds Accounting.ofSetBalSub, whose burn field is min(v, bal(s)); L003 gives min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s) always, and L004 gives min(v, bal(s)) = v exactly when v <= bal(s) — so 'reported burn == requested v' is equivalent to the bounds check. L002 is proved from the general supply account: L020/L021 (with L022/L024 supplying the duplicate-free summation lemma) show a single account write shifts supply by exactly the delta; specialising gives L015 (credit raises supply by v) and L016 (debit lowers it by min(v, bal(s))). Composing them yields L011 and, with the arithmetic identity L013, the shortfall equation L007: supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)). Since natural subtraction gives v - bal(s) = 0 exactly when v <= bal(s) (L014 forward, L005/L009 backward), supply' = supply is likewise equivalent to the bounds check (L008 for the guarded direction). Both halves therefore hinge on the same single precondition, and its absence simultaneously under-reports the burn by v - bal(s) and inflates supply by v - bal(s).

omitted_facts.reason: Pure arithmetic: left cancellation of natural addition. No implementation-visible obligation.
Pure arithmetic: right cancellation of natural addition, used only to rearrange the supply equations. No implementation-visible obligation.
Commutativity of min — a lattice bookkeeping step; the security-relevant content (burn = min(v, bal(s)), burn <= bal(s)) is preserved in FACT-2.
Greatest-lower-bound property of min, used only to prove min_comm. No independent security content.
min(a,b) <= a, a generic lattice bound used inside min_comm; the operative bound min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s) is kept as L003 in FACT-2.
Symmetric counterpart of min_eq_left (L004), which is already carried in FACT-2; adds no distinct implementation obligation.
List eliminator: nothing is a member of the empty list. Internal induction base case for the summation lemma.
List eliminator for cons-membership. Internal induction machinery for the summation lemma; the resulting requirement (membership plus distinctness) is carried in FACT-6.
