properties.label: evm
properties.text: Verify every balance-writing state transition preserves supply(i+1)+burned(i)=supply(i)+minted(i), and that any account balance reaching threshold W (the U256 wrap point) is bounded by supply(0)+cumulative minted, so no unchecked write creates value.
properties.assertion: forall i<=n,a: bal_i(a) <= supply_i <= supply_0 + sum(ms,range n) given supply_{i+1}+bs_i == supply_i+ms_i; W<=bal_i(a) => W<=supply_0+sum(ms,range n)

audit_packet.guarantee: No account balance can reach a threshold W (in particular the U256 representation boundary) unless the initial supply plus all issuance accounted over the transition window already reaches W. Equivalently: a balance overflow is impossible without a matching, accounted mint. This holds only while every state transition maintains the per-step accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i); a balance write that bypasses that identity (a missing bounds/accounting check on set_account_balance) voids the guarantee entirely.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] (h): for EVERY transition index i, the accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i) holds — no transition may write a balance outside this identity, including transitions that only touch a single account.

ROOT obligation [2] (hin): the inspected state index i lies at or before the horizon n over which issuance is summed (i <= n) — the balance being bounded must be from a state inside the accounted window, not from a state whose transitions were never accounted for.

ROOT obligation [3] (hover): the threshold W is one actually attained by the account balance at state i (W <= bal_i(a)); the audit must instantiate W at the representation width boundary (the U256 wrap point) for the overflow reading to apply.

Ledger well-formedness: the live-account list is duplicate-free (Distinct) and every account with a nonzero balance is present in it — otherwise the supply sum omits or double-counts balances and both bounds below collapse.

supporting_facts.claim: For any state index i <= n and any account a, any threshold W attained by that account's balance is also attained by supply(0) + total issuance over the window: W <= bal_i(a) implies W <= supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). So reaching the U256 boundary requires that much accounted issuance.
supporting_facts.check: Instantiate W at the U256 representation boundary and confirm the implementation cannot produce a stored balance at or above it without the summed issuance over the same window reaching it. Concretely: identify every path that writes an account balance and confirm none can raise a balance without a corresponding accounted issuance/transfer-source decrement.
supporting_facts.expected: Every balance-increasing write is paired with either an accounted issuance term or an equal decrement elsewhere, so a balance at the U256 boundary is unreachable unless supply(0) + cumulative issuance already reaches it.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any code path can set or increase a stored balance to a value not covered by supply(0) + accounted issuance — e.g. an unchecked or unbounded write, an addition performed without a width/bounds check before storing, or an increase whose issuance is never recorded in the accounting term.

supporting_facts.claim: Chain bound (stronger than the final consequence, and stated as an ordering on the balance itself): for i <= n, bal_i(a) <= supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). Every single account's balance at every accounted state is bounded by initial supply plus cumulative issuance — not merely 'nonzero mint occurred'.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the ordering directly as a state-consistency check: for the account under audit at any accounted state, its stored balance is <= supply(0) + cumulative accounted issuance up to the window horizon. Exercise it against maximal-balance and long-chain scenarios, not only single-step ones.
supporting_facts.expected: The ordering holds at every accounted state index, for every account, with no dependence on how many transitions have occurred.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A stored balance exceeds supply(0) + cumulative accounted issuance at any accounted state, or the bound is only checked at a single state / a single transition rather than for all i <= n.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-state containment: for any single ledger state L and account a, bal(a) <= supply(L), because a is a member of the duplicate-free live list and a summand never exceeds its sum. This is a bound, not a nonzero property: one account can never hold more than the whole supply of its own state.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the total-supply quantity is computed as the sum of the balances of a duplicate-free live-account list, and that every account carrying a nonzero balance appears in that list. Then assert bal(a) <= supply for each account of the state under audit.
supporting_facts.expected: Every account balance is <= the state's total supply; the live list contains no duplicates and omits no nonzero-balance account.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account's balance exceeds its state's total supply; the live/account set can contain the same account twice (double counting inflates supply and hides an over-large balance); or a nonzero balance can exist for an account absent from the accounted set (undercounted supply, silently unbounded balance).

supporting_facts.claim: Exact accumulated conservation (equality, not an inequality): supply(n) + sumOver(burned, range n) = supply(0) + sumOver(minted, range n). Over any window, total supply plus everything burned equals the starting supply plus everything minted — value is neither created nor destroyed outside the issuance/burn terms.
supporting_facts.check: Independently recompute both sides over a window of transitions and compare for exact equality, using the recomputed supply (sum over live balances) rather than a cached or incrementally-maintained counter.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact equality of the two sides at every window horizon; recomputed supply agrees with any incrementally maintained supply value.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sides differ by any amount, or the equality is only enforced as an inequality / only approximately; a balance write updates an account without updating the corresponding issuance or burn term; or a wrap-around in the balance representation lets the left side silently decrease while nothing is recorded as burned.

supporting_facts.claim: Monotonicity of the accounted issuance total: for i <= n, sumOver(f, range i) <= sumOver(f, range n); a per-step nondecreasing quantity is nondecreasing across the whole window. The cumulative issuance bound can only grow with the horizon, so a bound established at a later horizon still covers all earlier states.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the cumulative issuance accumulator is non-negative per step and never decreases as more transitions are accounted, and that extending the audited window cannot lower the bound used in FACT-1/FACT-2.
supporting_facts.expected: Cumulative issuance is monotonically nondecreasing in the window horizon; per-step issuance terms are non-negative.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The cumulative issuance accumulator can decrease when extending the window (negative or wrapped issuance term, subtraction folded into the mint term), which would make the bound in FACT-1/FACT-2 unsound for earlier states.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate every code path that writes an account balance (including the direct state-balance setter on the code surface) and confirm each one is covered by the per-step accounting identity supply(i+1) + burned(i) = supply(i) + minted(i) — i.e. each write either moves value between accounted accounts or is recorded as issuance/burn.
derived_obligations.expected: No balance-writing path exists that is outside the accounting identity; the identity is re-checkable at every transition index i, not just at chosen checkpoints.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any balance-writing path bypasses the accounting identity, or the identity is enforced only for some transition kinds — this is the direct realization of the missing-bounds-check class: an unaccounted write is exactly what lets a balance grow without issuance.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the state whose balances are being bounded is inside the accounted window (i <= n): the issuance total used as the bound must be summed over a horizon that reaches at least as far as the state being inspected.
derived_obligations.expected: Every inspected state index is at or before the horizon over which issuance is accumulated; no state's balances are validated against an issuance total that stops earlier.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Balances from a state beyond the accounted horizon are checked against a stale/earlier issuance total, or the window boundary is chosen so that some transitions contributing balance increases fall outside the sum.

derived_obligations.check: Instantiate the threshold W at the balance representation's width boundary (the U256 wrap point) and confirm the arithmetic that produces a balance performs its bounds/width check BEFORE the value is stored, so an attained value at or above W is impossible rather than silently wrapped.
derived_obligations.expected: Any addition that would carry a balance to or past the representation boundary is rejected or trapped before the store; the stored value never wraps.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Balance arithmetic wraps, truncates, or saturates silently instead of being rejected — a wrap makes the attained value invisible to the conservation identity, breaking FACT-4 while presenting a plausible-looking state.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the account set used to compute total supply is duplicate-free and that no account can hold a nonzero balance while absent from it, across account creation, deletion, and balance-zeroing paths.
derived_obligations.expected: Duplicate-free accounted set; nonzero balance implies membership in it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate entries are possible (inflating supply and masking an over-large balance), or an account can retain a nonzero balance after being removed from the accounted set (its value escapes the supply sum entirely).

audit_packet.derivation: The per-state containment bal(a) <= supply (FACT-3, from L002 via the membership bound L005 on the duplicate-free live list) says one account never exceeds its own state's supply. The accumulated conservation equality (FACT-4, L003) rewrites supply(n) + total burned as supply(0) + total minted, and monotonicity of the accumulated sums (FACT-5, L004/L006) lets a bound at horizon n cover every earlier index i <= n. Composing these gives the chain bound bal_i(a) <= supply(0) + total minted over the window (FACT-2, L001). Transitivity with the attained threshold hypothesis W <= bal_i(a) yields the root conclusion (FACT-1, ROOT): W <= supply(0) + total minted. Read contrapositively, a balance reaching the U256 boundary is only possible if supply(0) plus accounted issuance already reaches it — so an overflow implies an accounted mint of that magnitude. The security value therefore rests entirely on root obligation [1]: if any balance write escapes the per-step accounting identity (the missing-bounds-check class), the chain bound no longer applies and a balance can be driven to the representation boundary with no issuance recorded anywhere.

omitted_facts.reason: List-structure plumbing (range (n+1) = range n ++ [n]); it decomposes the index range for the inductive step and carries no implementation-observable security condition.

Arithmetic decomposition of a sum over a concatenated list (sumOver (l1 ++ l2) = sumOver l1 + sumOver l2); it is the mechanical basis of the monotonicity fact already reported as FACT-5 and adds no separate check.
Range-restricted variant of the step-monotonicity lemma used only to discharge L006; its security content is fully captured by FACT-5.
Internal accumulator-normalization lemma for the standard range construction (range.loop n acc = range.loop n [] ++ acc); pure library plumbing with no protocol meaning.

properties.label: opcodes
properties.text: Check the destroy phase: require the target account to be live, set its balance to exactly 0 before removing it from the live set, and verify supply_after + burned == supply_before with exactly one burn event charged to the target and zero mints.
properties.assertion: a in live_before && bal_after_zeroing(a)==0 && supply_after + burned == supply_before && minted==0 && trace==[burn(a, bal_before(a))]

audit_packet.guarantee: A destroy-phase step on a live account a (SELFDESTRUCT / state.destroy_account inside process_transaction) conserves total supply exactly: the post-state supply plus the burned amount equals the pre-state supply plus the minted amount, where the emitted trace is exactly one burn event of amount bal_before(a) attributed to a, and nothing is minted. Every client that implements the same zero-then-erase order over a duplicate-free live set must therefore compute an identical post-state supply and identical receipt/event content, leaving no room for consensus divergence over destroyed-account funds.
preconditions: Root obligation ha: the destroyed account a is a member of the live account set of the pre-state ledger M (a in M.live). A destroy applied to an account not in the live set is outside the proved statement and must be rejected or be a total no-op on supply and on emitted events.
Ledger structure invariant live_distinct: the live account list contains no duplicate entries (EthTotal.Distinct M.live). The supply accounting lemmas are only valid over a duplicate-free live set.
Ledger structure invariant bal_live: any account with a nonzero balance is a member of the live set (bal a != 0 -> a in live), so no balance is held outside the summed live set.
Balances and supply are non-negative unbounded integers (Nat): the checks below must be evaluated without wraparound or saturating arithmetic.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation across the destroy phase: supply(post-state) + burned(trace) = supply(pre-state) + minted(trace), and with the destroy trace this is the exact equality supply_after + bal_before(a) = supply_before (minted = 0). This is an equality, not an inequality or a 'supply does not increase' bound.
supporting_facts.check: Recompute the total supply as the sum of balances over all live accounts immediately before and immediately after a destroy step, and take the burned amount from the emitted burn event. Assert supply_after + burned == supply_before and burned == bal_before(a) exactly.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + burned == supply_before, burned == bal_before(a), minted == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: supply_after + burned != supply_before; or burned differs from the target's pre-destroy balance (partial burn, rounded burn, stale balance read after zeroing, or balance read from a different account); or any value is minted during the destroy phase.

supporting_facts.claim: The pre-removal zeroing is exact: after setting the target's balance to v, reading that same account's balance returns exactly v; with v = 0 the destroy guard establishes bal(a) = 0 in the intermediate state. The fact is an exact read-back equality, not merely 'the balance was cleared/is falsy'.
supporting_facts.check: In the intermediate state produced by the destroy phase, read the target account's balance back through the same accessor the supply computation uses and compare it to 0. Also confirm the write targets only account a and leaves every other account's balance byte-identical.
supporting_facts.expected: bal(a) == 0 in the intermediate state; balances of all accounts other than a are unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The read-back is nonzero, absent/undefined, or served from a different view than the one the supply sum uses; or the zeroing write also alters another account's balance.

supporting_facts.claim: Erasing an account from the live set changes the total supply by exactly zero, and this holds only under the hypothesis bal(a) = 0. Ordering is load-bearing: zero the balance first, then remove from the live set.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the implementation zeroes the target's balance before removing it from the live/account set, and that the removal step itself is supply-neutral: recompute the supply sum immediately before and immediately after the removal.
supporting_facts.expected: supply(after removal) == supply(before removal), with the removed account's balance already 0 at the moment of removal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account is removed from the live set while still holding a nonzero balance (removal-before-zeroing, or an unguarded removal path), which silently destroys value without a matching burn event; or the removal step changes the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Balance update accounting is exact over the live set: supply(setBal a v) + bal_before(a) = supply_before + v, valid because a occurs in the duplicate-free live set; and an update aimed at an account not in the live set leaves the summed supply unchanged.
supporting_facts.check: For the destroy's zeroing write (v = 0), assert supply(after zeroing) + bal_before(a) == supply_before. Independently assert the live/account set contains no duplicate entry for the target address.
supporting_facts.expected: supply(after zeroing) + bal_before(a) == supply_before; the target address occurs at most once in the live set.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The equality fails; or the target address appears more than once in the enumerated live set (double-counted or double-erased balance); or a destroy of an address absent from the live set alters the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Burn-site confinement: every burn event in the emitted destroy trace has its burn site equal to the destroyed account a — the burn set is the singleton {a}. Value may only be debited from the account being destroyed.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the events/receipt entries emitted by the destroy phase and assert that every event carrying a burn site names exactly the destroyed address a.
supporting_facts.expected: Every burn-site value in the destroy trace equals a; the burn set is exactly {a}.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A burn is attributed to any address other than the destroyed account (beneficiary, caller, coinbase, or an unrelated account), or a burn event carries a missing/placeholder site.

supporting_facts.claim: Mint-site confinement against the empty set: the destroy phase's mint set is empty, so the trace contains no event with a mint site — nothing is created during the destroy phase, and minted(trace) = 0.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the destroy phase emits zero events carrying a mint site and that the minted total over the destroy trace is 0.
supporting_facts.expected: No mint-site event in the destroy trace; minted == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any credit/mint event is emitted by the destroy phase (e.g. crediting the destroyed balance to a beneficiary as newly created value rather than as a transfer outside this proved step), or minted != 0.

supporting_facts.claim: The destroy trace is the exact singleton [burn(a, bal_before(a))]: any event that is a member of the trace is that one burn event, and there is no membership in an empty trace. The shape and multiplicity of emitted events are pinned, not merely bounded.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the destroy phase emits exactly one event, whose kind is burn, whose site is a, and whose amount equals bal_before(a). Assert no additional events (duplicate burns, retries, zero-amount fillers) accompany it.
supporting_facts.expected: len(destroy events) == 1 and that event == burn(a, bal_before(a)).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Zero events emitted for a destroy that changed supply; more than one event emitted; or the single event's kind, site, or amount deviates from burn(a, bal_before(a)) — any of which makes receipts client-dependent and forks the chain.

derived_obligations.check: Add a differential/consistency check around the destroy phase in process_transaction: snapshot the summed supply over live accounts before and after, and compare against the burned/minted totals derived from the emitted receipt events using unbounded arithmetic.
derived_obligations.expected: supply_after + burned == supply_before + minted, with minted == 0 and burned == bal_before(a).
derived_obligations.flag_if: The identity fails for any destroy, or the arithmetic used can wrap/saturate so the identity holds only modulo a word size.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm every code path reaching state.destroy_account first establishes that the target account is present in the live account set (the ha obligation).
derived_obligations.expected: Destroy is only applied to an account present in the live set; a destroy targeting an absent account is rejected or is a total no-op on supply and on emitted events.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A destroy path proceeds on an absent account and still emits a burn event or mutates the supply sum, or derives the burned amount from a default/zero balance for an account that in fact holds value.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the destroy phase's step order in code: the target's balance is written to 0, that zero is observable through the accessor used by the supply computation, and only then is the account removed from the live set.
derived_obligations.expected: Zero-then-erase ordering on every destroy path, with the removal guarded by the observed bal(a) == 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path removes the account first (or removes it without checking the zero guard), or the zeroing write and the removal read different state views so the guard is checked against a stale balance.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the live/account set enumerated by the supply computation contains no duplicate address entries, before and after the destroy.
derived_obligations.expected: The live set is duplicate-free; the destroyed address occurs zero times after the destroy.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The target address appears twice in the live set (its balance is double-counted in supply, or only one copy is erased leaving a resurrected live entry), or the address is still present in the live set after the destroy.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the receipt/event log emitted by the destroy phase against the exact expected singleton, field by field: one burn event, site == destroyed address, amount == pre-destroy balance, zero mint events.
derived_obligations.expected: Exactly one event equal to burn(a, bal_before(a)); no mint-site events.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Event count, kind, site, or amount deviates in any way, since receipts feed the receipts root and any deviation is remotely triggerable by a single transaction and forks the network.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the destroy touches no account other than a: balances of all other live accounts and the membership of all other addresses in the live set are unchanged across the destroy phase.
derived_obligations.expected: Only the target's balance and its live-set membership change.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any other account's balance changes or any other address enters/leaves the live set during the destroy phase.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is proved as a pair. The supply conjunct comes from acc_destroy (L002), which is supply_destroy (L005) restated with burned/minted evaluated on the singleton trace: burned([burn a v]) = v and minted([burn a v]) = 0. supply_destroy composes three exact equalities: the destroy guard (L001, from setBal_bal_self L004 / setBalOfPoint_bal_self L009) proving the target's balance reads back as exactly 0 after zeroing; supply_eraseLive (L010, from sumOver_eraseOne_of_zero L013 / L017) proving that removing a zero-balance account leaves the summed supply unchanged — which is exactly why the zero-then-erase order is load-bearing; and supply_setBal_zero (L011, the v = 0 case of supply_setBal L014, itself from sumOver_update L018 / L019, which requires the live list to be duplicate-free and to contain the target, with L020 covering the not-in-list case). The confinement conjunct comes from SiteConfined.burn (L003): forall_mem_singleton (L006, via eqOfMemSingleton L012, memConsElim L015, notMemNil L016) reduces the obligation to the single emitted event; no_site (L007) discharges the mint side vacuously because a burn event has no mint site, giving an empty mint set; site_singleton (L008) pins the burn side to the singleton {a}. So the packet's checks are: the root precondition (OBS-2), the structural invariants distinctness and bal_live (OBS-4), the exact zeroing and its ordering before erasure (OBS-3), the exact conservation identity (OBS-1), and the exact event shape and site confinement (OBS-5), with non-interference on other accounts (OBS-6). Weakening any equality to a bound — e.g. checking only that supply did not increase, or that the balance is 'cleared' rather than exactly 0, or that 'a burn was emitted' rather than exactly one burn of the exact pre-destroy amount at site a — would admit a client-dependent post-state and receipts root, which is a remotely reachable, single-transaction consensus divergence with fund-integrity impact.

  Not (List.instMembership.mem l a) → Eq (EthTotal.sumOver (fun b => ite (Eq b a) v (f b)) l) (EthTotal.sumOver f l)

properties.label: gas
properties.text: Verify P=R+(T+B)<=sender balance before charging; route refund R, tip T and burn B through the escrow; check escrow returns to its initial balance, supply drops by exactly B, no mint occurs, and the live set is unchanged.
properties.assertion: R+(T+B)=P & P<=bal0(sender) & escrow!=sender,coinbase & bal'(escrow)=bal0(escrow) & supply'+burned=supply0 & minted=0 & live'=live2

audit_packet.guarantee: A gas settlement that debits P from the sender into an escrow and then pays out refund R, priority tip T and base-fee burn B ends with: total supply plus cumulative burned equal to the initial supply plus cumulative minted (exact conservation), cumulative burned increased by exactly B, cumulative minted unchanged (and zero, since no mint site is authorized), final supply no greater than the initial supply, the escrow drained back to exactly its pre-transaction balance, and the live account set unchanged. Every deduction is guarded so that no subtraction can wrap or be silently truncated, which is what would otherwise inflate supply.
preconditions: escrow != sender (obligation hse): the escrow account is distinct from the payer
escrow != coinbase (obligation hec): the escrow account is distinct from the fee recipient
sender is a live/known account in the initial ledger L0 (obligation hs0)
escrow is a live/known account in the initial ledger L0 (obligation he0)
R + (T + B) = P (obligation hsplit): the refund, priority tip and base-fee burn sum EXACTLY to the amount P debited from the sender - no rounding, no leftover, no extra
P <= bal0(sender) (obligation hP): the sender can cover the full charge before any debit is performed
sender is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation hs2)
escrow is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation he2)
coinbase is live in the post-debit ledger L2 (obligation hc2) - the fee recipient must already exist in the accounted account set
bal2(escrow) = bal0(escrow) + P (obligation hesc): the escrow received exactly the full charge P, no more and no less

supply2 + burned(tau_e) = supply(L0 after debiting P from sender and crediting P to escrow) + minted(tau_e) (obligation hacce): the ledger reached by the debit phase is accounted-consistent with its event trace
SiteConfined [] [escrow] tau_e (obligation hconfe): in the trace so far, no event carries a mint site at all, and every burn site is the escrow

supporting_facts.claim: Exact global conservation is preserved across the whole settlement: final_supply + burned(tau) = initial_supply + minted(tau). Each intra-ledger transfer (sender->escrow of P, escrow->sender of R, escrow->coinbase of T) is supply-neutral, and the chain of accounted steps composes by transitivity.
supporting_facts.check: Sum every account balance before the transaction and after settlement. Compute delta_supply = supply_before - supply_after. Compare against (burn amount recorded in the trace) - (mint amount recorded in the trace).
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + total_burned == supply_before + total_minted holds exactly, with each of the three transfers individually leaving total supply unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any transfer step changes the summed balances, or the equality holds only approximately / only modulo a word size, or the settlement is accounted with a net that differs from burn minus mint.

supporting_facts.claim: The base-fee burn removes EXACTLY B from supply: burned(tau) = burned(tau_e) + B and the burn step is accounted as supply_after + B = supply_before + 0. This equality depends on the guard B <= escrow_balance at the moment of the burn; the underlying accounting lemma only yields min(B, escrow_balance), so an unguarded burn would record a burn of B while destroying less than B.
supporting_facts.check: At the burn step, record the escrow balance before the burn, the burn amount B, and the escrow balance after. Verify balance_after = balance_before - B with no truncation, and that the burn event amount equals the supply reduction.
supporting_facts.expected: escrow_balance_before >= B, escrow_balance_after == escrow_balance_before - B, and cumulative burned increases by exactly B.
supporting_facts.flag_if: B > escrow balance at the burn site; the balance clamps at zero or wraps; or the recorded burn amount (min(B, balance)) differs from the amount used in fee accounting.

supporting_facts.claim: No new ether is created anywhere in the settlement: minted(tau) = minted(tau_e), and confinement to an empty mint-site list forces minted(tau) = 0. Every event in the extended trace has no mint site, and the only burn site is the escrow.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate every balance-increasing effect produced by the settlement (refund credit, tip credit, escrow credit) and confirm each is matched by an equal decrement from another live account. Confirm no event in the trace is a mint, and every burn is attributed to the escrow account.
supporting_facts.expected: total minted over the whole settlement == 0; the trace's burn events all name the escrow as their source; the mint-site set is empty.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any credit lacks a matching debit; any event carries a mint site; a burn is attributed to an account other than the escrow; or a subtraction underflow manufactures a large balance that acts as an implicit mint.

supporting_facts.claim: Total supply is monotonically non-increasing across the settlement: final_supply <= initial_supply. Combined with the zero-mint fact this strengthens to final_supply + burned(tau) = initial_supply exactly.
supporting_facts.check: Compare the summed supply before and after settlement, and check the difference equals the total burned.
supporting_facts.expected: final_supply <= initial_supply, and initial_supply - final_supply == B (the base-fee burn for this transaction).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Supply after settlement exceeds supply before, or the drop differs from the recorded burn amount.

supporting_facts.claim: Every one of the three escrow deductions is provably covered, in order, with an exact residual: the escrow holds e0 + (R + (T + B)) after being funded, so R <= escrow balance; after paying R it holds exactly e0 + (T + B), so T <= escrow balance; after paying T it holds exactly e0 + B, so B <= escrow balance; after the burn it holds exactly e0. Each residual is an EXACT equality, not merely a non-negativity claim.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the escrow balance at four points: after funding, after the refund payout, after the tip payout, after the burn. Compare against e0+R+T+B, e0+T+B, e0+B, e0 respectively, where e0 is the escrow balance before the transaction.
supporting_facts.expected: The four observed balances match the four predicted values exactly, and each deduction amount is <= the balance immediately preceding it.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any observed escrow balance deviates from its predicted value; any deduction exceeds the current escrow balance; or the ordering of refund/tip/burn is changed so that a later step is no longer covered.

supporting_facts.claim: A transfer of v from source s to a DISTINCT destination d leaves the source at exactly bal(s) - v, and writing one account's balance does not perturb any other account's balance. The distinctness side conditions (escrow != sender for the refund, escrow != coinbase for the tip) are load-bearing: without them the credit would overwrite the debit and the source residual would be wrong.
supporting_facts.check: For the refund (escrow -> sender) and the tip (escrow -> coinbase), confirm the destination is not the escrow itself, and confirm that after each transfer the source balance is reduced by exactly the transferred amount while all uninvolved accounts are bit-identical.
supporting_facts.expected: source_after == source_before - v; destination_after == destination_before + v; all other balances unchanged; source != destination enforced.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A transaction where the sender or the coinbase equals the escrow account is processed without rejection or special handling; or a balance write clobbers a sibling account; or the source residual differs from bal - v.

supporting_facts.claim: The escrow is a pure conduit with zero residue: its final balance equals its pre-transaction balance exactly, bal_final(escrow) = bal_0(escrow).
supporting_facts.check: Compare the escrow balance before the transaction with its balance after settlement completes.
supporting_facts.expected: They are equal, for every transaction and for any starting escrow balance e0 including zero.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any dust, rounding remainder, or unpaid amount remains in (or is missing from) the escrow after settlement - that residue is an unaccounted claim on supply.

supporting_facts.claim: The set of live/accounted accounts after settlement equals the set after the debit phase: live_final = live_2. Settlement neither creates nor removes accounted accounts.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the live account set before and after the payout phase.
supporting_facts.expected: Identical sets, with no duplicates introduced.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account is added, dropped, or duplicated during payout - a duplicate makes the same balance counted twice in the supply sum.

supporting_facts.claim: Trace accounting is additive and confinement is closed under extension: burned(t1 ++ t2) = burned(t1) + burned(t2), minted(t1 ++ t2) = minted(t1) + minted(t2), and appending a site-confined segment preserves site confinement. Appending the base-fee burn event therefore adds exactly B to burned and 0 to minted.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that cumulative burn/mint counters are computed as a plain sum over all recorded events, and that appending this transaction's burn event to the prior trace preserves the mint-empty / burn-site-escrow confinement.
supporting_facts.expected: Counters are additive over trace concatenation; the extended trace is still confined to no mint sites and burn site = escrow.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Cumulative burn or mint is recomputed by overwrite rather than accumulation, events are dropped or reordered so a burn is lost or double-counted, or an appended event introduces an unconfined mint/burn site.

supporting_facts.claim: CRITICAL anti-underflow fact: without the coverage guard, a transfer of v from an account holding less than v does not fail - it raises total supply by exactly (v - bal(s)). The general accounting lemma is supply_after = supply_before + (v - bal(s)), which collapses to supply-neutral ONLY when v <= bal(s). Every guard in this packet (P <= bal0(sender), R/T/B <= escrow balance) exists to force that subtraction to zero.
supporting_facts.check: Attempt settlement paths where the charge exceeds the payer's balance and where a payout exceeds the escrow balance (e.g. R+T+B computed from an inflated gas limit or an oversized base fee). Observe whether the deficit is rejected or silently absorbed.
supporting_facts.expected: Every such path is rejected before any balance is written; no path exists in which a debit is applied to an account with insufficient balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A saturating/clamping subtraction, a wrapping unsigned subtraction, or a debit applied without a preceding balance check - any of these mints (v - balance) out of thin air at network scale and is remotely reachable by a single crafted transaction.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply sum is well-defined only over a DISTINCT account list, and updating one account's balance changes the sum by exactly (new - old) while leaving all non-matching entries untouched. Aliasing in the accounted account set breaks the conservation arithmetic itself.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the accounted account collection contains no duplicate entries, and that a balance update to account a changes the supply total by exactly the delta on a and nothing else.
supporting_facts.expected: No duplicate accounts; supply delta after a single write == new_balance - old_balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The same account appears twice in the accounted set (e.g. sender == coinbase == escrow collapsing to one entry) without being deduplicated, or a write to one account perturbs the recorded total by a different amount.

derived_obligations.check: Assert R + T + B == P as an exact integer identity before any state write, using arithmetic that cannot wrap.
derived_obligations.expected: The three payout components sum exactly to the amount debited from the sender.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The sum is computed with wrapping arithmetic, or refund/tip/burn are derived independently such that their sum can differ from the charged amount.

derived_obligations.check: Assert P <= sender balance before the debit, and reject the transaction otherwise.
derived_obligations.expected: No debit is written unless the sender fully covers P.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The debit is written first and checked later, or the check uses a clamped/wrapped comparison.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the escrow account is distinct from both the sender and the coinbase for the transaction being settled.
derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness holds; otherwise the settlement path is rejected or handled by a separately verified path.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A transaction whose coinbase or sender coincides with the escrow is processed by the ordinary path.

derived_obligations.check: Assert that sender, escrow and coinbase are all present in the accounted account set before any payout, and that the set contains no duplicates.
derived_obligations.expected: All three are live and the set is duplicate-free at every step.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A payout targets an account absent from the accounted set, or the set contains duplicates.

derived_obligations.check: At each of the three escrow deductions, assert amount <= current escrow balance BEFORE writing.
derived_obligations.expected: R, then T, then B are each individually covered by the escrow balance at that moment.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any deduction proceeds unchecked, or relies on the aggregate guard P <= sender balance instead of a per-step check.

derived_obligations.check: After settlement, assert escrow balance == its pre-transaction value and cumulative burned increased by exactly B with cumulative minted unchanged.
derived_obligations.expected: Zero escrow residue; burn delta == B; mint delta == 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Escrow retains or loses any amount, or the burn/mint deltas disagree with B/0.

derived_obligations.check: Recompute total supply after settlement and assert supply_after + total_burned == supply_before + total_minted and supply_after <= supply_before.
derived_obligations.expected: Exact conservation and monotone non-increase both hold.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Either relation fails for any transaction, including edge cases with zero refund, zero tip, zero burn, or a zero starting escrow balance.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes a ledger L0 in which the sender has been charged P and the escrow credited P (obligations hesc, hacce), with P split exactly as R + (T + B) (hsplit) and covered by the sender (hP), and all four participants live and pairwise distinct where required (hs0, he0, hs2, he2, hc2, hse, hec), and the prior trace confined to no mint sites and burn site = escrow (hconfe). It then constructs the three payout steps in order: escrow -> sender of R, escrow -> coinbase of T, and a burn of B from the escrow. The escrow-guard and escrow-after lemmas (L001, L003, backed by L013/L015) give the exact residual after each step - e0+(T+B), then e0+B, then e0 - which both proves the coverage precondition for the NEXT step and pins the escrow's final balance to its initial value. The source-residual lemmas (L002/L014/L004/L016/L026) supply the exact bal - v semantics of a transfer and require the distinctness side conditions. The accounting lemmas (L006/L018 for transfers, L007/L020/L029 for the burn) are each supply-neutral or supply-exact ONLY under their coverage hypotheses; the general form (L027/L035) shows the failure mode explicitly - an uncovered debit of v raises supply by v - bal(s), i.e. mints. Chaining the four accounted steps by transitivity (L005/L017) and rewriting the trace counters via the append laws (L008/L009) yields exact conservation, burned increased by exactly B, and minted unchanged; confinement is preserved by L010/L011, and confinement to an empty mint-site list forces minted = 0 (L033/L041/L050/L051/L053/L054/L055). That in turn upgrades conservation to final_supply <= initial_supply (L012/L025/L032). The audit therefore checks the guards (OBS-1..OBS-5) that make every subtraction exact, and then the three exact outcomes (OBS-6, OBS-7): escrow drained to its start balance, supply down by exactly B, nothing minted.

omitted_facts.reason: forall_mem_append: pure list-membership plumbing used to lift a predicate over concatenation; carries no implementation-observable content beyond FACT-9's additivity/closure claim.
forall_mem_singleton: list-membership plumbing for the single appended burn event; subsumed by FACT-9 and FACT-3.
memAppendElim: structural list-membership elimination, no security-relevant consequence of its own.
eqOfMemSingleton: structural list lemma (membership in a one-element list implies equality); infrastructure only.
memConsElim: structural list case-analysis helper; infrastructure only.
notMemNil: nothing is a member of the empty list; used only to discharge the empty mint-site case already captured in FACT-3.
add_left_cancel: arithmetic cancellation identity on naturals, no independent audit content.
le_min: lattice property of min on naturals; internal to the exact-burn arithmetic already captured in FACT-2.
min_le_right: lattice property of min on naturals; internal arithmetic.
min_le_left: lattice property of min on naturals; internal arithmetic.
min_eq_right: arithmetic identity for min under the reversed ordering; only reachable in the uncovered branch, whose security content is already stated as the anti-underflow warning in FACT-10.

properties.label: beacon-chain:withdrawal
properties.text: Verify process_withdrawal credits W only to an account already in the live set, raising total supply by exactly W with zero burn, leaving every other balance and the live set unchanged, and rejecting targets that are non-live or duplicated in the live set.
properties.assertion: w ∈ live_pre ∧ distinct(live) ∧ supply_post = supply_pre + W ∧ burned=0 ∧ minted=W ∧ ∀a≠w: bal_post a = bal_pre a ∧ live_post=live_pre

audit_packet.guarantee: Processing one withdrawal that credits amount W to account w is exactly supply-conserving and site-confined: the post-state total supply equals the pre-state total supply plus W, the emitted trace is a single mint of W at site w with burned total 0, the credit is confined to the single site w (no other account's balance and no other mint/burn site is affected), and the operation is only defined when w is already a member of the live account set.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hw: the withdrawal recipient w is a member of L.live (the live account set) BEFORE the balance write. The credit path must establish membership first; it must not create, resurrect, or implicitly insert an account entry as a side effect of crediting.

Ledger structural invariant live_distinct: the live account list contains no duplicate entries (EthTotal.Distinct L.live). Supply is defined as sumOver bal live, so a duplicated entry double-counts the credited balance.
Ledger structural invariant bal_live: any account with a non-zero balance is a member of live; no balance may be held outside the enumerated live set.

The state transition is exactly the point update L.setBal w (L.bal w + W) hw — the new balance is the pre-state balance of w plus W, and only the bal component changes (live and live_distinct are carried over unchanged by setBalOfPoint).
The event trace emitted for this operation is exactly the one-element list [Ev.mint w W] — one mint event, amount W, site w, and no burn event.

Modelling-fidelity precondition: amounts are ℕ in the proof (unbounded, no wraparound, no negative values). The implementation's balance and supply arithmetic must not truncate, saturate, or wrap for the credit L.bal w + W, otherwise the proved equality does not transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation, not merely a bound: (L.setBal w (L.bal w + W) hw).supply + burned [Ev.mint w W] = L.supply + minted [Ev.mint w W]; since burned [Ev.mint w W] = 0 and minted [Ev.mint w W] = W, the post-state total supply equals the pre-state total supply plus exactly W.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the withdrawal path to compute the total issued supply (the sum of balances over the whole live account set) immediately before and immediately after the credit, alongside the amount W recorded in the withdrawal and the amount attributed to issuance. Compare supply_post - supply_pre against W for exact equality, for W = 0, W = 1, a typical withdrawal amount, and the largest representable amount.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_post - supply_pre == W exactly, for every W including W = 0; the issuance/minted accounting for the operation equals W and the burned accounting equals 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: supply_post - supply_pre differs from W in any direction (credit applied twice, credit applied to a mirror/aggregate counter as well as the account, supply recomputed from a stale snapshot, rounding or unit conversion applied to W, or a wrap/saturation at the representable maximum). Any inequality here is a fund-integrity break in the issuance accounting reachable through ordinary withdrawal processing.

supporting_facts.claim: The point write REPLACES the target's contribution to supply rather than adding to it: (L.setBal a v ha).supply + L.bal a = L.supply + v. The proved +W delta therefore holds only because the written value is the pre-state balance plus W; writing an absolute value v computed from anything other than the current bal w changes the supply delta to v - bal w.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the value written to the account is derived from the account's current, freshly-read balance plus W, and that the total supply figure is derived from the same account set the write lands in. Exercise the case where the target account already has a non-zero balance, and the case where the balance is read before some other adjustment to the same account within the same operation.
supporting_facts.expected: written_balance == balance_read_immediately_before + W, and the resulting supply delta is v - bal_pre(w) == W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The written balance is an absolute value not anchored to the current balance, is computed from a stale or cached read of bal w, or the operation both adds W to the account and separately adds W to the aggregate supply figure. Either produces a supply delta that is not W while each individual field still looks plausible.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply delta is exact only under the distinctness hypothesis: sumOver (update f a v) l + f a = sumOver f l + v requires both a ∈ l and Distinct l. Duplicate entries for the target in the account set break the equality.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the live account set enumerated for supply accounting is duplicate-free and that the withdrawal target resolves to exactly one entry in it. Attempt a state in which the target identity appears more than once in the enumerated set (e.g. two entries that compare equal under the identity/equality relation used by the credit path but are distinguishable elsewhere) and observe the supply delta.
supporting_facts.expected: The account set carries no duplicate entries under the same equality relation the credit uses; exactly one entry is updated; supply delta remains W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Duplicate or aliasing entries can exist in the enumerated account set, or the equality relation used to locate the target differs from the one used to enforce distinctness (e.g. one path normalises the identifier and the other does not). Then a single withdrawal message multiplies its credited amount across duplicates — a remotely-reachable fund-integrity break.

supporting_facts.claim: No collateral mutation: updating an account not present in a list leaves that list's sum unchanged (sumOver (update f a v) l = sumOver f l when a ∉ l). Combined with the point update, only the target's balance contributes to the change.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the full pre- and post-state account map for a single withdrawal: enumerate every account whose balance changed and every change to the membership of the live set itself.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one balance changed, that of w, by exactly +W; the live set membership is byte-for-byte identical before and after (setBalOfPoint carries live and live_distinct through unchanged).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any account other than w has a changed balance, or the live set gains/loses/reorders entries as a side effect of the credit. Collateral writes to a neighbouring account (index/offset error, shared slot, iteration reuse) silently redistribute funds while the target's own balance still reads correctly.

supporting_facts.claim: Mint-site confinement: SiteConfined [w] [] [Ev.mint w W] — every event in the trace whose mintSite is Some d has d = w. The withdrawal may credit at exactly one site, the withdrawal's own recipient.
supporting_facts.check: Collect every issuance/mint event the operation emits and check each event's credited site against the recipient recorded in the withdrawal request itself. Include the case where the recipient identifier is supplied by the incoming message.
supporting_facts.expected: Every mint event emitted by the operation names w — the withdrawal's own recipient — as its site, and there is exactly one such event carrying amount W.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The operation emits a mint whose site is any account other than the withdrawal's recipient, emits more than one mint per withdrawal, or the site used to write the balance and the site recorded in the issuance event can diverge. A divergence lets a single message credit an account of the attacker's choosing while accounting attributes it elsewhere.

supporting_facts.claim: Burn-site emptiness: the burn site set is empty ([]), so no event in the withdrawal trace may have a burnSite of Some s, and burned [Ev.mint w W] = 0. The proof of the accounting equality relies on the burn total being exactly zero, not merely small.
supporting_facts.check: Assert that the withdrawal path emits zero burn events and contributes zero to any burned/destroyed accumulator, including on every early-exit, retry, or error branch of the operation.
supporting_facts.expected: burned contribution of the operation == 0 and no event carries a burn site.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The withdrawal path records any burn, debit, or destroyed amount — even a compensating one intended to 'balance the books'. A non-zero burn paired with the +W mint keeps the aggregate equality looking correct while destroying real balance held by whichever account is debited.

supporting_facts.claim: The whole result is conditioned on the root obligation hw : w ∈ L.live. The theorem says nothing about crediting an account that is not already live; outside that hypothesis neither the supply equality nor the confinement is established.
supporting_facts.check: Drive the withdrawal path with a recipient that is not a member of the live account set (never initialised, or removed) and observe the result. Confirm that membership is established before, not after or during, the balance write, and that the check uses the same account set that supply is summed over.
supporting_facts.expected: The operation fails closed — it rejects the withdrawal or errors — rather than silently writing a balance for a non-live account; supply accounting is left untouched on the rejecting path.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A non-live recipient is credited, the account is implicitly inserted into the live set by the credit, or membership is tested against a different set than the one supply is computed from. This is the unguarded-precondition case: it puts balance outside the enumerated set (violating bal_live) so that the total supply figure no longer accounts for issued funds.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the liveness/membership guard on the recipient is unconditional on every path into the credit — including any fast path, batch path, or replay/reprocessing path — and that it precedes the balance write.
derived_obligations.expected: Every reachable route into the balance write is dominated by a membership check against the live account set, with a fail-closed outcome on failure.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any route reaches the balance write without the membership check, or the check's failure is logged and ignored rather than aborting the operation.

derived_obligations.check: Establish and test the duplicate-freedom of the live account set as a maintained invariant: attempt to insert a recipient identity that already exists under the equality relation used by the credit path.
derived_obligations.expected: Insertion of an already-present identity is impossible or is rejected; the set remains duplicate-free under exactly the equality relation used to locate the credit target.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicates are representable, or two identifiers that the credit path treats as equal are treated as distinct by the enumeration used for supply.

derived_obligations.check: Run a differential invariant test around the withdrawal operation: recompute total supply by summing all live balances before and after, and compare the delta to the sum of amounts in the mint events emitted, minus the sum of amounts in any burn events emitted.
derived_obligations.expected: recomputed_supply_post + total_burned == recomputed_supply_pre + total_minted, holding exactly, with total_burned == 0 for the withdrawal path.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The recomputed identity fails, or supply is only ever read from a cached aggregate that is never cross-checked against the recomputed sum — a drifting aggregate hides every one of the failures above.

derived_obligations.check: Fuzz the credited amount W and the pre-state balance of w across the full representable range, including 0, 1, the maximum representable balance, and values whose sum exceeds the representable maximum of the balance and of the total-supply accumulator.
derived_obligations.expected: The +W delta holds exactly for all in-range values; any value that cannot be represented is rejected explicitly rather than wrapping, saturating, or truncating.
derived_obligations.flag_if: bal w + W wraps, saturates, or truncates, or the supply accumulator overflows while individual balances do not. The proof is over ℕ and offers no protection here; a wrap turns a large credit into an arbitrary supply change from a single message.

derived_obligations.check: Snapshot the complete account state (all balances plus live-set membership and ordering) before and after one withdrawal and assert the diff has exactly one entry.
derived_obligations.expected: The diff contains exactly the pair (w, +W); membership and the enumerated set itself are unchanged.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The diff contains any additional entry, or the live set changes as a side effect of the credit.

derived_obligations.check: Verify that the recipient identity used to write the balance is the same value, taken from the same read, as the recipient identity recorded in the emitted issuance event and as the identity used for the membership check — no separate re-derivation, re-parse, or re-normalisation between the three uses.
derived_obligations.expected: A single recipient value flows to the membership check, the balance write, and the event site.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The recipient is re-derived independently for any of the three uses, allowing the checked account, the credited account, and the accounted account to diverge for a crafted incoming message.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem process_withdrawal_effect is a conjunction. Its first component is the exact accounting equality supplied by L001 (Ledger.acc_setBal_add), which specialises L003 (supply_setBal_add: (setBal d (bal d + v)).supply = supply + v) to the case where the burn total is 0. L003 in turn rests on L008 (supply_setBal: (setBal a v).supply + bal a = supply + v — the write replaces the target's contribution) cancelled by L007/L010 to isolate the delta, and L008 rests on L011/L014 (sumOver_update), whose exactness holds only under the hypotheses a ∈ l and Distinct l. L015 supplies the complementary case: an update outside the list changes nothing, which is what pins the effect to the single target and rules out collateral movement. The second component is L002 (SiteConfined.mint), assembled from L005 (site_singleton: the only mint site of the singleton trace is the target) and L006 (no_site: the mint event has no burn site, so the burn-site obligation is vacuous), quantified over the trace by L004/L009. The root obligation hw : w ∈ L.live is the single must-establish hypothesis of the whole result and is carried into FACT-7 and OBS-1; the Ledger structure fields live_distinct and bal_live are carried into the preconditions and OBS-2, since L011's distinctness hypothesis is discharged from live_distinct rather than proved locally. The packet therefore preserves the equality form (supply_post = supply_pre + W) rather than a weaker 'supply does not decrease' or boolean success check, preserves the exact burn total of 0 rather than 'few burns', and preserves the membership conclusions of L005/L006 as site-identity checks rather than an unspecific 'events look right' check.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.forall_mem_singleton is pure quantifier plumbing — it discharges a ∀-over-a-singleton-list goal. Its security content is fully carried by FACT-5, which states the confinement conclusion it helps establish.

EthTotal.add_right_cancel is a ℕ arithmetic cancellation step used to isolate the supply delta from L008. It introduces no state, event, or membership condition an implementation could violate independently.

EthTotal.eqOfMemSingleton (membership in a singleton implies equality) is list plumbing supporting L004/L005; its audit-relevant consequence — the mint site must equal the withdrawal recipient — is stated directly in FACT-5.
EthTotal.add_left_cancel is a ℕ arithmetic cancellation lemma with no implementation-facing condition; the arithmetic exactness it supports is checked end-to-end by FACT-1 and OBS-4.
EthTotal.memConsElim is the cons-case eliminator for list membership, used to structure the induction in L009 and L014. It is a proof-structuring device, not a state condition.

EthTotal.notMemNil (nothing is a member of the empty list) closes the base case of the same inductions. Its only audit-visible consequence — a recipient absent from the account set has no entry to credit — is covered by FACT-7 and OBS-1.

properties.label: beacon-chain:withdrawal
properties.text: Verify that a withdrawal to a fresh recipient adds the account with zero starting balance, credits exactly W, raises total supply by exactly W with no burn, and emits one mint event sited only at that recipient.
properties.assertion: w∉live ⇒ bal(w)=0 ∧ supply'=supply+W ∧ burned=0 ∧ minted=W ∧ mintSites⊆{w} ∧ burnSites=∅ ∧ ∀a≠w: bal'(a)=bal(a)

audit_packet.guarantee: Processing a withdrawal of amount W to a recipient w that is not yet a live account creates the account at balance exactly 0, credits it exactly W, and increases total supply by exactly W (supply' + burned = supply + minted, with burned = 0 and minted = W). The single emitted event is a mint sited at w only, no burn site is used, and no other account's balance changes.
preconditions: Freshness (root obligation hw): w is NOT a member of the live account list before the withdrawal is applied; the create-account path is taken only under this negative-membership check.
Address equality is decidable (DecidableEq A): the identity of w is compared exactly, so 'fresh' and 'same account' are decided without collision or truncation of the address key.
Ledger well-formedness carried by the state: live is Distinct (no duplicate account entries) and bal_live holds (any address with nonzero balance is already live).
The withdrawal is applied as exactly the one-event trace [mint w W]: one issuance event, no accompanying burn event.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact conservation across the withdrawal: post-state supply + burned([mint w W]) = pre-state supply + minted([mint w W]). Because the trace holds a single mint, burned = 0 and minted = W, so supply increases by exactly W — an equality, not a bound.
supporting_facts.check: Recompute total supply (sum of all account balances) before and after processing the withdrawal, and independently total the issuance (minted) and burn amounts attributed to this withdrawal.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_after + burn_total == supply_before + mint_total, with burn_total == 0 and mint_total == W, hence supply_after - supply_before == W exactly.
supporting_facts.flag_if: supply_after - supply_before differs from W by any amount (including 1 wei/Gwei), or the equality only holds after rounding, saturation, or a separate reconciliation step.

supporting_facts.claim: Creating the live entry for a fresh w is supply-neutral: (L.addLive w hw).supply = L.supply, which holds precisely because a non-live address has balance exactly 0.
supporting_facts.check: Isolate the account-creation step from the credit step: snapshot total supply immediately after the account for w is created but before W is credited.
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply is bit-for-bit unchanged by account creation; the newly created account's balance reads exactly 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Account creation alone moves total supply, or the new account is initialized from stale/reused storage carrying a nonzero balance.

supporting_facts.claim: Setting the recipient's balance to bal(w) + W raises total supply by exactly W: supply(setBal w (bal w + W)) = supply + W, derived by cancelling the old balance from supply(setBal) + bal(w) = supply + v. The credit is an exact addition, never an overwrite that silently discards the prior balance.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the credit is computed as (current balance of w) + W and written back, and that the recorded supply delta equals W independent of what bal(w) was.
supporting_facts.expected: balance_after(w) == balance_before(w) + W and supply delta == W, for any prior balance value.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The recipient's balance is overwritten with W (dropping a prior balance), the credit wraps/saturates on overflow, or the supply delta is derived from balance_after rather than from W.

supporting_facts.claim: SiteConfined [w] [] [mint w W]: every mint event in the trace has its mint site equal to w and that site is a member of the permitted singleton mint set {w}. Issuance from this withdrawal is confined to the one intended recipient.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate every mint/issuance event emitted while processing this withdrawal and extract its destination site; compare against the withdrawal's declared recipient.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one mint event, whose destination is w; the set of mint destinations is a subset of {w}.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any mint event carries a destination other than w, more than one mint event is emitted for a single withdrawal, or a mint event is emitted with no recorded destination site.

supporting_facts.claim: The permitted burn-site set is empty and a mint event has no burn site (burnSite of a mint is none), so this withdrawal path is provably burn-free — it cannot debit any account as a side effect.
supporting_facts.check: Scan the events and state deltas produced by the withdrawal for any burn/debit attributed to any address.
supporting_facts.expected: Zero burn events; no account's balance decreases as part of processing this withdrawal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any burn/debit event appears, or any account balance decreases, while the withdrawal is applied.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply recomputation under a point balance update over a Distinct account list changes only the target's contribution: for every address other than w the summed balance term is unchanged (sumOver over a list not containing the target is invariant). Distinctness of the live list is what makes the single-entry accounting sound.
supporting_facts.check: Diff the full account-balance map before and after the withdrawal, and confirm the live/account index contains no duplicate entry for w.
supporting_facts.expected: Exactly one entry differs (w, by +W); the account list contains w exactly once after creation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any address other than w changes balance, or w appears twice in the account set so its balance is counted more than once in total supply.

supporting_facts.claim: Root-obligation consequence: because w is not live, its balance is exactly 0 before the withdrawal. The freshness guard is therefore load-bearing for the supply arithmetic, not a cosmetic precondition.
supporting_facts.check: At the create-account branch, assert the freshness predicate and the read-back balance of w.
supporting_facts.expected: The freshness check returns true and balance(w) reads exactly 0 at that point.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The create-account branch is reachable for an address already present in the account set, or is entered without reading/asserting a zero starting balance.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the code takes the create-account path only after a negative-membership test against the live account set, and that the test uses exact address identity.
derived_obligations.expected: Create-account is strictly guarded by 'w not already an account'; an existing account takes the plain-credit path instead.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Creation is unconditional, guarded by a proxy signal (e.g. a zero-balance heuristic alone), or uses a truncated/derived key that can alias two distinct addresses.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the account index preserves distinctness after insertion of w.
derived_obligations.expected: w appears exactly once; insertion cannot produce a duplicate entry.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Insertion can append a second entry for an address already present, breaking the distinctness premise the supply accounting relies on.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the exact supply/issuance bookkeeping delta for the withdrawal equals W, computed from W itself and cross-checked against a full re-sum of balances.
derived_obligations.expected: Recorded issuance delta == W == (re-summed supply after - re-summed supply before).
derived_obligations.flag_if: The bookkeeping counter and the re-summed balances disagree, allowing total supply to drift from the sum of accounts.

derived_obligations.check: Test the boundary cases W = 0 and a maximal W against the credit and supply update.
derived_obligations.expected: W = 0 is a no-op on supply; a maximal W either applies exactly or is rejected — never wraps or saturates.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Addition wraps, saturates, or is silently truncated so supply_after - supply_before != W.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the withdrawal emits its mint event and its state mutation atomically, so a failure between them cannot leave a credited balance with no recorded issuance (or the reverse).
derived_obligations.expected: Event trace and state delta commit together; a partial application is impossible.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The balance write and the issuance record can commit independently, letting the conservation equality hold in state but not in the trace.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is proved for a fresh recipient w (obligation hw: w not in live). Its first conjunct is the conservation equality, obtained by chaining acc_setBal_add [L001] with supply_addLive [L002]: creating the live entry is supply-neutral because a non-live address has balance exactly 0 [L005], and the subsequent point credit raises supply by exactly W [L004], which itself follows from supply_setBal [L010] by cancelling the old balance [L009] over a distinct-list point update [L013, L016, L017] where non-target entries are provably unchanged. The second conjunct is SiteConfined [w] [] [mint w W] [L003]: mint sites land in the singleton {w} [L007] and mints expose no burn site, so the empty burn set is respected [L008]. The auditor therefore checks four things jointly — the freshness guard, the zero starting balance it implies, the exact +W supply delta with zero burn, and the single mint confined to w — rather than the weak consequence that supply merely increased.

omitted_facts.reason: forall_mem_singleton is a quantifier-over-singleton plumbing lemma used to discharge the SiteConfined fields; its security content is already carried by FACT-4 (mint sites confined to {w}).
eqOfMemSingleton is pure list reasoning (membership in a one-element list forces equality) with no independent implementation-level obligation.
add_left_cancel is Nat arithmetic cancellation used only to derive L009; the implementation-relevant content is the exact +W equality asserted in FACT-1 and FACT-3.
memConsElim is a list case-analysis eliminator with no security-relevant consequence beyond the membership facts already checked in FACT-4 and FACT-6.
notMemNil states nothing is a member of the empty list; it is a base-case library fact, and its security-relevant instance (empty burn-site set) is captured by FACT-5.
