properties.label: gas
properties.text: Verify gas fee accounting: reject or bound any transaction where gas_used > gas_limit or effective_price < base_fee, and check that refund (G-U)*p, tip U*(p-f) and burn U*f sum EXACTLY to the prepayment G*p with no wraparound or truncated subtraction.
properties.assertion: U<=G && f<=p && (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + U*f) == G*p exactly (no unsigned wrap, no truncating sub)

audit_packet.guarantee: For gas limit G, gas used U, base fee f and effective price p, the prepaid amount G*p is partitioned with exact equality into refund (G-U)*p, priority tip U*(p-f) and burned base fee U*f. No value is created or destroyed by process_transaction fee settlement, provided U<=G and f<=p hold before any subtraction.
preconditions: hU: U <= G — gas used never exceeds the gas limit purchased/prepaid (root obligation [1]).
hf: f <= p — the base fee never exceeds the effective gas price actually charged (root obligation [2]).

All quantities are natural numbers under truncating (non-negative) subtraction, so G-U and p-f are only the intended values when hU and hf respectively hold; an implementation using wrapping or unbounded-width integers must enforce both guards explicitly.
Products G*p, (G-U)*p, U*(p-f), U*f are computed at a width that cannot overflow the balance/wei representation.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact conservation: (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + U*f) = G*p — the three settlement components partition the prepayment with equality, not merely with an inequality or a nonzero check.
supporting_facts.check: For the settlement path, compute the prepaid debit G*p and the three credits (refund to sender, tip to the block beneficiary, burn) and compare the sum against the debit as an exact equality over the full input domain, including U=0, U=G, f=0, f=p, and maximum-width G, U, p.
supporting_facts.expected: refund + tip + burn == G*p for every input satisfying U<=G and f<=p; every individual component matches its formula ((G-U)*p, U*(p-f), U*f) rather than only the total matching.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The sum differs from G*p in any direction; the code compares only a weaker property (e.g. 'refund <= prepayment' or 'burn > 0'); or any component is computed by a route that can round, saturate, or truncate.

supporting_facts.claim: The conservation is stable under an accumulated burn total: (G-U)*p + (U*(p-f) + (U*f + Fb)) = G*p + Fb for any pre-existing burn accumulator Fb, under the same hypotheses U<=G and f<=p.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise fee settlement repeatedly against a running burn accumulator and confirm the accumulator grows by exactly U*f each time while the per-transaction partition still closes; verify the accumulator arithmetic uses the same width guarantees as the per-transaction values.
supporting_facts.expected: Accumulated burn after n settlements equals the exact sum of the per-transaction U*f terms, and each settlement's refund/tip/burn still sums to that transaction's G*p.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The accumulator wraps, saturates, or is updated with a value other than U*f; the burn is double-counted into both the accumulator and a per-transaction credit; or the accumulator update is applied before the U<=G / f<=p guards are checked.

supporting_facts.claim: The partition rests on the guarded cancellation identities (G-U)+U = G and f+(p-f) = p, each of which is valid ONLY under its ordering hypothesis (U<=G, f<=p respectively). These are the exact points where truncating or wrapping subtraction breaks conservation.
supporting_facts.check: Audit every subtraction on this surface — the unused-gas term G-U and the priority-fee term p-f — and confirm each is dominated by an enforced check or type invariant establishing U<=G and f<=p. Then verify by test that (G-U)+U reproduces G and (p-f)+f reproduces p for the widest representable inputs.
supporting_facts.expected: Both subtractions are unreachable unless their ordering precondition holds; the cancellation identities hold exactly at every representable boundary.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Either subtraction is reachable with U>G or f>p (e.g. a gas-used value derived from execution that can exceed the purchased limit, or an effective price selected below the block base fee); the guard is an assertion compiled out in release builds; or an underflow is 'handled' by clamping to zero, which silently mints refund/tip value instead of rejecting the transaction.

supporting_facts.claim: The regrouping is justified by exact distributivity in both arguments: k*(m+n) = k*m + k*n and (m+n)*k = m*k + n*k. The identity therefore holds only if every intermediate product and sum is computed exactly, with no reassociation-induced rounding, saturation, or intermediate wraparound.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the intermediate products (G-U)*p, U*(p-f), U*f and the reference total G*p are each representable at the widths used, and that no intermediate step is narrowed or clamped before the final comparison. Test with G, U at the block/transaction gas ceiling and p at the maximum representable fee-per-gas.
supporting_facts.expected: Every intermediate product is computed and stored at full width; regrouping the terms in any valid order yields an identical total.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any intermediate multiplication can wrap or saturate at maximum gas limit times maximum fee-per-gas; a narrower type is used for an intermediate than for the final balance; or the total is derived by a different grouping than the one that was bounds-checked.

derived_obligations.check: Locate the enforcement of U <= G on the settlement path and confirm a transaction whose reported gas used exceeds its purchased gas limit is rejected (or the block invalidated) before any refund, tip, or burn is credited.
derived_obligations.expected: No settlement arithmetic executes when U > G; the condition is enforced, not assumed.
derived_obligations.flag_if: U is taken from an attacker-influenceable path (metering result, refund adjustment, or a caller-supplied value) without a check against G, making the G-U underflow remotely reachable with a single transaction.

derived_obligations.check: Locate the enforcement of f <= p and confirm any transaction whose effective gas price is below the block base fee is rejected before the tip term U*(p-f) is computed.
derived_obligations.expected: No settlement arithmetic executes when f > p; the check accounts for the base fee value actually used in the burn term (the same f in both U*(p-f) and U*f).
derived_obligations.flag_if: A transaction can be included with effective price below base fee; or the f used for the tip differs from the f used for the burn, so the two terms no longer telescope to U*p.

derived_obligations.check: Bound-check the widest products: G*p and (G-U)*p at maximum gas limit and maximum fee-per-gas, and U*f at maximum gas used and maximum base fee.
derived_obligations.expected: All products fit the balance representation with no wraparound or saturation at every boundary value.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any product can overflow the type used, which would let a single crafted high-gas-limit / high-fee transaction produce a refund or tip far exceeding the prepayment — a remotely reachable fund-integrity break.

derived_obligations.check: Add a settlement-level conservation test/invariant asserting total debited (G*p) equals refund + tip + burn for every processed transaction, and fuzz it across U in [0,G], f in [0,p], and boundary-magnitude G, U, p.
derived_obligations.expected: The invariant holds with exact equality on every input, including all four corner combinations (U=0/U=G crossed with f=0/f=p).
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any input produces a mismatch, or the invariant is expressed as an inequality/tolerance rather than exact equality.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the burn credit is exactly U*f and the tip credit exactly U*(p-f) — not U*p minus a separately computed burn, and not a value re-derived from a different base-fee or gas-used snapshot.
derived_obligations.expected: Tip and burn are derived from one consistent (U, f, p) triple captured for the transaction, so their sum is exactly U*p.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Tip and burn are computed from different snapshots of the base fee or gas used, which breaks the telescoping even when both individual computations look correct in isolation.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem states the settlement partition as an exact equality (FACT-1) under exactly two hypotheses: U<=G and f<=p. Its proof reduces via the accumulator-general form fee_split (FACT-2, L001) to distributivity (FACT-4, L002/L004) plus the two guarded cancellation lemmas (FACT-3, L003 via L005). Because the arithmetic is over naturals with truncating subtraction, the ordering hypotheses are not cosmetic — they are precisely the conditions under which G-U and p-f denote the intended quantities. An implementation that reaches either subtraction without its guard, or that computes any intermediate product at a width that can wrap, loses the equality and therefore mints or destroys ether during process_transaction: a remotely reachable, single-transaction fund-integrity break at network scale.

    instLENat.le f p →

          (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul U (instHSub.hSub p f)) (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul U f) Fb)))

Eq
  (instHAdd.hAdd (instHMul.hMul (instHSub.hSub G U) p)

properties.label: evm
properties.text: Verify the fee-burn path reports burn = min(fee, balance) for a live account, debits exactly that reported amount, leaves other accounts untouched, and keeps supply + burn conserved.
properties.assertion: s in live && receipt.burn == min(v, bal(s)) && bal'(s) == bal(s) - receipt.burn && supply' + receipt.burn == supply

audit_packet.guarantee: For a fee burn of requested amount v from a live account s, the burn recorded in the accounting/receipt is exactly the saturated value min(v, bal(s)) — never the unclamped request — and the ledger update that accompanies it is a point update on s that keeps supply + burn == supply_before + mint.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hs: the burn source account s is a member of the ledger's live account list (s ∈ L.live); the balance-setting operation is only invoked under this membership witness.
The live account list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct), so the point update on s is unambiguous.
Any account with a non-zero balance is live (Ledger.bal_live), so no funded account can be debited outside the membership precondition.
The requested burn amount v and every balance are non-negative naturals; subtraction on balances is the saturating (truncated) operation.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact equality (not a bound, not a boolean): the burn field of the accounting produced by the balance-subtracting fee operation equals min(v, bal(s)), where v is the requested amount and bal(s) the pre-state balance of the source.
supporting_facts.check: Drive the fee-burn path with requested amounts spanning v < bal(s), v == bal(s), and v > bal(s) (including v = 2^256-1 and bal(s) = 0), then read the burn amount the implementation reports/accumulates for that operation.
supporting_facts.expected: reported_burn == min(v, bal(s)) in every case; for v > bal(s) the reported burn is exactly bal(s), and for bal(s) == 0 it is 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The reported burn equals the unclamped request v when v > bal(s), or is computed from a value that was not clamped against the pre-state balance, or is derived from a wrapped/underflowed difference.

supporting_facts.claim: Conservation (Ledger.acc_setBal_sub, the balanced field of Accounting): post-state supply plus the reported burn equals pre-state supply plus mint, with mint = 0 for this operation — i.e. the reported burn accounts for exactly the value removed from supply.
supporting_facts.check: For each fee burn, compare total supply before and after against the reported burn: recompute total_supply' + reported_burn and total_supply + reported_mint.
supporting_facts.expected: total_supply' + reported_burn == total_supply + 0; the actual balance decrement of s equals the reported burn.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Supply drops by more or less than the reported burn, mint is non-zero on this path, or the receipt-visible burn diverges from the value actually removed from the account.

supporting_facts.claim: The accompanying state update is the point update setBal s (bal(s) - v) hs: the target balance is set via saturating subtraction and every other account's balance is returned unchanged (bal' b = if b = s then new else bal b).
supporting_facts.check: Snapshot all account balances before and after a fee burn, including the v > bal(s) case, and diff them.
supporting_facts.expected: Only s changes; bal'(s) == bal(s) - reported_burn == max(0, bal(s) - v), never negative and never wrapped.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A second account's balance changes, s's new balance is not the saturated difference, or the balance underflows/wraps to a huge value when v > bal(s).

supporting_facts.claim: The membership witness hs is a required input to the operation, not an assumption discharged after the fact: the balance-setting primitive cannot be applied to a source that is not in the live account set.
supporting_facts.check: Attempt the fee-burn path with a source account absent from the live/existing account set (never-touched or pruned address) and inspect whether the implementation checks existence before mutating and before recording a burn.
supporting_facts.expected: The path either establishes liveness first (creating/loading the account so membership holds) or rejects; no burn is recorded for a non-live source.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The implementation mutates or records a burn for an account whose existence was never established, or infers liveness from a stale/assumed lookup result.

derived_obligations.check: Property/fuzz test over (bal, v) pairs concentrated near the boundary v == bal(s) and at extremes (bal=0, v=0, v at max word), asserting reported burn against an independently computed min(v, bal).
derived_obligations.expected: reported_burn == min(v, bal(s)) with no off-by-one at v == bal(s) and no wraparound at extremes.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any pair yields a reported burn greater than bal(s) or greater than v.

derived_obligations.check: Cross-check the burn amount surfaced to consumers (receipt/accounting output) against the delta actually applied to the account and to total supply, on the same operation.
derived_obligations.expected: All three agree: reported burn == balance delta of s == supply delta.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The consumer-visible burn is computed from the requested amount while the state change uses the saturated amount (or vice versa) — a remotely triggerable divergence in supply accounting between implementations.

derived_obligations.check: Review the subtraction used on the balance for saturating (not wrapping, not signed) semantics, and confirm no bounds check is skipped on any caller path into the fee-burn routine.
derived_obligations.expected: Every path clamps the debit to the available balance before both the state write and the burn record.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any caller reaches the balance write with an unclamped amount, or the clamp exists only on one of the two outputs (state vs. report).

derived_obligations.check: Exercise the fee-burn path against a source account not present in the live account set and against duplicate/aliased account entries.
derived_obligations.expected: Liveness is established or the operation is refused; no duplicate entry makes the point update ambiguous.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A burn is recorded or state is written without an established membership witness, or two entries for the same account allow the debit to be applied to only one of them.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem gives an exact identity for the reported burn: (Accounting.ofSetBalSub L s v hs).burn = min v (L.bal s). Its only implementation obligation is the membership witness hs : s ∈ L.live, which is a required argument of both setBal and ofSetBalSub — hence a mandatory guard (FACT-4, OBS-4). The accounting value is constructed together with the state transition L → L.setBal s (L.bal s - v) hs, so the reported burn (FACT-1) and the point update with saturating subtraction (FACT-3) are two halves of one operation and must be checked jointly. Its balanced field, supplied by Ledger.acc_setBal_sub, is the stronger conservation statement supply' + min v (bal s) = supply + 0 and is preserved as FACT-2 rather than weakened to 'some burn was recorded'. A missing bounds check manifests as reported_burn = v (or a wrapped balance) when v > bal(s), which desynchronizes supply accounting across implementations — the highest-impact, remotely reachable failure of this invariant.

properties.label: transactions
properties.text: For a live sender s with bal(s)<v, reject the transfer instead of saturating: debit-then-credit inflates total supply by exactly v-bal(s), and any positive-value self-transfer must also be rejected.
properties.assertion: s in live and bal(s)<v => reject (no saturating debit); supply' == supply; v>0 and src==dst => reject

audit_packet.guarantee: In the transactions area (CALL / state.move_ether / transfer semantics), a value transfer of amount v from a live account s must be rejected whenever bal(s) < v. If instead the debit is applied with truncating (saturating-at-zero) subtraction and the credit of v is applied on top of the debited state, total supply strictly increases by exactly v - bal(s) — remote, unbounded minting of ether. Additionally, a positive-value self-transfer (source == destination) is unsatisfiable under transfer semantics and must be rejected rather than silently applied.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] hs: the source account s is a member of the live account set (s in L.live) — the debited account must be an existing, tracked account whose balance participates in the supply sum.

ROOT obligation [2] hgt: the requested amount strictly exceeds the source balance (L.bal s < v) — this is the overdraft precondition under which the naive saturating implementation is proved to inflate supply.

Balances are non-negative naturals (Nat), so subtraction is truncating: bal(s) - v evaluates to 0 rather than wrapping or going negative; the overflow/underflow defect surfaces as silent truncation on the debit leg.
The live account list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct / Distinct L.live) and any account with a nonzero balance is live (Ledger.bal_live); supply is defined as sumOver bal live.

supporting_facts.claim: Root conjunct 2: for a live s with bal(s) < v, applying the truncating debit setBal s (bal s - v) and then crediting v to the resulting state yields a ledger whose supply is STRICTLY GREATER than the original supply — the naive overdraft path mints ether.
supporting_facts.check: Construct a live account s with bal(s) = b and issue a transfer of v > b through the CALL / move_ether transfer path with the balance check removed or evaluated after the debit; sum all account balances before and after.
supporting_facts.expected: The transfer is rejected before any state mutation, and the summed total supply is bit-for-bit unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The transfer succeeds (or partially applies) and the post-state total supply is strictly larger than the pre-state total supply.

supporting_facts.claim: EXACT equality, not merely an inequality: after the truncating debit of v from s and the credit of v to d, supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)). The amount minted is exactly the shortfall v - bal(s), so the inflation is attacker-chosen and unbounded (choose v arbitrarily large against a zero-balance account).
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the transfer path to record supply before and after for several (bal(s), v) pairs with v > bal(s), including bal(s) = 0 and v at the maximum representable value.
supporting_facts.expected: No such post-state is reachable because the overdraft is rejected; if a test harness forces the naive path, the delta must equal exactly v - bal(s), confirming the shortfall is the mint amount.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any code path can reach a post-state where supply increased, or where the delta is treated as a rounding/dust artifact rather than a supply break; also flag if only a weaker 'supply changed' assertion is implemented instead of checking the exact delta.

supporting_facts.claim: The inflation is not specific to self-transfer: for ANY live source s and live destination d (distinct or equal), bal(s) < v implies the truncating debit plus credit of v strictly increases supply. Every caller of the transfer primitive, not just the self-transfer edge case, is affected.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate all call sites that reach the value-transfer primitive (the CALL value path and the generic move_ether path) and confirm each performs the sufficiency check on the SOURCE balance before the debit.
supporting_facts.expected: Every entry point into the transfer primitive enforces bal(source) >= v before any mutation, or the primitive itself enforces it unconditionally and returns a failure the caller must handle.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any call site reaches the debit with an unchecked or caller-supplied amount, or the check lives only in one wrapper while another entry point bypasses it.

supporting_facts.claim: General conservation law for one transfer step: supply' + min(v, bal(s)) = supply + v. Value is conserved only when min(v, bal(s)) = v, i.e. exactly when v <= bal(s). The sufficiency check is precisely the side condition that turns this identity into conservation.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the conservation identity as a property/differential test over the transfer primitive across randomized (bal(s), bal(d), v) triples, including v > bal(s).
supporting_facts.expected: For all accepted transfers, supply' = supply exactly; the min(v, bal(s)) = v case is the only reachable one.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An accepted transfer yields supply' != supply, i.e. a reachable case where min(v, bal(s)) < v.

supporting_facts.claim: Debit leg, exact: supply(setBal s (bal s - v)) + min(v, bal(s)) = supply. The debit removes only min(v, bal(s)) from supply, NOT v — this is where the truncation loses the shortfall.
supporting_facts.check: Isolate the debit half of the transfer and measure the supply decrease for v > bal(s).
supporting_facts.expected: Supply decreases by exactly bal(s) (the full source balance) and the source is zeroed; this state must never be committed without a matching credit of the same reduced amount.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The debit is applied with a truncating/saturating subtraction while the credit leg uses the original v, or the implementation zeroes the sender and proceeds as if v had been removed.

supporting_facts.claim: Credit leg, exact: supply(setBal d (bal d + v)) = supply + v. The credit adds the full v unconditionally, with no clamping and no dependence on the debit outcome.
supporting_facts.check: Isolate the credit half and confirm the credited amount is derived from the amount actually debited, not from the unvalidated request amount.
supporting_facts.expected: Credit amount == debited amount for every accepted transfer.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The credit uses the requested v while the debit was clamped, creating the v - bal(s) mint; or the credit can overflow the destination's balance representation.

supporting_facts.claim: The minted quantity is strictly positive: bal(s) < v implies 0 < v - bal(s). There is no degenerate boundary at which the overdraft path is harmless — every overdraft mints at least one unit.
supporting_facts.check: Test the boundary case v = bal(s) + 1 in addition to large v.
supporting_facts.expected: Rejected, exactly as the large-v case is; no off-by-one window where v = bal(s) + 1 slips through a >= vs > comparison.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The sufficiency comparison is written such that v = bal(s) + 1 (or v = bal(s)) is misclassified — a strict/non-strict inequality inversion in the balance check.

supporting_facts.claim: Root conjunct 1: no positive-value self-transfer can satisfy transfer semantics. If K.bal s + w = M.bal s and K.bal s = M.bal s + w both hold, then by add_left_cancel the amount w = 0; hence 0 < w is contradictory. A self-transfer is only consistent at amount zero.
supporting_facts.check: Submit a transfer where source == destination with v > 0 through every entry point and inspect both the resulting balances and the total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: Either the self-transfer is rejected, or it is a strict no-op: bal(s) unchanged and supply unchanged. It must NOT be implemented as an independent debit followed by an independent credit on stale reads.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The self-transfer path reads the pre-debit balance to compute the credit (stale-read pattern), producing bal(s) = bal(s) + v or bal(s) - v as a net effect, or any supply change; also flag if source == destination is unhandled and reaches the generic two-sided debit/credit code.

supporting_facts.claim: The supply accounting identity supply(setBal a v) + bal(a) = supply + v holds only when the live list is duplicate-free (Distinct l) and a is a member of it. Account uniqueness and membership are load-bearing preconditions of the entire conservation argument.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the account collection backing balances cannot contain duplicate entries for one address, and that the account touched by a debit or credit is registered in that collection before its balance is read or written.
supporting_facts.expected: Duplicate-free account registry enforced structurally; every debited or credited account is a registered member.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An address can appear twice in the balance-summation domain (double-counting its balance in supply), or a balance is written for an address not in the summation domain.

supporting_facts.claim: Updating a non-member leaves the sum unchanged: sumOver (update a v) l = sumOver f l when a is not in l. A credit written to an account outside the live/summation domain is invisible to the supply total — the mirror-image accounting break (silent burn / unaccounted balance).
supporting_facts.check: Credit a destination account that is not yet registered in the account collection and then recompute total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: The destination is registered (created) as part of the credit so its balance is included in the supply sum.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A credit to a previously unseen destination does not register the account, so the credited value is excluded from the supply total while remaining spendable, or vice versa.

derived_obligations.check: Locate the sufficiency check on the source balance in the value-transfer path and confirm it is evaluated BEFORE any balance mutation, on a freshly read source balance, and against the full transfer amount v.
derived_obligations.expected: A guard equivalent to `bal(source) >= v` (equivalently: reject when bal(source) < v) gates the debit; failing it aborts the transfer with no partial state change.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The check is absent, evaluated after the debit, applied to a cached/stale balance, applied to a different amount than the one debited, or its failure path still commits one of the two legs.

derived_obligations.check: Inspect the arithmetic used on the debit leg for unsigned truncation or saturation at zero, and on the credit leg for wraparound at the balance type's maximum.
derived_obligations.expected: Subtraction is guarded by OBS-1 so it can never truncate; addition is checked or provably bounded by total supply so it cannot wrap.
derived_obligations.flag_if: `bal - v` on an unsigned type without a preceding guard (silently yielding 0), or `bal + v` without an overflow check on a fixed-width type.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the credit amount is computed from the post-debit state, i.e. the two legs are sequenced against a single evolving state rather than both reading the original pre-transfer snapshot.
derived_obligations.expected: Debit then credit applied in sequence to the same state value, matching the nested setBal composition in the proof; source == destination therefore nets to zero.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Both legs read the pre-transfer balances (aliasing bug), so a self-transfer or aliased source/destination yields a net balance change and a supply change.

derived_obligations.check: Add a supply-conservation assertion (total of all balances is invariant across a transfer) to the differential/fuzz test harness for the transfer path, exercised with v > bal(source), v = bal(source) + 1, bal(source) = 0, source == destination, and unregistered destinations.
derived_obligations.expected: The invariant holds on every accepted transfer and every rejection leaves state untouched.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any input in that set produces a supply delta, a partially applied transfer, or an unregistered account holding a nonzero balance.

derived_obligations.check: Enumerate every entry point that can reach the transfer primitive with a remotely attacker-controlled amount (the value field on a CALL, and any internal move_ether caller) and verify each is covered by OBS-1.
derived_obligations.expected: No remotely reachable path can supply an amount that bypasses the source-balance guard.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any path accepts an attacker-chosen amount and reaches the debit without the guard — this is the remote single-transaction fund-integrity break that sets the severity.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem's two hypotheses are exactly the audit preconditions: s is a live account (hs) and the requested amount exceeds its balance (hgt). Under those, the root proves a conjunction. Conjunct 2 (via L002 -> L004) says the naive debit-then-credit sequence yields supply' > supply. L004 is refined by L006/L009 into an EXACT equality, supply' = supply + (v - bal(s)), and L007 shows that shortfall is strictly positive — so the mint amount is exactly the attacker-chosen overdraft, not an epsilon. The mechanism is decomposed by L012 (supply' + min(v, bal(s)) = supply + v) into a debit leg L016 (removes only min(v, bal(s))) and a credit leg L015 (adds the full v); the gap between them is precisely the truncating subtraction on unsigned balances, which is the integer_overflow_underflow defect class in its saturating form. All of this accounting rests on L024/L025/L026, whose own hypotheses are duplicate-freeness of the account list and membership of the touched account — captured as FACT-9 — with L028 giving the dual failure (a credit outside the summation domain vanishes from supply). Conjunct 1 (via L001 -> L003 -> L005 -> add_left_cancel) independently rules out positive-value self-transfers: the two transfer equations force the amount to zero, so an implementation that services a self-transfer as two stale-read legs is already outside the specification. The audit therefore requires a pre-mutation source-balance guard on every remotely reachable transfer entry point, non-truncating arithmetic on both legs, sequenced (non-aliased) application of debit then credit, account-registry uniqueness and membership, and a supply-conservation assertion in tests.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.add_left_cancel is a generic Nat cancellation lemma; its security content is fully carried by FACT-8 (the self-transfer amount must be zero), which it is used to prove. No independent implementation obligation.
EthTotal.add_sub_cancel_right ((n + m) - m = n) is pure Nat arithmetic plumbing used to establish L007; the security-relevant consequence (the shortfall is strictly positive) is FACT-7.
EthTotal.add_right_cancel is generic Nat cancellation used inside the supply algebra (L012/L015/L016); no separate implementation-visible claim beyond FACT-4/5/6.
EthTotal.min_comm is commutativity of min, a normalization step in the supply algebra with no implementation-level meaning.

EthTotal.min_add_sub (min v b + (b - v) = b) is the arithmetic core of truncating subtraction; its security meaning is already exposed concretely as FACT-5 (the debit removes only min(v, bal(s))) and FACT-2 (the exact shortfall), so restating it separately would duplicate rather than add coverage.
EthTotal.le_min is a lattice property of min used only within L013; no implementation obligation.
EthTotal.min_le_right is a lattice property of min used only within L013; no implementation obligation.
EthTotal.min_le_left is a lattice property of min used only within L013; no implementation obligation.
EthTotal.min_eq_left is a case-split helper for L014 (the v <= b branch); the branch's security content is the conservation case in FACT-4.

EthTotal.add_sub_cancel_of_le (x + (y - x) = y under x <= y) is the arithmetic statement that subtraction is exact when the guard holds; surfaced operationally as OBS-1/OBS-2 rather than as a separate fact.
EthTotal.min_eq_right is the dual case-split helper for L014 (the b <= v branch); the branch's security content is the truncation case already in FACT-5 and FACT-2.

EthTotal.sub_eq_zero_of_le (x - y = 0 when x <= y) is the formal statement of saturation-to-zero; its concrete manifestation is covered by FACT-5 and OBS-2 (unguarded unsigned subtraction silently yields 0).
EthTotal.notMemNil is a base-case elimination for the empty account list inside the sumOver induction; no implementation obligation.
EthTotal.memConsElim is a list-membership case-analysis combinator inside the sumOver induction; no implementation obligation beyond the membership requirement already captured in FACT-9.

∀ {n m k : Nat}, Eq (instHAdd.hAdd n m) (instHAdd.hAdd k m) → Eq n k

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify every fee-burn balance write is non-increasing per account, that the live-account enumeration is duplicate-free and covers every nonzero balance before and after, and that new_supply + Σ(old_bal − new_bal) over that set equals old_supply exactly.
properties.assertion: ∀a. new_bal[a] <= old_bal[a] & distinct(live) & supp(old)|supp(new) ⊆ live => new_supply + Σ_live(old_bal-new_bal) == old_supply

audit_packet.guarantee: Under a state update that never increases any account balance (fee burn), total supply is exactly conserved: the post-state total supply plus the sum of all per-account decrements over a duplicate-free account enumeration that covers the support equals the pre-state total supply. The guarantee is an exact equality over natural-number balances, not a bound or a nonzero-burn check.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hbal: for every account a, the post-state balance (L'.bal a) is less than or equal to the pre-state balance (L.bal a) — the update is non-increasing on every account, and no account gains value during the burn.
Pre-state ledger well-formedness (Ledger.live_distinct): the account enumeration used to total supply (L.live) contains no duplicate accounts.

Pre-state support coverage (Ledger.bal_live): every account with a nonzero pre-state balance appears in L.live. Combined with hbal this also forces coverage of every nonzero post-state account, so the update must not produce a nonzero balance for an account outside the enumerated set.

Total supply of a ledger is defined as the sum of that ledger's own balance function over that ledger's own enumeration (Ledger.supply = sumOver bal live); balances are non-negative naturals, so subtraction is truncated (saturating) rather than signed.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation: post-state total supply plus the summed per-account decrements over the pre-state enumeration equals the pre-state total supply exactly (L'.supply + Σ_{a∈L.live}(L.bal a − L'.bal a) = L.supply).
supporting_facts.check: Independently recompute total supply before and after the burn-bearing state update over the full account set, recompute the sum of per-account decrements, and compare the two sides of the equality with exact integer arithmetic.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply + total_decrement == pre_supply, holding as an exact equality for every update in the burn path.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sides differ by any amount, or the implementation only asserts a weaker consequence (post_supply <= pre_supply, burn amount nonzero, burn amount within a tolerance) instead of the exact equality — a remotely reachable transaction that breaks this equality makes total supply client-dependent and diverges the resulting state, a chain-split-scale fund-integrity defect.

supporting_facts.claim: Two-sided exchange identity: for ANY duplicate-free list covering both the pre- and post-state supports, L'.supply + Σ(L.bal − L'.bal) = L.supply + Σ(L'.bal − L.bal). Conservation is symmetric — decrements and increments must balance — and it follows from list distinctness plus support coverage, with additivity of the sum (sumOver_add) and the per-element symmetry x + (y − x) = y + (x − y) (add_sub_symm) as the load-bearing steps.
supporting_facts.check: On the burn path, compute both directional aggregates over the enumerated account set: total debited (old − new) and total credited (new − old). Confirm the balance equation holds in both directions, not just the debit direction.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply + total_debited == pre_supply + total_credited, with total_credited == 0 for a pure burn.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any nonzero credited aggregate appears in the burn path, or the implementation accounts only for debits and would therefore silently absorb an unexpected credit into the supply total.

supporting_facts.claim: Enumeration independence: two duplicate-free lists with the same nonzero support produce the same sum (sumOver_eq_of_support_iff). Total supply therefore depends only on the set of accounts with nonzero balance, not on iteration order, container, or which enumeration was used.
supporting_facts.check: Compute the total supply of the same state through at least two independent enumerations of the account set (e.g. differing orders, or a full enumeration versus one restricted to accounts with nonzero balance) and compare results.
supporting_facts.expected: All enumerations yield the identical total; a nonzero-balance account is present in every enumeration used for totalling.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Totals differ across enumerations or orders, or an enumeration omits an account whose balance is nonzero, or includes/relies on order-sensitive accumulation — this makes the invariant unverifiable and is exactly how one node's supply accounting can diverge from another's.

supporting_facts.claim: Saturating-subtraction hazard: over naturals, x ≤ y implies x − y = 0 (sub_eq_zero_of_le), and the root proof uses this with pointwise congruence (sumOver_congr / sumOver_congr_mem) and sumOver_zero to collapse the reverse-delta sum to exactly 0. The collapse is valid ONLY because hbal holds; without it, a genuine balance increase is silently truncated to a zero delta and vanishes from the accounting.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect every subtraction used to derive a burned/decrement amount in the balance-update path. Confirm the non-increase is checked before subtracting (or that a checked/signed subtraction surfaces the violation) rather than relying on unsigned truncation or a max(0, ·) clamp.
supporting_facts.expected: Any case where the new balance exceeds the old balance is detected and rejected/errored; the zero-delta result is reachable only when the two balances are genuinely equal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A decrement is computed as an unsigned or clamped subtraction with no prior non-increase check, so an account that gained value yields delta 0 (or wraps) — the conservation ledger then loses that amount and total supply is quietly inflated relative to the sum of balances.

supporting_facts.claim: No double counting: the sum splits additively across list concatenation (sumOver_append) and across extraction of a middle element (sumOver_middle), and distinctness is preserved and enforced by the split lemmas (exists_split_of_mem, Distinct.notMemMiddle, Distinct.removeMiddle). Each account therefore contributes its balance exactly once to the total.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the account enumeration used for supply totalling cannot list the same account twice — including via aliasing (two entries resolving to the same account) or via merging partial enumerations/subtries whose ranges overlap. Verify subtotal composition is a disjoint partition.
supporting_facts.expected: Every account occurs at most once across all subtotals; the total supply equals the sum of subtotals of a disjoint partition of the enumeration.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can be enumerated twice or an account can be dropped when subtotals are combined — a remotely reachable duplicate/omission inflates or deflates the computed supply and breaks the equality of FACT-1 while every per-account balance still looks correct.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-account exactness: x ≤ y implies x + (y − x) = y (add_sub_cancel_of_le). For each account, the recorded decrement plus the new balance reconstitutes the old balance exactly — no rounding, clamping, or residue is permitted at the per-account level.
supporting_facts.check: For each account written during the update, assert new_balance + recorded_decrement == old_balance individually, not merely in aggregate.
supporting_facts.expected: The per-account identity holds exactly for every written account.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any per-account residue exists (rounding, truncation, clamp-to-zero, or a decrement recorded from a value other than the actual pre-state balance), even if aggregate totals happen to cancel out.

derived_obligations.check: At the balance-write site in the burn path, compare the value being written against the current stored balance for that account.
derived_obligations.expected: The write is accepted only when the new value is less than or equal to the current value; a would-be increase aborts the update rather than being applied.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any burn-path write can set a balance above its prior value, or the non-increase condition is assumed from a caller rather than enforced where the state is mutated — this voids the ROOT obligation hbal outright.

derived_obligations.check: Audit the arithmetic type and operator used for balance decrements and for accumulating the total decrement.
derived_obligations.expected: Subtraction is checked (error/None on negative result) and accumulation cannot overflow or wrap; no silent max(0, ·) saturation stands in for a validity check.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Truncating, wrapping, or clamped arithmetic is used, so an invalid update produces a well-formed but wrong delta instead of a failure.

derived_obligations.check: Audit how the account set used for supply totalling is built and whether duplicates or aliases are possible.
derived_obligations.expected: The enumeration is duplicate-free by construction (set/keyed structure or an explicit distinctness check), and any composition of subtotals is over disjoint account ranges.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicates, aliased keys, or overlapping subtotal ranges are reachable.

derived_obligations.check: After the update, check that every account with a nonzero balance — including any account first touched by this update — is present in the enumeration used for totalling.
derived_obligations.expected: Support coverage holds for both pre- and post-state: no nonzero balance lives outside the enumerated set.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An update can create or leave a nonzero balance for an account absent from the enumeration, so its value is excluded from the total and conservation appears to hold while supply has actually changed.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the FACT-1 equality as a consensus-visible check at the update/block boundary, computing the two sides via independent paths (per-account delta accumulation versus full re-total of the account set).
derived_obligations.expected: Both computation paths agree and the equality holds; a mismatch halts processing of the offending update rather than committing it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The equality is never checked at runtime, is checked only in debug/test builds, or a mismatch is logged and the state committed anyway — a mismatch committed by one implementation and rejected by another is the chain-split path for this defect class.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem is discharged in two moves. First, exact_supply_on (L001) gives the symmetric exchange identity L'.supply + Σ(L.bal − L'.bal) = L.supply + Σ(L'.bal − L.bal) over the pre-state enumeration; its three obligations are supplied by ledger well-formedness — distinctness of L.live (live_distinct) for dl, bal_live for hcov, and bal_live composed with hbal for hcov' (an account nonzero after the update must have been nonzero before it, since balances only decrease). Internally L001 rests on enumeration-independence of the sum (L005, itself resting on the append/middle splitting and distinctness-preservation lemmas L018, L016, L014, L015, L011), additivity (L006), and the per-element symmetry x + (y − x) = y + (x − y) (L007, which uses add_sub_cancel_of_le L017 and sub_eq_zero_of_le L003). Second, the reverse-delta sum is collapsed: hbal gives L'.bal a ≤ L.bal a, so sub_eq_zero_of_le (L003) makes each reverse delta 0, sumOver_congr (L002, via L008) rewrites the summand to the constant 0, and sumOver_zero (L004) makes the whole sum 0, leaving L.supply + 0 = L.supply. Audit consequence: the equality is load-bearing only when (a) the non-increase is actually enforced at the write site, (b) the account enumeration is duplicate-free, and (c) it covers every nonzero balance before and after. Break any one and the natural-number subtraction saturates or an account is double-counted/omitted, so total supply silently drifts while every individual balance still reads correctly — the improper_state_update class, reachable by a single remote transaction, producing implementation-dependent supply accounting and a divergent committed state.

omitted_facts.reason: notMemNil (no element is a member of the empty list) is list-membership plumbing internal to the base case of the sum lemmas; it carries no implementation-observable condition and no strong fact about balances, supply, coverage, or ordering.

memConsElim is a case-analysis eliminator for membership in a cons cell — a proof-mechanical step with no corresponding implementation obligation beyond the duplicate-freedom and coverage checks already captured in FACT-5, OBS-3, and OBS-4.

memRemoveMiddleOfNe (membership survives removing a distinct middle element) is bookkeeping supporting the enumeration-independence result; its security content is fully subsumed by FACT-3 (enumeration independence) and FACT-5 (no double counting).

memInsertMiddle (membership survives inserting a middle element) is the converse bookkeeping step for the same enumeration-independence argument; subsumed by FACT-3 and FACT-5 with no additional check to perform.

properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: Verify that with no authorized mint or burn sites, every event's mint/burn amount is 0, burned=minted=0, and post-state total supply exactly equals pre-state supply, given L'.supply+burned = L.supply+minted.
properties.assertion: SiteConfined([],[],tau) AND L'.supply+burned(tau)=L.supply+minted(tau) => burned(tau)=0 AND minted(tau)=0 AND L'.supply=L.supply

audit_packet.guarantee: Over a block-processing trace whose mint sites and burn sites are both confined to the empty authorized-site list, total supply is exactly conserved: the post-state ledger supply equals the pre-state ledger supply, with zero minted and zero burned, not merely 'approximately' or 'nonzero-unchanged'.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] hacc: the accounting identity L'.supply + burned(tau) = L.supply + minted(tau) holds across the processed trace, where supply = sumOver bal live over the distinct live account list.

ROOT obligation [2] hc: SiteConfined [] [] tau holds — the trace's authorized mint-site list and authorized burn-site list are both empty, so no event in tau may name a mint destination or a burn source.

Ledger well-formedness carried by the structure: live is Distinct (no duplicated account in the supply sum) and bal_live holds (any account with nonzero balance is present in live), so supply counts every unit exactly once.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact supply conservation: under both root obligations, L'.supply = L.supply — an equality, not a bound or a boolean 'supply did not obviously change'.
supporting_facts.check: Recompute total supply as the sum of balances over the distinct live account list before and after block processing, and compare the two totals for exact equality.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply == pre_supply exactly, with no tolerance, rounding slack, or per-account exemption.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any processed block yields post_supply != pre_supply while no mint site and no burn site was authorized, or the implementation only checks a weaker predicate (e.g. 'supply changed by a small amount', 'supply nonzero') instead of exact equality.

supporting_facts.claim: Minting is exactly zero: with an empty authorized mint-site list, every event's mintAmount is 0 and therefore minted(tau) = 0.
supporting_facts.check: For each event in the processed trace, read its mint amount and assert it is 0; independently assert the accumulated minted total over the whole trace is 0.
supporting_facts.expected: Every per-event mintAmount == 0 and minted(tau) == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event carries a nonzero mint amount, or the accumulated minted total is nonzero, while no mint site was authorized — including a value-creating path inside internal transfer / state.move_ether that credits a destination without a matching debit.

supporting_facts.claim: Burning is exactly zero: with an empty authorized burn-site list, every event's burnAmount is 0 and therefore burned(tau) = 0.
supporting_facts.check: For each event in the processed trace, read its burn amount and assert it is 0; independently assert the accumulated burned total over the whole trace is 0.
supporting_facts.expected: Every per-event burnAmount == 0 and burned(tau) == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event carries a nonzero burn amount, or the accumulated burned total is nonzero, while no burn site was authorized — including a value-destroying path inside internal transfer / state.move_ether that debits a source without a matching credit.

supporting_facts.claim: Site-level strengthening: confinement to the empty list forces each event's mintSite and burnSite to be None outright — no event may even name a mint destination or burn source, which is strictly stronger than the amounts merely summing to zero.
supporting_facts.check: Enumerate the events of the processed trace and assert mintSite is None and burnSite is None for every one, rather than only checking the aggregate totals.
supporting_facts.expected: For all e in tau: e.mintSite == None and e.burnSite == None.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event records a Some mint destination or Some burn source under empty authorization, or the implementation validates only the summed amounts and never rejects an unauthorized site, letting a positive and a negative unauthorized site cancel out in aggregate.

supporting_facts.claim: Additive cancellation is exact on Nat: from L'.supply + b = L.supply + m, left and right cancellation give supply equality iff b = m; there is no slack term that could absorb an inconsistency.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the accounting reconciliation is performed by exact cancellation over unsigned/natural balances — burned and minted totals are compared to each other and to zero — with no saturating subtraction, wraparound, or truncation that could silently absorb a discrepancy.
supporting_facts.expected: supply equality is derived exactly from burned == minted (here both == 0); reconciliation arithmetic neither saturates nor wraps.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Balance or supply arithmetic can underflow, wrap, saturate to zero, or be truncated, so an unbalanced block still reconciles; or the reconciliation compares only one side (e.g. checks minted but never burned).

derived_obligations.check: Guard the value-moving path (internal transfer / state.move_ether) with an explicit bounds check on the moved amount against the source account's available balance BEFORE applying the debit and credit, and reject the whole operation when the bound is violated.
derived_obligations.expected: amount <= bal(source) is validated up front; on violation the transfer is rejected and no balance is mutated, so debit and credit are always equal and opposite.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The moved amount is applied without a prior balance bounds check, or the check happens after mutation, or an over-balance move is clamped/wrapped instead of rejected — any of which mints or burns value with no authorized site and breaks FACT-1 at network scale from a single remotely submitted transaction.

derived_obligations.check: Verify that the value-moving path emits no mint or burn event and touches exactly the source and destination balances: the sum of the two affected balances is identical before and after.
derived_obligations.expected: bal(src)+bal(dst) is unchanged by the move; no event with Some mintSite or Some burnSite is produced by an internal transfer.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A transfer path can create or destroy value (credit without debit, debit without credit, self-transfer double-credit) or can synthesize a mint/burn event that bypasses the empty-authorized-site confinement.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the supply accounting itself: the total is summed over a duplicate-free live account set, and any account carrying a nonzero balance is present in that set.
derived_obligations.expected: live has no duplicates (Distinct) and every nonzero-balance account is in live, so supply neither double-counts nor drops units.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An account can appear twice in the live set (double-counted supply) or a nonzero balance can exist outside the live set (invisible supply), either of which makes the supply comparison in FACT-1 pass while real value was created or lost.

derived_obligations.check: Assert the full-block reconciliation identity end to end: recomputed post_supply + total_burned == pre_supply + total_minted, and independently total_burned == 0 and total_minted == 0 when no site is authorized.
derived_obligations.expected: The identity holds exactly and both totals are zero; a failure aborts block processing rather than being logged and ignored.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The reconciliation is not enforced per block, is only advisory/logged, or is satisfied by adjusting a balancing term instead of rejecting the block.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes two obligations: the accounting identity hacc (L'.supply + burned = L.supply + minted) and the confinement hypothesis hc (SiteConfined [] [] tau). From hc, membership in the empty list is impossible, so every event's mintSite and burnSite must be None (FACT-4, via L014/L010). None sites force per-event mintAmount = 0 and burnAmount = 0 (L016, L013), which sum to minted(tau) = 0 (FACT-2, via L015/L011/L006/L003) and burned(tau) = 0 (FACT-3, via L012/L009/L005/L002). Substituting both zeros into hacc reduces it to L'.supply + 0 = L.supply + 0, and exact Nat cancellation (FACT-5, L007/L008 through L004) yields the exact equality L'.supply = L.supply (FACT-1, L001). The audit therefore checks all four strong levels rather than only the final consequence: no unauthorized site at all, zero per-event amounts, zero aggregate minted/burned, and exact supply equality. The derived obligations aim these at the missing_bounds_check class on the value-moving surface: an unchecked amount in internal transfer / state.move_ether is the remotely reachable, single-transaction way to violate the zero-mint/zero-burn facts and split the network on supply state.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.notMemNil (membership in the empty list yields False) is a pure library-level elimination with no implementation-observable content; its security-relevant consequence is already carried by FACT-4 (sites must be None under empty authorization) via L014 and L010.

properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: Verify that with no permitted mint sites, block processing mints zero value and post-state supply plus burned fees equals pre-state supply exactly, with every burn charged to an allowed burn site.
properties.assertion: SiteConfined([],B,tau) & L'.supply+burned(tau)=L.supply+minted(tau) => minted(tau)=0 & L'.supply+burned(tau)=L.supply

audit_packet.guarantee: For a block whose event trace has an empty set of permitted mint sites and whose burn sites are confined to B, the post-state total supply plus the total burned amount equals the pre-state total supply exactly (no net issuance, no silent loss).
preconditions: Accounting identity (root obligation hacc): L'.supply + burned(tau) = L.supply + minted(tau) holds over the block's event trace tau, where supply is the sum of bal over the distinct live account list.

Site confinement (root obligation hc): SiteConfined([], B, tau) holds, i.e. every event carrying a mint site is impossible (permitted mint-site list is empty) and every event carrying a burn site names a site in B.
Ledger well-formedness: live is Distinct and any account with nonzero bal is in live, so supply is a well-defined sum with no double counting.

supporting_facts.claim: Under the accounting identity and empty-mint-site confinement, post supply plus burned equals pre supply EXACTLY (equality, not an inequality or nonzero check).
supporting_facts.check: Recompute pre-state total supply, post-state total supply, and the total burned amount for the block, then compare L'.supply + burned == L.supply as exact integers.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact equality; total supply decreases by precisely the burned amount and by nothing else.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any block where the recomputed post supply plus burned differs from pre supply, or where the check is implemented as a bound/approximation/nonzero test instead of exact equality.

supporting_facts.claim: Burn confinement (hc.burn_mem): every event with a burn site names a site belonging to B; no burn may be charged to a site outside the permitted set.
supporting_facts.check: For each burn event in the block trace, verify its burn site is a member of the permitted burn-site list B before the balance is reduced.
supporting_facts.expected: Every burn site is in B; burns from any other site are rejected.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A burn is applied whose site is absent from B, or the membership test is skipped/short-circuited for any code path that reduces supply.

supporting_facts.claim: Confinement to the empty mint-site list forces minted(tau) = 0 for the whole trace — an exact zero total, not merely a bound.
supporting_facts.check: Sum the mint amounts over all events in the block trace and confirm the total is exactly 0 whenever the permitted mint-site list is empty.
supporting_facts.expected: minted(tau) == 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Total minted is nonzero while no mint site is permitted, or the total is never computed/checked.

supporting_facts.claim: Per-event: with an empty permitted mint-site list, each event's mint site is necessarily none, because membership in the empty list is uninhabited (notMemNil yields False).
supporting_facts.check: For each event in the trace, confirm its mint site is absent; assert that a claimed mint site can never satisfy membership in an empty permitted list.
supporting_facts.expected: Every event has mintSite = none.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any event carries a mint site while the permitted list is empty, or code treats an empty permitted list as 'unconstrained'/'allow all' rather than 'deny all'.

supporting_facts.claim: An event with no mint site has mint amount exactly 0, and a trace where every event has zero mint amount has minted(tau) = 0.
supporting_facts.check: Verify per-event that absence of a mint site implies the credited amount is exactly zero, and that the trace-level sum of zero amounts is zero.
supporting_facts.expected: mintAmount = 0 per event; sum = 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A nonzero amount is credited by an event with no mint site, or the amount field is read without the bounds check that ties it to the site being present.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact-accounting step: from L'.supply + burned = L.supply + 0 the conclusion L'.supply + burned = L.supply follows as exact equality; the zero-mint term must be substituted, not dropped or absorbed into a tolerance.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the supply reconciliation substitutes the proven zero mint total into the accounting identity and preserves exact equality through the whole block-processing step.
supporting_facts.expected: Reconciliation yields exact equality with no residual slack term.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The reconciliation carries an unproven mint term, an epsilon/tolerance, or a saturating/clamping operation that hides a mismatch.

derived_obligations.check: Before any burn (including fee burn) reduces an account balance, bounds-check that the burn amount does not exceed that account's current balance.
derived_obligations.expected: Burn amount <= payer balance; an over-large burn is rejected and the block is invalid.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A burn is applied without comparing the amount against the balance, or an underflow wraps/saturates so the recomputed supply no longer satisfies FACT-1.

derived_obligations.check: Bounds-check the accumulated burned total for the block against the pre-state total supply.
derived_obligations.expected: burned(tau) <= L.supply, so L'.supply + burned = L.supply is satisfiable with non-negative supply.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Accumulated burn exceeds pre-state supply, or the accumulator is allowed to overflow/wrap.

derived_obligations.check: When an account is destroyed, verify its full balance is accounted for as burned or transferred and that it is removed from the live list exactly once, keeping the live list distinct.
derived_obligations.expected: Supply after destruction differs from before by exactly the destroyed balance, which appears in the burned total.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Destruction drops a nonzero balance without recording it, or leaves a duplicate/stale live entry that would double-count or lose balance in the supply sum.

derived_obligations.check: Assert at block-processing boundaries that no credit path can execute when the permitted mint-site list is empty (deny-all semantics for an empty allow-list).
derived_obligations.expected: Zero credits recorded; minted total is exactly 0.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An empty allow-list is interpreted as unrestricted, or a credit path bypasses the site check.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the incrementally maintained supply against a full recomputation (sum of bal over the distinct live list) at the end of block processing.
derived_obligations.expected: Incremental and recomputed supply agree exactly.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any divergence, or the incremental value is trusted without an equality reconciliation — a remotely reachable divergence here splits consensus on state validity.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes two obligations: the accounting identity hacc relating post supply, burned, pre supply and minted (FACT-1, FACT-6), and site confinement hc with an empty permitted mint-site list (FACT-2, FACT-3). From hc, membership in the empty list is impossible (L009), so no event carries a mint site (L008, L005 -> FACT-4); an event with no mint site has mint amount exactly zero (L007) and a trace of zero amounts has zero total (L006, L004 -> FACT-5), giving minted(tau) = 0 (L003, L002 -> FACT-3). Substituting that zero into hacc and applying the exact-accounting lemma (L001 -> FACT-6) yields the exact equality L'.supply + burned(tau) = L.supply. The derived obligations turn this into bounds checks at the implementation sites where a missing check would break the identity remotely: burn versus balance, burn total versus supply, account destruction versus the live-list sum, deny-all mint gating, and an exact incremental-versus-recomputed supply reconciliation.

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify supply cannot rise: every account with a nonzero new balance is in the iterated live set, and no live account's balance increases; recompute the sum over the distinct live list and reject any block whose new total supply exceeds the old.
properties.assertion: (forall a: bal'(a)!=0 -> a in live) && (forall a in live: bal'(a)<=bal(a)) -> supply'<=supply

audit_packet.guarantee: If every account carrying a nonzero post-state balance is a member of the pre-state live account list, and no account in that list has its balance increased, then the post-state total supply (sum of balances over the distinct live list) is less than or equal to the pre-state total supply.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] (hsupp): for every account a, if the post-state balance L'.bal a is nonzero then a is a member of the pre-state live list L.live — no account outside the iterated live set may hold value after the state update.

ROOT obligation [2] (hbal): for every account a that is a member of L.live, the post-state balance L'.bal a is less than or equal to the pre-state balance L.bal a — no live account's balance increases.

Structural precondition from Ledger: both L.live and L'.live are Distinct (no duplicate account entries), and each ledger satisfies bal_live (any account with a nonzero balance is a member of that ledger's own live list).
supply is defined as sumOver bal live — total supply is the sum of the balance function over the live account list, not a separately maintained counter.

supporting_facts.claim: Under both root obligations jointly, post-state supply is bounded above by pre-state supply (a non-strict ordering, not merely 'supply is not corrupted').
supporting_facts.check: For a state transition, enumerate the accounts touched or reachable via account iteration and state.get_account, recompute total supply on both the pre- and post-state ledgers, and compare.
supporting_facts.expected: post_supply <= pre_supply, and both root obligations hold on the same transition.
supporting_facts.flag_if: post_supply > pre_supply, or the ordering is asserted while either obligation is unchecked.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_eq_of_support_iff gives an EXACT EQUALITY, not a bound: for a fixed balance function f, sumOver f l1 = sumOver f l2 whenever l1 and l2 are both Distinct and, for every a with f a nonzero, membership in l1 is equivalent to membership in l2. The root uses this to re-sum L'.bal over L.live instead of L'.live with no change in value.
supporting_facts.check: Compute the post-state total by summing post-state balances over the pre-state live account list, and independently by summing over the post-state's own live list; confirm the two totals are identical.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact equality of the two totals (bit-for-bit), justified by both lists being duplicate-free and by nonzero-balance accounts having equivalent membership in the two lists.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two totals differ, or the implementation only checks that the total is 'not smaller/nonzero' rather than equal, or either list may contain duplicates, or an account with a nonzero post-state balance is in exactly one of the two lists.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_le_mem is a pointwise-to-aggregate ORDERING lemma: if f a <= g a for every a in list l, then sumOver f l <= sumOver g l over that same list. The root composes this with FACT-2's equality via transitivity of <=.
supporting_facts.check: Over the single pre-state live account list, compare post-state balance to pre-state balance account-by-account, then compare the two sums over that same list.
supporting_facts.expected: Every per-account comparison holds (post <= pre), and the aggregate ordering post_sum <= pre_sum follows over the identical list.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any single live account has post-state balance greater than pre-state balance, or the aggregate bound is asserted without the per-account comparison, or the two sums are taken over different account lists.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_congr_mem gives EXACT EQUALITY of sums under pointwise equality on the list: if f a = g a for every a in l, then sumOver f l = sumOver g l. Untouched accounts therefore contribute identically to both totals.
supporting_facts.check: Identify accounts whose balance is unchanged by the state update and confirm their contribution to the pre- and post-state totals is equal.
supporting_facts.expected: Sums restricted to unchanged accounts are exactly equal; only genuinely modified accounts can move the total.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account whose balance was not modified contributes a different amount to the two totals (e.g. it is skipped, double-counted, or re-read from a different state view).

supporting_facts.claim: Distinct.notMemMiddle and Distinct.removeMiddle: in a Distinct list split as l1 ++ (a :: l2), the account a is NOT a member of l1 ++ l2, and l1 ++ l2 remains Distinct. Duplicate-freeness of the live account list is a load-bearing invariant, preserved under removal.
supporting_facts.check: Assert that the live account list used for supply accounting contains no duplicate account entries, and that removing an account preserves that property.
supporting_facts.expected: No account appears twice in the live list, before or after any removal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An account can appear more than once in the iterated live set, or a removal leaves a residual duplicate — either lets one account's balance be counted multiple times in the total.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_middle and sumOver_append are EXACT ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITIONS: sumOver f (l1 ++ l2) = sumOver f l1 + sumOver f l2, and sumOver f (l1 ++ (a :: l2)) = f a + sumOver f (l1 ++ l2). Total supply splits exactly along any partition of the account list, with no ordering dependence.
supporting_facts.check: Partition the live account list arbitrarily (including pulling out a single account) and confirm the total equals the sum of the parts, and that iteration order does not change the total.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact additive equality for every partition; the total is independent of the order in which accounts are iterated.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Partitioning or reordering the account iteration changes the computed total, or removing one account changes the total by anything other than exactly that account's balance.

supporting_facts.claim: sumOver_zero: the sum of the identically-zero balance function over any list is exactly 0; and notMemNil: nothing is a member of the empty list. These fix the base case of the accounting.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that a ledger in which all balances are zero, and an empty live account list, both yield a total supply of exactly 0.
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply is exactly 0; no account is treated as live in an empty account set.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An all-zero or empty ledger reports a nonzero total supply, or lookups on an empty account set return a live account.

supporting_facts.claim: exists_split_of_mem, memRemoveMiddleOfNe, and memInsertMiddle establish exact MEMBERSHIP preservation: any member of the list can be split out; removing an account a preserves membership of every other (distinct) account; inserting an account preserves all existing memberships.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that adding or removing one account from the live account set does not change the liveness status of any other account.
supporting_facts.expected: Membership of all other accounts is preserved exactly across single-account insertion or removal.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Removing or inserting one account silently drops or resurrects a different account in the live set — which would let value vanish from or appear in the total.

derived_obligations.check: On every state update, check that no account outside the iterated live account set ends up with a nonzero balance (root obligation hsupp).
derived_obligations.expected: Every account with a nonzero post-state balance is a member of the pre-state live account list.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero balance exists at an account that the supply accounting never iterates — value created outside the counted set.

derived_obligations.check: On every state update, check per-account that no live account's balance increases (root obligation hbal).
derived_obligations.expected: For every account in the live list, post-state balance <= pre-state balance.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any live account's balance increases, or the per-account comparison is skipped for accounts not in a 'touched' subset while the aggregate bound is still asserted.

derived_obligations.check: Check that the two supply totals are computed over duplicate-free account lists and that accounts with nonzero balances have equivalent membership across the pre- and post-state live sets.
derived_obligations.expected: Both lists Distinct; equal totals for the same balance function (exact equality, per FACT-2).
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate account entries in either list, or a nonzero-balance account present in one live set and absent from the other.

derived_obligations.check: Check that total supply is derived by summing the balance function over the live account list (additively, order-independently) rather than read from an independently maintained counter that could drift.
derived_obligations.expected: Recomputed sum matches the reported total exactly, and is invariant under partition and iteration order.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The reported total diverges from the recomputed sum, or depends on iteration order.

audit_packet.derivation: The root chains two facts. First, sumOver_eq_of_support_iff (L001) re-sums the post-state balance function over the PRE-state live list with EXACT equality, valid because both live lists are Distinct and, for any account with a nonzero post-state balance, membership in the two lists is equivalent (left-to-right from root obligation hsupp, right-to-left from the ledger's own bal_live field). Second, with both sums now over the single list L.live, sumOver_le_mem (L002) lifts the pointwise ordering of root obligation hbal to the aggregate: sumOver L'.bal L.live <= sumOver L.bal L.live. Nat.le_trans composes the equality with the ordering to yield L'.supply <= L.supply. The supporting lemmas L003–L013 are the accounting substrate that makes L001 sound: exact additive decomposition of the sum (L012, L013), the zero base case (L005, L004), duplicate-freeness preserved under removal (L010, L011), and exact membership preservation under split/remove/insert (L007, L008, L009). Both root obligations are load-bearing and independent — hsupp alone permits value to appear at an un-iterated account, and hbal alone permits value to appear at an account outside the live list; only together do they bound total supply.

omitted_facts.reason: memConsElim is a pure case-analysis eliminator for membership in a cons cell (head-equal or tail-member). It carries no security-relevant standalone conclusion — it is proof plumbing used inside L007–L011, whose security content (membership and duplicate-freeness preservation) is already captured in FACT-5 and FACT-8.
