properties.label: opcodes
properties.text: Verify that zeroing a self-destructed account's balance lowers total ether supply by exactly that account's balance at zeroing time, that the account occurs exactly once in the live/accounting set, and that the beneficiary transfer itself is supply-neutral.
properties.assertion: s in live AND distinct(live) AND supply_post + bal_at_zeroing(s) == supply_pre AND supply_delta(move_ether) == 0

audit_packet.guarantee: Setting a live account's balance to 0 decreases the total supply by exactly that account's balance at the moment of zeroing: supply(after zeroing) + bal(s) = supply(before). All ether destruction in SELFDESTRUCT is attributable to the zeroing step alone; the beneficiary transfer moves value without changing the total. Any implementation whose supply/state accounting deviates from this exact equality (duplicate or missing account entry, stale balance read, transfer that is not value-neutral, divergent treatment of the self-beneficiary case) is remotely reachable by a single SELFDESTRUCT-executing transaction and splits clients that account differently.
preconditions: Root obligation hs: the destroyed account s is a member of the live/accounting account set (L.live) at the instant its balance is set to 0; the equality is claimed only under this membership.
The live/accounting set is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct / EthTotal.Distinct): s appears at most once, so its balance is counted exactly once in the total supply.
Total supply is defined as the sum of bal over exactly the live set (Ledger.supply = sumOver bal live) — no ether tracked outside that set and no account in the set excluded from the sum.
Ledger structure invariant bal_live: any account with a nonzero balance is a member of the live set.
bal s in the equality is the balance held by s at the point of zeroing (after any beneficiary transfer has been applied), not a value snapshotted earlier.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact conservation of the zeroing step: for a live account s, supply(setBal s 0) + bal(s) = supply. The supply decrement equals the account balance exactly — not merely 'supply decreases' or 'a burn occurred'.
supporting_facts.check: For a transaction whose execution zeroes a self-destructed account, compute total ether supply before and after the zeroing step and compare the difference against the account's balance read at the zeroing instant.
supporting_facts.expected: supply_pre - supply_post == bal_at_zeroing(s), as an exact equality on unsigned integers, with no rounding, clamping, or saturation.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The supply delta differs from bal_at_zeroing(s) in either direction; the delta is derived from a different quantity (pre-transfer balance, transferred amount, a beneficiary-side value); or the burn is only asserted as 'nonzero'/'balance became 0' without checking the total-supply delta.

supporting_facts.claim: General write accounting (stronger than the v=0 case): supply(setBal a v) + bal(a) = supply + v for any live a and any value v. Every balance write shifts the total by exactly v - bal(a).
supporting_facts.check: Instrument each balance write performed during SELFDESTRUCT handling (debit of the destroyed account, credit of the beneficiary, zeroing) and assert this equality per write against the total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: For every individual write of value v at live account a: supply_after == supply_before - bal_before(a) + v.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any single balance write moves the total supply by an amount other than v - bal_before(a), e.g. a credit applied without a matching accounting update, an overflow/underflow-wrapped write, or a write that updates the account record but not the tracked total.

supporting_facts.claim: The pointwise-update accounting law underlying supply: for a duplicate-free list l with a in l, sumOver(update f a v, l) + f(a) = sumOver(f, l) + v. Both distinctness of l and membership of a are required hypotheses of this law.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the account set used to compute total supply contains no duplicate entry for the destroyed account (or for the beneficiary), and that the set is the same collection the balance write targets.
supporting_facts.expected: Each account key occurs at most once in the accounting collection; the update targets that single occurrence; the resulting total shifts by exactly v - old balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The same account key can appear more than once (aliasing between address representations, a shadowed or re-added entry, a per-touch append), or the balance write and the supply computation range over different collections — either makes the balance be double-counted or dropped from the total.

supporting_facts.claim: Non-membership makes the update supply-invisible: if a is not in l, sumOver(update f a v, l) = sumOver(f, l). Writing to an account outside the accounting set changes the total by exactly zero.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise the case where the destroyed account (or beneficiary) is not present in the live/accounting set at the moment of the write, and observe the total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply is unchanged by that write, and no burn or credit is attributed to it anywhere in the resulting state or receipts.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A write to a non-member account changes total supply, silently creates or destroys ether, or is reported as a burn/credit — or, conversely, membership itself is computed by a rule that could answer differently across implementations for the same account (see OBS-4).

supporting_facts.claim: Ledger structural invariant bal_live: an account with a nonzero balance is necessarily a member of the live set — no ether exists outside the summed collection, so the total supply is the whole supply.
supporting_facts.check: After SELFDESTRUCT handling, confirm that every account holding a nonzero balance (destroyed account, beneficiary) is a member of the accounting set used for the supply sum.
supporting_facts.expected: No account carries a nonzero balance while being absent from the live/accounting set at any observation point.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A nonzero balance is reachable for an account excluded from the accounting set (e.g. an account pruned or marked destroyed while still holding value), which puts ether outside the conserved total and breaks the equality's premise.

derived_obligations.check: Apply FACT-2 to the two writes of a beneficiary transfer (debit of the source by amount t, credit of the beneficiary by t, both live and distinct): sum the two per-write supply deltas.
derived_obligations.expected: Net supply delta of the transfer is exactly 0 (-t then +t); the transfer relocates value and destroys none of it.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The transfer pair yields a nonzero net supply delta — a credit that is skipped, clamped, wrapped, or applied to an account outside the accounting set — which would make the transfer, rather than the zeroing, the source of a burn.

derived_obligations.check: Exercise SELFDESTRUCT with beneficiary equal to the destroyed account itself, then apply FACT-1 to the zeroing step using the balance held at that instant.
derived_obligations.expected: The full balance present at zeroing time is removed from total supply (supply_pre - supply_post == bal_at_zeroing(s)); the self-transfer does not cancel or reduce the burn.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Total supply is unchanged, or drops by less than the balance at zeroing time, because the implementation treats the self-directed transfer as preserving the value — the canonical remotely-triggerable divergence between implementations that burn and implementations that retain.

derived_obligations.check: Compare the destroyed-account balance recorded in receipts / the emitted state diff for the transaction against the measured total-supply delta for the same transaction.
derived_obligations.expected: Reported destroyed amount == supply_pre - supply_post == bal_at_zeroing(s), byte-for-byte equal as integers.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The reported amount is taken from a pre-transfer snapshot, from the transferred amount, or from a beneficiary-side value, so receipts and the actual accounting disagree — divergent receipt/state commitments across implementations.

derived_obligations.check: Determine the exact predicate deciding membership in the live/accounting set for the destroyed account and the beneficiary, and confirm it is a total, deterministic function of the pre-state and the transaction — evaluated identically at the zeroing point.
derived_obligations.expected: Membership is decided identically for the same input by every conforming implementation; FACT-1 (member: exact burn) and FACT-4 (non-member: zero delta) are never both reachable for the same account.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Membership can differ across implementations or across evaluation points within one execution (an account considered live by one and absent by another), which makes one side burn the balance and the other not — a state-root split from a single transaction.

derived_obligations.check: Establish the ordering between the beneficiary transfer and the zeroing, and which balance value feeds the burn accounting.
derived_obligations.expected: The amount removed from the total is the balance read at the zeroing instant, consistent with the ordering actually executed; no stale snapshot is reused across the transfer.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The burn is computed from a balance captured before the transfer while zeroing happens after it (or vice versa), so the supply delta and the account's actual balance diverge whenever the account is credited between the two points.

audit_packet.derivation: The root equality (FACT-1, ROOT/L001) is the v=0 instance of the general write law (FACT-2, L002), which in turn is the ledger-level form of the pointwise-update summation law (FACT-3, L003/L004). That law is discharged only under two hypotheses that the implementation must supply operationally: the account is a member of the summed live set (the root obligation hs) and that set is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct / Distinct). FACT-4 (L006) covers the complementary branch: outside the set, the write is supply-invisible — so membership is the exact switch between 'burn the balance' and 'change nothing', which is why OBS-4 treats a divergent membership decision as the High-severity, single-transaction chain-split vector. FACT-5 (Ledger.bal_live) closes the gap by forbidding value to sit outside the summed set. OBS-1 applies FACT-2 twice to show a debit/credit pair is exactly supply-neutral, which is what makes the theorem's name literally checkable: the entire supply loss is attributable to the zeroing step. OBS-2 instantiates that at beneficiary == destroyed account, OBS-3 ties receipts to the same exact quantity, and OBS-5 pins the balance read to the zeroing instant. Every fact is kept as an exact integer equality; none is weakened to 'balance is zero' or 'supply decreased'.

omitted_facts.reason: EthTotal.notMemNil (membership in the empty list is absurd) is the vacuous base case of the list induction. It carries no implementation-observable content beyond the membership precondition already required by FACT-1/FACT-3 and the non-membership branch stated as FACT-4.

EthTotal.memConsElim is a structural case-analysis eliminator over list cons/nil used to drive the induction in L004. It is a proof-mechanics constant with no security-relevant conclusion of its own; its operational content (an account either is or is not in the accounting set) is covered by FACT-3 and FACT-4.

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: When bridge accounting adds an external claim cl and debits live account d, verify (total_supply + cl) − balance(d) equals the recomputed sum over the remaining live accounts plus cl, with d present exactly once in a distinct live set.
properties.assertion: live == l1++[d]++l2 && distinct(live) => (supply+cl)-bal(d) == sumOver(bal,l1++l2)+cl && supply == bal(d)+sumOver(bal,l1++l2)

audit_packet.guarantee: For a ledger whose supply is defined as the sum of balances over its live account list, removing one live account d's balance from the total while an external claim cl is carried alongside yields exactly the sum over the remaining live accounts plus cl. Equivalently: a total that counts d's balance both inside supply and again in a second (bridge) ledger overcounts by exactly bal(d). The equality is exact — no rounding, no residual, and no truncated-subtraction loss — and it holds at any position of d in the live list.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hsplit: the live account list decomposes as L.live = l₁ ++ d :: l₂, i.e. the debited account d is genuinely a member of the live set and the split witnesses (l₁, l₂) are the actual remaining accounts — every root obligation of the theorem is this one hypothesis and it must be established, not assumed.
Supply is not an independently stored scalar: L.supply is by definition sumOver L.bal L.live — the total must be derivable from the per-account balances over the live list at the moment of the check.

Ledger structural field live_distinct: Distinct L.live — no account appears twice in the live list (otherwise the split (l₁, l₂) does not name the remaining accounts and the cover argument does not apply).
Ledger structural field bal_live: bal a ≠ 0 → a ∈ L.live — no account outside the live list may carry a nonzero balance.
cl is an arbitrary Nat carried unchanged on both sides; it is not constrained by the theorem and must not be used to absorb a discrepancy.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact equality of the adjusted total: (L.supply + cl) − L.bal d = sumOver L.bal (l₁ ++ l₂) + cl, for every live account d and every Nat cl.
supporting_facts.check: With the live account list split as l₁ ++ d :: l₂, compute the left side from the implementation's total-supply value plus the external claim cl minus the account balance read for d, and independently compute the right side by summing state.get_account balances over l₁ ++ l₂ and adding cl.
supporting_facts.expected: The two values are bit-identical for every choice of d in the live set and every cl, including cl = 0 and bal d = 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two sides differ by any amount, or the implementation only checks a weaker property (e.g. that the adjusted total is nonzero, non-negative, or merely ≤ the original supply) instead of the exact equality.

supporting_facts.claim: Cover split at any live account (conservation): L.supply = L.bal d + sumOver L.bal (l₁ ++ l₂). The total decomposes exactly into the singled-out account's balance plus the sum over all remaining accounts — this is the strong conservation fact the root consequence rests on, and it holds for an arbitrary live d, not just the head or tail.
supporting_facts.check: For each live account d, verify the stored/derived total supply equals bal(d) plus the recomputed sum over the live list with d removed.
supporting_facts.expected: Exact equality for every live account d, independent of d's position in the live list.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The decomposition holds only for some positions (e.g. only when d is first/last), or supply exceeds / falls short of bal(d) + sum(rest), which means the total is not a faithful cover of the per-account balances.

supporting_facts.claim: Middle extraction is exact: sumOver f (l₁ ++ a :: l₂) = f a + sumOver f (l₁ ++ l₂). Deleting an element from anywhere in the list decreases the sum by exactly that element's value.
supporting_facts.check: Remove a live account from an arbitrary interior position of the live list and recompute the balance sum.
supporting_facts.expected: The recomputed sum is exactly the original sum minus that account's balance — the same result as removing it from the front or the back.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The delta from removing an interior account differs from that account's balance, or removal at an interior position changes the summation result compared with an equivalent front/back removal (position-dependent accounting).

supporting_facts.claim: Additivity over concatenation: sumOver f (l₁ ++ l₂) = sumOver f l₁ + sumOver f l₂. The total over a partitioned account set equals the sum of the partial totals.
supporting_facts.check: Partition the live account list at an arbitrary point, total each part separately, and compare against the total over the whole list.
supporting_facts.expected: Equality for every partition point, including empty parts.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Partial totals do not recombine to the whole-list total — e.g. a per-segment accumulator saturates, wraps, or drops a segment boundary.

supporting_facts.claim: Cancellation is exact on both sides: (a + b) − a = b (L002) and (n + m) − m = n (L004). Debiting a quantity that was genuinely added recovers the remainder exactly, with no truncation residue.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that the debit of bal(d) is applied to a total that provably already includes bal(d) (per FACT-2), so the subtraction is a cancellation rather than an unguarded subtraction on a natural-number/unsigned total.
supporting_facts.expected: The subtraction returns the exact complement; the operand order used by the implementation matches the direction proved (either (a+b)−a or (n+m)−m), both of which are covered.
supporting_facts.flag_if: bal(d) is subtracted from a total that does not demonstrably contain it (truncating unsigned subtraction would silently clamp to zero, or a signed total would go negative), or the debit is applied to the wrong accumulator (e.g. to cl rather than to supply).

derived_obligations.check: Establish the ROOT precondition itself before relying on the equality: prove d is a member of the live account list and materialize the split (l₁, l₂) from the actual live list, rather than assuming membership from an external ledger's records.
derived_obligations.expected: L.live = l₁ ++ d :: l₂ is witnessed by the live list as read at check time.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The debit of bal(d) is performed for an account that is not in the live list (the hypothesis fails and the equality carries no guarantee), or membership is taken from a second/bridge-side record instead of the live set.

derived_obligations.check: Verify the Ledger distinctness field live_distinct: the live account list contains no duplicate account.
derived_obligations.expected: Distinct L.live holds.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An account appears more than once in the live list — the split then fails to name the true remainder, and a single debit of bal(d) leaves a duplicate copy still counted in the total (an overcount that survives the adjustment).

derived_obligations.check: Verify the Ledger field bal_live: every account with a nonzero balance is a member of the live list.
derived_obligations.expected: bal a ≠ 0 → a ∈ L.live, so no value sits outside the summed cover.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero balance is reachable for an account absent from the live list — supply then under-reports and the conservation fact FACT-2 does not constrain the missing value.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the total supply used on the left side is the value derived from the current per-account balances over the current live list (the L.supply definition), not a separately maintained scalar that could have drifted from the account state.
derived_obligations.expected: supply == sumOver bal live at the moment the adjusted total is computed.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A cached or independently updated total is used, so an improper per-account state update leaves the scalar and the summed cover disagreeing while the equality check still appears to pass.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the external claim cl is carried through unmodified on both sides of the accounting — it is added before the debit and reappears unchanged in the result.
derived_obligations.expected: The same cl value appears on both sides; the debit of bal(d) touches only the supply component.
derived_obligations.flag_if: cl is scaled, clamped, netted against bal(d), or otherwise altered by the adjustment, which would let a bridge-side quantity absorb an accounting discrepancy instead of surfacing it.

audit_packet.derivation: The root equality is obtained by rewriting L.supply with the cover split at the live account d (FACT-2 / L001), which itself follows from exact middle extraction on the summation (FACT-3 / L003) and additivity of sumOver over concatenation (FACT-4 / L005). After the rewrite the left side reads (bal d + sumOver bal (l₁ ++ l₂)) + cl − bal d; reassociation puts bal d in cancellable position, and exact cancellation (FACT-5 / L002 with L004) removes it, leaving sumOver bal (l₁ ++ l₂) + cl (FACT-1 / ROOT). Every step is an equality, so the audit must compare exact values: the security content is that a total which counts a live account's balance both inside supply and again in a second ledger overcounts by exactly bal(d), and the correction must be exactly that amount, at any position of d, over a distinct live set whose cover captures all nonzero balances. Because the total supply of the state trie is consensus-relevant, a wrong adjustment reachable via a single message would put nodes on divergent totals — the network-scale failure this check is aimed at.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (d : A) (l₁ l₂ : List A),
  Eq L.live (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons d l₂)) →
    Eq L.supply (instHAdd.hAdd (L.bal d) (EthTotal.sumOver L.bal (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)))
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq L.supply (instHAdd.hAdd (L.bal d) (EthTotal.sumOver L.bal (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)))

x_proof_closure.statement: ∀ (a b : Nat), Eq (instHSub.hSub (instHAdd.hAdd a b) a) b

∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) (l₁ : List A) (a : A) (l₂ : List A),
  Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)))
    (instHAdd.hAdd (f a) (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)))
x_proof_closure.conclusion:
Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ (List.cons a l₂)))
  (instHAdd.hAdd (f a) (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂)))

x_proof_closure.statement: ∀ (n m : Nat), Eq (instHSub.hSub (instHAdd.hAdd n m) m) n

∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) (l₁ l₂ : List A),
  Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂))
    (instHAdd.hAdd (EthTotal.sumOver f l₁) (EthTotal.sumOver f l₂))
x_proof_closure.conclusion:
Eq (EthTotal.sumOver f (instHAppendOfAppend.hAppend l₁ l₂))
  (instHAdd.hAdd (EthTotal.sumOver f l₁) (EthTotal.sumOver f l₂))

properties.label: block-processing
properties.text: For every trace accepted between ledger states L and L', require the exact equality L'.supply + burned(τ) = L.supply + minted(τ) with unclamped Nat arithmetic, and reject any two accepted traces whose burned/minted cross-sums disagree.
properties.assertion: accept(L,L',τ) ⇒ L'.supply+burned(τ)==L.supply+minted(τ); accept(L,L',τ)∧accept(L,L',τ') ⇒ burned(τ)+minted(τ')==burned(τ')+minted(τ)

audit_packet.guarantee: Any two event traces that both reconcile the same pre-state ledger L with the same post-state ledger L' agree on net issuance: burned(τ) + minted(τ') = burned(τ') + minted(τ). Equivalently, the (minted − burned) net implied by a state transition is uniquely determined by the endpoint supplies, so no second trace can be accepted for the same endpoints while accounting for a different amount of issuance or burn.
preconditions: ROOT obligation [1] (h): the first trace τ satisfies the exact supply-conservation equation L'.supply + burned(τ) = L.supply + minted(τ), where Ledger.supply = sumOver bal live.

ROOT obligation [2] (h'): the second trace τ' satisfies the same exact equation against the same endpoints, L'.supply + burned(τ') = L.supply + minted(τ'). Both obligations are required; establishing only one does not yield the guarantee.
burned and minted are total Nat-valued folds over a Trace (List of Ev.mint/Ev.burn events); all arithmetic is exact Nat addition with no truncation, saturation, or modular wraparound.
L and L' are well-formed Ledgers: live is Distinct, and bal a ≠ 0 implies a ∈ live, so supply is a well-defined finite total over the live set.

supporting_facts.claim: Given both conservation obligations for the same endpoint pair (L, L'), the cross-sums are exactly equal: burned(τ) + minted(τ') = burned(τ') + minted(τ). This is an exact equality over Nat, not a bound or a nonzero/boolean consequence — the net issuance for a transition between two fixed supplies is unique.
supporting_facts.check: Take any two distinct traces the implementation would accept for the same pre-state L and post-state L' (e.g. two candidate issuance/receipt logs for one state transition). Compute burned(τ)+minted(τ') and burned(τ')+minted(τ) from the recorded mint/burn events and compare for exact equality.
supporting_facts.expected: The two cross-sums are bit-for-bit equal for every such pair; the implementation either rejects one of the traces or produces identical net issuance for both.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Two traces are both accepted for the same (L, L') yet the cross-sums differ, or the code compares net issuance with an inequality/tolerance/range test instead of exact equality — a remotely reachable divergence in accepted issuance between honest nodes on the same state transition.

supporting_facts.claim: The uniqueness result is stated at the ledger level with the endpoints given by Ledger.supply, i.e. the sum of bal over the Distinct live list — not by an independently tracked or cached total. Both obligations are hypotheses of this lemma; the conclusion is the exact cross-sum equality.
supporting_facts.check: Verify that the supply values used on both sides of the conservation equation are derived from the same accounting quantity — the aggregate of per-account balances over the live account set — for both L and L', and that the same supply values feed both trace checks.
supporting_facts.expected: Both obligations are evaluated against one consistent notion of supply per ledger state, computed from the live/bal accounting, with L used only as pre-state and L' only as post-state in both equations.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The two obligations are checked against different supply notions (e.g. one against an aggregate total, the other against a per-account or partial subtotal), or the post-state supply is taken from a value written before the trace's events were applied.

supporting_facts.claim: The uniqueness holds purely from the shape z + b = y + m and z + b' = y + m' for fixed Nat endpoints z and y: only the two endpoint values matter, so any two traces sharing endpoints are forced to agree on net. No property of the event list beyond its burned/minted totals is required.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm the acceptance predicate binds both traces to the same two endpoint scalars (pre-state supply and post-state supply) and that no per-trace side channel (a separately supplied expected-total, a per-trace adjustment term, or a trace-specific correction) can shift one side of either equation.
supporting_facts.expected: Both equations are anchored to one shared (pre-supply, post-supply) pair; the only trace-dependent inputs are burned(τ) and minted(τ).
supporting_facts.flag_if: Either equation admits a trace-specific offset, override, or exemption path, which breaks the shared-endpoint premise and permits two traces with different nets to both pass.

supporting_facts.claim: The derivation rests on left cancellation over Nat: n + m = n + k implies m = k. Cancellation is valid only for exact, unbounded, non-wrapping, non-saturating addition; under a clamped or modular accumulator the cancellation step — and therefore the uniqueness guarantee — fails.
supporting_facts.check: Inspect the accumulation of burned and minted totals and the supply aggregation for any operation that can silently lose information at a boundary: saturation at a maximum, modular wraparound, truncation to a narrower width, or clamping of a would-be-negative intermediate. Exercise the accounting with totals near the representable maximum of the accumulator type.
supporting_facts.expected: Every addition in the burned, minted, and supply computations is exact for all reachable values, or an out-of-range result causes explicit rejection of the trace rather than a clamped/wrapped value that is then compared.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any accumulator saturates, wraps, or truncates instead of failing, or a subtraction of burn from supply is clamped at zero — the missing bounds check that lets two traces with genuinely different nets compare equal, remotely reachable via a single crafted message and capable of splitting the network.

derived_obligations.check: For each trace the implementation accepts for a state transition, independently recompute L.supply, L'.supply, burned(τ) and minted(τ) and evaluate L'.supply + burned(τ) = L.supply + minted(τ) as an exact equality. Confirm the acceptance path cannot be reached with the equality unchecked, partially checked, or checked only for one of two candidate traces.
derived_obligations.expected: The exact equality is a hard gate on acceptance, enforced for every trace on every transition; failure rejects the trace.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The equality is skipped, downgraded to an inequality or approximate/range comparison, applied to only one candidate, or bypassed on any path (e.g. a fast path that trusts a supplied total).

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the accounting total is computed over a duplicate-free live account set and that every account with a nonzero balance is present in that set, matching the Ledger well-formedness fields (live is Distinct; bal a ≠ 0 implies a ∈ live).
derived_obligations.expected: Supply is a well-defined total: no account is double-counted, and no nonzero balance is excluded from the aggregate.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The live set can contain duplicates, or an account can hold a nonzero balance while absent from the aggregated set — either makes the supply endpoints unfaithful and voids the premise of both obligations.

derived_obligations.check: Drive the burned and minted accumulators, and the supply aggregate, with values at and beyond the accumulator's representable range (large single mint/burn amounts, long traces of large events). Observe whether the result is exact, rejected, or silently clamped/wrapped.
derived_obligations.expected: Exact result or explicit rejection. No silent clamping, saturation, wraparound, or truncation anywhere in the burned/minted/supply arithmetic.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any boundary produces a silently adjusted total that is then used in the conservation comparison.

derived_obligations.check: Construct two distinct candidate traces (differing mint/burn event sequences) that both pass the implementation's conservation check for the same (L, L') pair, and compare their net issuance. Repeat with amounts chosen to stress the accumulator boundaries identified in OBS-3.
derived_obligations.expected: No such pair exists with differing net; if both pass, burned(τ)+minted(τ') = burned(τ')+minted(τ) holds exactly.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A pair is found — this is a concrete break of the guarantee and a remotely reachable consensus divergence on issuance accounting between nodes processing the same block.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem takes both conservation obligations (h for τ, h' for τ') over shared endpoints L.supply and L'.supply and concludes the exact cross-sum equality burned(τ)+minted(τ') = burned(τ')+minted(τ). It delegates to L001 (the same statement phrased over Ledger supplies), which generalizes to L002 (the statement over bare Nat endpoints z, y — showing only the endpoint scalars and the two totals matter), which in turn rests on L003, left cancellation over Nat. The audit therefore enforces: both obligations as gates (OBS-1), well-formed supply endpoints so the obligations mean what they say (OBS-2), exact non-wrapping arithmetic so cancellation is sound (OBS-3), and a direct differential test that no two accepted traces disagree on net (OBS-4). The missing_bounds_check defect class lands squarely on OBS-3: a clamped or wrapping accumulator makes two materially different issuance histories compare equal, which is exactly the cancellation failure L003 forbids.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} {L L' : EthTotal.Ledger A} {b m b' m' : Nat},
  Eq (instHAdd.hAdd L'.supply b) (instHAdd.hAdd L.supply m) →
    Eq (instHAdd.hAdd L'.supply b') (instHAdd.hAdd L.supply m') → Eq (instHAdd.hAdd b m') (instHAdd.hAdd b' m)

∀ {y z b m b' m' : Nat},
  Eq (instHAdd.hAdd z b) (instHAdd.hAdd y m) →
    Eq (instHAdd.hAdd z b') (instHAdd.hAdd y m') → Eq (instHAdd.hAdd b m') (instHAdd.hAdd b' m)
∀ {n m k : Nat}, Eq (instHAdd.hAdd n m) (instHAdd.hAdd n k) → Eq m k

properties.label: state-trie
properties.text: Verify that writing zero to a storage slot yields exactly the same trie/storage-root state as if the slot were never written: the zero write must delete the entry, not store a zero-valued node.
properties.assertion: f(k)=0 -> supportOf(f, k::l) == supportOf(f, l)

audit_packet.guarantee: For any key whose written value is the default (zero), including that key in the state produces a support set exactly equal to the support set without it — a zero write is deletion, and the resulting storage/state root is byte-identical to the never-written case.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hz: the value assigned to key k is exactly the default, f k = 0 (SSTORE of value 0, or state.set_storage with zero).
The support/trie contents are modeled as a keyed map f : A -> Nat over a key list l, matching the state-trie key enumeration under audit.
Key k is an arbitrary key drawn from the same key domain A as the entries in l (no special-casing of particular slots).

supporting_facts.claim: Root theorem writing_the_default_is_deletion: if f k = 0 then supportOf f (k :: l) = supportOf f l — exact equality of the resulting support, not merely 'similar' or 'nonzero-equivalent'.
supporting_facts.check: For an arbitrary key set l and key k, set the value at k to 0 via the storage-write path (SSTORE / state.set_storage / trie_set) and compare the full resulting support/trie entry set against the same state built from l alone.
supporting_facts.expected: The two supports are exactly equal as structures (same entries, same order), so the derived storage root and state root are identical.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Writing 0 leaves a residual entry for k (an explicit zero node, a tombstone, or an empty-but-present branch), or produces a support/root differing in any way from the l-only state.

supporting_facts.claim: Supporting lemma supportOf_cons_zero: for any x with f x = 0, supportOf f (x :: l) = supportOf f l — the deletion property is a general, per-key head-elimination equality with no side conditions beyond zero-ness, and it holds for every key, not just fresh ones.
supporting_facts.check: Exercise the zero write on keys in each distinguishable position: a key already present with a nonzero value, a key absent from l, a key already zero, and a key repeated in l. Each time compare the resulting support and storage root against the state constructed from l alone.
supporting_facts.expected: Every case yields exactly supportOf f l — identical entry set and identical root hash — independent of whether k was previously present, absent, or duplicated.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Zero-write deletion holds only for previously-absent keys (or only for previously-present keys), or a repeated/duplicated key leaves one copy behind, or the root differs between cases.

supporting_facts.claim: The equality is on supportOf itself — the structure other consumers read — so the deletion property propagates to everything derived from the support, including the storage root and the account's state-trie entry.
supporting_facts.check: After each zero write, recompute every consumer of the support that the code surface exposes (storage root, trie enumeration/iteration order, entry count) and compare against the l-only baseline.
supporting_facts.expected: All derived values agree exactly with the l-only baseline: same root, same enumeration, same count.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The support compares equal but a derived value (root hash, iteration order, or entry count) differs — indicating the deletion is applied at only one layer of the state update.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the zero-value guard is an exact equality test against the default value (value = 0) and not an approximate, truncated, or type-coerced comparison.
derived_obligations.expected: Only an exactly-zero value triggers the delete path; every nonzero value is stored.
derived_obligations.flag_if: A nonzero value is treated as zero (deleting live state) or a zero value fails the test (storing a zero node) due to width truncation, signedness, or encoding differences between the written value and the default.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm the delete-on-zero behavior is unconditional across all entry points that write storage (SSTORE, state.set_storage, trie_set), with no path that bypasses it.
derived_obligations.expected: Every write path applies the same zero-is-deletion rule, so no entry point can introduce a divergent state root.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any one write path stores an explicit zero while another deletes — the two would produce different roots for the same transaction, a remotely triggerable consensus split.

derived_obligations.check: Confirm that deleting the last entry of a subtree collapses it fully, so the resulting structure equals the l-only structure rather than retaining an empty container.
derived_obligations.expected: Structural equality with the l-only state holds down to the root, with no empty branch or node retained.
derived_obligations.flag_if: An emptied subtree, branch, or account storage container persists after the zero write, yielding a root that differs from the never-written state.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem's single obligation hz (f k = 0) is carried as the packet precondition. Under it, L001 (supportOf_cons_zero) gives the exact equality supportOf f (k :: l) = supportOf f l for an arbitrary head key; the root is precisely that lemma instantiated at k. FACT-1 and FACT-2 preserve the equality in full strength (structural identity, not a weaker nonzero/boolean consequence) and FACT-2 additionally records the lemma's generality over the head key's prior status. FACT-3 propagates the equality to the derived storage/state root, which is where an improper_state_update becomes a remotely reachable, chain-splitting divergence. OBS-1..OBS-3 discharge the implementation-side conditions the Lean statement assumes: an exact zero test, uniform application across every write path, and full structural collapse.

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} (f : A → Nat) {x : A},
  Eq (f x) 0 → ∀ (l : List A), Eq (EthTotal.supportOf f (List.cons x l)) (EthTotal.supportOf f l)
x_proof_closure.conclusion: Eq (EthTotal.supportOf f (List.cons x l)) (EthTotal.supportOf f l)

properties.label: transactions
properties.text: Verify CALL/move_ether rejects value > sender balance before any state write: a saturating debit removes only min(v,bal) while crediting v, inflating total supply by exactly v-bal(s).
properties.assertion: s,d live && live distinct && (bal(s)>=v || abort) && supply_after==supply_before && supply_after!=supply_before+(v-bal(s))

audit_packet.guarantee: For a transfer of value v from sender s to recipient d, both live in the balance state, if the debit is computed with truncated/saturating subtraction and the credit with the full v, then whenever bal(s) < v the total supply strictly increases by exactly v - bal(s). The implementation must make this state unreachable: the balance check must reject v > bal(s) before any balance write, so that every applied transfer conserves total supply exactly.
preconditions: ROOT obligation hs: sender s is a member of the live account list (s exists in the state being summed for total supply)
ROOT obligation hd: recipient d is a member of the live account list (d exists in the state being summed for total supply)
ROOT obligation hgt: the overdraft condition bal(s) < v holds — this is the guarded state, i.e. the transfer value exceeds the sender's balance
The live account list is duplicate-free (Ledger.live_distinct), and any account with nonzero balance is live (Ledger.bal_live)
Balances are non-negative machine naturals, so subtraction below zero saturates at 0 rather than wrapping or erroring

supporting_facts.claim: Root theorem: with s and d live and bal(s) < v, the debit-then-credit sequence yields a state whose total supply is strictly greater than the pre-transfer total supply — an unbacked mint of ether.
supporting_facts.check: Construct a state with two live accounts, set bal(s) = k, and attempt a CALL/move_ether transfer of value v > k from s to d. Sum all balances before and after.
supporting_facts.expected: The transfer is rejected by the balance check and no balance is written; the summed total supply is unchanged.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The transfer is applied (s clamped to 0, d credited v) and the summed total supply after is strictly greater than before — treat any strict increase as a Critical supply-inflation finding.

supporting_facts.claim: Exact quantification, not merely an inequality: the post-transfer supply equals supply + (v - bal(s)). The amount minted is exactly the shortfall, so an attacker chooses the mint size by choosing v.
supporting_facts.check: For several (bal(s), v) pairs with v > bal(s), record post_supply - pre_supply if the transfer is (incorrectly) applied.
supporting_facts.expected: No transfer with v > bal(s) is ever applied, so the difference is never observable; when v <= bal(s) the difference is exactly 0.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any applied transfer yields post_supply - pre_supply == v - bal(s) > 0, or any nonzero difference at all — the attacker-controlled v makes the inflation unbounded and remotely reachable in one transaction.

supporting_facts.claim: General conservation law for the debit-then-credit pair: post_supply + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply + v. Supply is conserved exactly when the debited amount min(v, bal(s)) equals the credited amount v.
supporting_facts.check: Instrument the transfer path to record the amount actually removed from s and the amount actually added to d, then compare them for each executed transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: debited == credited == v for every executed transfer, so post_supply + v = pre_supply + v and supply is conserved.
supporting_facts.flag_if: debited < credited for any executed transfer (i.e. debited == min(v, bal(s)) < v), which is precisely the conservation-breaking case.

supporting_facts.claim: The credit leg is exact and unconditional: crediting d with bal(d) + v raises total supply by exactly v, with no clamping or cap on the recipient side.
supporting_facts.check: Apply only the recipient-side credit of a transfer and measure the change in total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: Total supply rises by exactly v on the credit leg — meaning the debit leg must remove exactly v to restore balance.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The credit leg is applied without a matching, equally sized debit leg having already succeeded, or the two legs are not atomic under any failure or revert path.

supporting_facts.claim: The debit leg is deficient under saturation: supply_after_debit + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply, i.e. the debit removes only min(v, bal(s)), which is strictly less than v exactly when bal(s) < v.
supporting_facts.check: Apply only the sender-side debit with v > bal(s) and measure the removal from total supply.
supporting_facts.expected: The debit is refused before mutation because v > bal(s); no partial debit state exists.
supporting_facts.flag_if: The debit clamps bal(s) to 0 and removes only bal(s), leaving the shortfall v - bal(s) uncovered — especially if the credit leg then proceeds.

supporting_facts.claim: Single-account update accounting: for a live account a in a duplicate-free list, supply(setBal a v) + bal(a) = supply + v. Total supply tracks per-account writes exactly only when the list has no duplicate entries and the written account is a member.
supporting_facts.check: Verify the account/balance container admits no duplicate keys for the same account and that every balance write targets an account already present in (or correctly inserted into) that container.
supporting_facts.expected: Each write changes the total by exactly (new_value - old_value); no duplicate key can be updated on one path and summed on another.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Duplicate or aliased account entries exist, or a balance write targets an account not accounted for in the supply sum — either breaks the per-write accounting that the whole conservation argument rests on.

supporting_facts.claim: Saturating-subtraction identity: min(v, b) + (b - v) = b for naturals, with b - v = 0 whenever b <= v and min(v,b) = b in that same case. Truncated subtraction silently loses exactly v - b of value.
supporting_facts.check: Locate every truncated/saturating subtraction on a balance in the transfer path and confirm each is guarded by a prior check that the minuend is at least the subtrahend.
supporting_facts.expected: Every balance subtraction is preceded by an explicit check bal >= v that aborts the whole transfer on failure; the subtraction can therefore never truncate.
supporting_facts.flag_if: Any balance subtraction can execute with subtrahend > minuend and silently produce 0 (or a clamped value) instead of aborting the transfer.

supporting_facts.claim: Strict positivity of the shortfall: bal(s) < v implies 0 < v - bal(s). The inflation is never zero in the overdraft case — every overdraft transfer mints a strictly positive amount.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm there is no boundary or rounding case in which an overdraft (v > bal(s)) is treated as harmless or as a no-op.
supporting_facts.expected: Overdraft is always an error path; there is no v > bal(s) that is silently tolerated.
supporting_facts.flag_if: An overdraft is tolerated on the assumption that the discrepancy is zero or negligible — for v = bal(s) + 1 it is already a strictly positive unbacked mint.

supporting_facts.claim: Updating an account that is not a member of the summed list leaves the sum unchanged — so a write to a non-tracked account creates a balance that the supply accounting never sees.
supporting_facts.check: Confirm that sender and recipient are resolved into the same account set used to compute total balances before either leg is applied, including newly created recipients.
supporting_facts.expected: Both s and d are members of the accounted set at the time of the write, so every credit is visible to supply accounting.
supporting_facts.flag_if: A credit can land on an account outside the accounted set (e.g. an untracked or lazily created recipient), making the credited value invisible to any conservation check.

supporting_facts.claim: Order bounds on the actual debit: min(v, bal(s)) <= v and min(v, bal(s)) <= bal(s), and min is symmetric — so the debit is capped by the sender's available balance and can never reach v when bal(s) < v.
supporting_facts.check: Assert the recorded debit amount satisfies debit <= bal(s) and debit == v for every executed transfer.
supporting_facts.expected: Both hold simultaneously, which forces v <= bal(s) — exactly the balance-check precondition.
supporting_facts.flag_if: debit <= bal(s) holds while debit == v fails, i.e. the cap bound binds and the transfer still proceeds.

derived_obligations.check: In the CALL / value-transfer path, confirm the sender-balance check (bal(s) >= v) executes before any balance mutation and aborts the entire transfer, not just the debit leg, when it fails.
derived_obligations.expected: Insufficient balance aborts the transfer atomically with no balance written to either s or d.
derived_obligations.flag_if: The check is missing, occurs after a mutation, is advisory only, or aborts the debit while allowing the credit to persist.

derived_obligations.check: Replace or guard every saturating/truncating balance subtraction in move_ether so that an underflow is an explicit error rather than a clamp to zero.
derived_obligations.expected: Underflow is unrepresentable on the transfer path: either the type errors, or an explicit precondition makes truncation unreachable.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any subtraction on a balance can clamp at zero (or wrap) without raising an error.

derived_obligations.check: Add a conservation invariant over the whole account set: sum of all balances before a transfer equals the sum after, checked in tests and, if feasible, as a debug-mode assertion over the transfer path.
derived_obligations.expected: Total supply is bit-exact identical before and after every value transfer, for all values including v = 0, v = bal(s), and v = bal(s) + 1.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any transfer changes the summed total in either direction; an increase is the Critical fund-integrity break, a decrease indicates silent value burn.

derived_obligations.check: Fuzz and property-test the transfer with adversarially chosen v — in particular v = bal(s) + 1, v = 2^256 - 1, and v far exceeding total supply — from a remotely submitted transaction.
derived_obligations.expected: Every such transfer is rejected; the total supply and both account balances are unchanged.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Any such input is accepted and increases total supply — a single remote transaction minting attacker-chosen value is a network-scale fund-integrity break (Critical).

derived_obligations.check: Verify the account container preserves the distinctness and membership assumptions: no duplicate entries per account, and both sender and recipient are present in the accounted set before any write.
derived_obligations.expected: Distinctness and membership hold at every transfer, so per-account writes map one-to-one onto changes in the total.
derived_obligations.flag_if: Duplicate/aliased account entries are possible, or a balance write targets an account outside the accounted set.

audit_packet.derivation: The root theorem (FACT-1) gives strict inflation of total supply under the three obligations: s live, d live, and bal(s) < v. FACT-2 sharpens this from an inequality to the exact identity post_supply = pre_supply + (v - bal(s)), so the minted amount is attacker-controlled through v. That identity comes from FACT-3's conservation law post_supply + min(v, bal(s)) = pre_supply + v, which decomposes into the exact credit leg (FACT-4: +v, unconditional) and the deficient debit leg (FACT-5: only min(v, bal(s)) removed). Both legs reduce to the single-account accounting rule (FACT-6), which is valid only because the live list is duplicate-free and the written account is a member — hence the membership obligations are genuine preconditions, not bookkeeping. FACT-7 explains the mechanism: truncated subtraction satisfies min(v,b) + (b - v) = b, so it silently absorbs exactly the shortfall instead of failing, and FACT-10's bounds show the debit is capped at bal(s) and therefore cannot reach v in the overdraft case. FACT-8 confirms the shortfall is strictly positive, so no overdraft is benign. FACT-9 closes the flank where a credit lands outside the accounted set and escapes conservation checks entirely. The implementation guard is therefore the contrapositive: enforce bal(s) >= v atomically before any write (OBS-1), make truncation unreachable (OBS-2), and continuously assert exact supply conservation (OBS-3) under adversarial remote inputs (OBS-4) and a well-formed account set (OBS-5).

omitted_facts.reason: add_right_cancel is a pure natural-number cancellation step used to rearrange the supply equations; it carries no independent security content beyond the equalities already exposed as FACT-2/FACT-3/FACT-5.
add_left_cancel is the mirror arithmetic cancellation lemma backing L005; it is proof plumbing with no implementation-checkable consequence.

notMemNil states that nothing is a member of the empty list — a base case of the list induction behind sumOver_update, with no distinct check beyond the membership obligations already listed as preconditions.

memConsElim is the cons-case eliminator driving the same list induction; it is structural recursion machinery, and its security-relevant outcome is fully captured by FACT-6 (per-account update accounting) and FACT-9 (non-member updates are invisible to the sum).

x_proof_closure.statement:
∀ {A : Type u} [inst : DecidableEq A] (L : EthTotal.Ledger A) (s d : A) (v : Nat)
  (hs : List.instMembership.mem L.live s) (hd : List.instMembership.mem L.live d),
  Eq
    ((L.setBal s (instHSub.hSub (L.bal s) v) hs).setBal d
        (instHAdd.hAdd ((L.setBal s (instHSub.hSub (L.bal s) v) hs).bal d) v) hd).supply
    (instHAdd.hAdd L.supply (instHSub.hSub v (L.bal s)))
x_proof_closure.conclusion:
Eq
  ((L.setBal s (instHSub.hSub (L.bal s) v) hs).setBal d
      (instHAdd.hAdd ((L.setBal s (instHSub.hSub (L.bal s) v) hs).bal d) v) hd).supply
  (instHAdd.hAdd L.supply (instHSub.hSub v (L.bal s)))
